title: GSK Marks Second Lung Cancer Drug Approval This Year
description:
On Tuesday, the Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval to GSK Plc.’s (NYSE:GSK) Nelkarmi (neladalkib) for locally advanced or metastatic anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
The milestone marks the second lung cancer approval this year for the European drug giant.
Regulators cleared the kinase inhibitor for patients who previously received either one prior ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) consisting of alectinib or two or more prior ALK TKIs alongside platinum-based chemotherapy in the unresectable locally advanced or metastatic setting.
Clinical Trial Results Show Durable Responses
The FDA based its decision on the Phase 1/2 ALKOVE-1 trial, which demonstrated clinically meaningful and durable responses in pretreated patients.
Investigators evaluated efficacy in the study across two patient groups to assess confirmed overall response rate (CRR) and duration of response (DOR).
Among 67 patients who previously received one ALK TKI consisting of alectinib in the metastatic setting, neladalkib achieved a 49% ORR.
Within that responding group, 76% maintained a DOR of at least six months, and 52% maintained a DOR of at least 12 months.
Among 155 patients who previously received two or more ALK TKIs and platinum-based chemotherapy, treatment produced a 32% ORR.
Of those responders, 69% achieved a DOR of at least six months, while 51% reached a DOR of at least 12 months.
GSK added the drug via a Nuvalent deal worth $10.6 billion.
The acquisition gives GSK three lung cancer assets in a single transaction, including Nuvalent’s lead drug candidates, zidesamtinib and neladalkib, which are being developed for certain forms of non-small cell lung cancer.
GSK Price Action: Gsk shares were up 0.12% at $49.30 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

fullContent:
Oracle released its November edition of Critical Security Patch Update. The update received patches for 655 security vulnerabilities. Some of the vulnerabilities addressed in this update impact more than one product. These patches address vulnerabilities in various product families, including third-party components in Oracle products.

Out of the 655 security updates published, a total of 62 (9.5%) vulnerabilities are rated critical, 249 are rated as important (38%), and 274 are rated as medium.

In this Oracle Critical Security Patch Update, Oracle Hyperion received the highest number of patches, 267, constituting about 41% of the total patches released.

71 of the 655 (about 11%) security patches provided by the November Critical Security Patch Update are for non-Oracle CVEs, such as open-source components included in and exploitable within Oracle product distributions.

This batch of security patches received 20 updates for Oracle Database products. The following is the product-wise distribution: 

  • 7 new security updates for Oracle Database Server with a maximum reported CVSS Base Score of 9.9.
    • None of these updates applies to client-only deployments of the Oracle Database.
  • 2 new security updates for Oracle APEX with a maximum reported CVSS Base Score of 9.8.
  • 3 new security updates for Oracle Autonomous Health Framework with a maximum reported CVSS Base Score of 9.1.
  • 8 new security updates for Oracle REST Data Services with a maximum reported CVSS Base Score of 9.8.

The complete list of Oracle product families and the no of patches issued are listed below:

Qualys QID Coverage

Qualys has released the following QIDs mentioned in the table:

Note: The table will be updated with additional QIDs once released.

Notable Oracle Vulnerabilities Patched

Oracle Hyperion

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle Hyperion received 267 security patches. Out of these, 107 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

A total of 12 vulnerabilities have critical severity ratings.

Oracle Supply Chain

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle Supply Chain received 74 security patches. Out of these, 36 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

CVE-2026-114980, CVE-2026-127324, CVE-2026-127325, CVE-2026-127326, CVE-2026-127327, and CVE-2026-101356 have critical severity ratings.

Oracle E-Business Suite

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle E-Business Suite received 71 security patches. Out of these, 19 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

CVE-2026-114880, CVE-2026-114924, CVE-2026-114925, CVE-2026-114863, CVE-2026-101691, and CVE-2026-114881 have critical severity ratings.

Oracle Fusion Middleware

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle Fusion Middleware received 71 security patches. Out of these, 19 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

CVE-2026-114880, CVE-2026-114924, CVE-2026-114925, CVE-2026-114863, CVE-2026-101691, and CVE-2026-114881 have critical severity ratings.

Oracle Communications

This Critical Security Patch Update for Oracle Communications received 31 security patches. Out of these, 21 vulnerabilities can be exploited over a network without user credentials.

CVE-2026-111497, CVE-2026-1229, CVE-2026-41889, and CVE-2026-114820 have critical severity ratings.

title: Nvidia’s New AI Customers Are Growing 3X Faster Than Big Tech
description:
Nvidia Corp‘s (NASDAQ:NVDA) next growth engine may be emerging outside the world’s biggest technology companies. While Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Alphabet Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) Google remain among the most important buyers of its AI infrastructure, a less-discussed customer category is expanding nearly three times faster — and is already contributing more incremental revenue than hyperscalers.
Neoclouds: A New AI Spending Powerhouse
Nvidia’s AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise business generated $47.5 billion in revenue in the third quarter of fiscal 2027, up 195% year over year. By comparison, revenue from hyperscale customers, including major cloud providers, rose 71% to $60.1 billion, according to interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress‘ commentary.




The difference becomes even more interesting when measured in dollars. The AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise category added $31.4 billion in revenue over the past year, compared with a $25 billion increase from hyperscalers. In other words, the smaller customer category generated more than half of the combined year-over-year revenue increase across these two groups.
That is a potentially important shift for investors accustomed to viewing Nvidia’s growth primarily through the spending plans of a handful of Big Tech companies.
Beyond Amazon, Microsoft and Google
The emerging buyers include specialized AI cloud providers, enterprises building their own AI infrastructure and industrial customers deploying accelerated computing. Neocloud companies such as CoreWeave, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) are particularly important because they rent out computing capacity to AI developers and businesses that cannot afford or do not want to build their own data centers.
The ecosystem also includes Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ:NBIS), Nscale, Crusoe, Lambda and IREN Limited (NASDAQ:IREN), with Nvidia helping CoreWeave, Nebius and Nscale build out their infrastructure businesses as demand for specialized AI computing expands.
Nvidia’s latest results also point to a broader change in how AI infrastructure is being deployed. Frontier AI developers are increasingly building their own data centers, while specialized cloud providers are expanding capacity to serve customers beyond traditional hyperscalers.
Kress said both customer platforms benefited from the introduction of Nvidia’s Rubin infrastructure, its fastest architecture ramp ever, standalone Vera CPUs and continued growth in Blackwell Ultra.
The distinction matters because Nvidia’s demand pool may be broadening beyond the capital expenditure budgets of the largest cloud companies. More enterprises and specialized infrastructure providers are becoming part of the AI spending cycle, potentially creating additional sources of demand as adoption spreads.




However, the numbers do not establish that hyperscalers are losing importance. At $60.1 billion, they still represent the larger revenue category, and Nvidia does not separately disclose how much of the 195% growth came from neoclouds, industrial customers or enterprise deployments.
Investment Takeaway
Investors should watch whether AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise revenue can sustain its faster growth as Nvidia’s Rubin platform scales. 
The bigger question is whether this expanding customer base represents genuinely diversified end demand or whether much of it ultimately depends on financing and infrastructure commitments from the same handful of technology giants. For Nvidia, the distinction could determine how durable its next phase of growth really is.

title: Target's Comeback Picks Up Speed Ahead of Crucial Holiday Season
description:
Target Corp. (NYSE:TGT) stock edged higher in Wednesday’s premarket session after the retailer reported better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results and raised its full-year forecast.
Strong customer traffic, digital sales growth and tariff refunds supported the quarterly performance.
Sales Growth and Customer Traffic
Target’s turnaround is gaining momentum ahead of the crucial holiday shopping season. Rising customer traffic, accelerating November sales and stronger digital demand suggest the retailer’s renewed focus on style, affordability and customer experience is paying off.
Net sales rose 7.1% year over year to $27.07 billion, exceeding the $26.55 billion analyst estimate.
Comparable sales increased 5.6%, driven by a 5% increase in customer traffic. Store comparable sales rose 4.6%, while digital comparable sales climbed 9.8%.
CEO Michael Fiddelke highlighted progress in Target’s strategy centered on style, design, affordability and customer experience. The retailer recorded sales growth across most of its core merchandising categories.
Fiddelke also said November sales through the reporting date aligned with expectations, with sales trends accelerating from October.
Holiday Strategy and AI Investments
For the holiday season, Target plans to introduce more than 8,000 new gifts. More than half will be exclusive to the retailer, with thousands priced at $5 or less.
During the earnings call, management highlighted efforts to revitalize the women’s apparel business. Target plans to reduce the number of styles by 20% and lower prices on hundreds of items.
Management expects early signs of progress by spring 2027.
Meanwhile, Target is introducing artificial intelligence-powered shopping experiences and expanding its use of AI to improve inventory decisions.
Earnings and Margins Expand
GAAP diluted earnings rose to $2.65 per share from $1.51 a year earlier. Adjusted earnings increased to $2.65 per share from $1.78.
Tariff refunds contributed $228 million to net earnings and 50 cents per share to both GAAP and adjusted earnings.
Excluding the tariff refund benefit, adjusted earnings of $2.15 per share exceeded the $2.07 analyst estimate.
Operating income rose to $1.67 billion from $948 million, while operating margin expanded to 6.2% from 3.8%.
Gross margin increased to 30.5% from 28.2%, including a 110-basis-point benefit from tariff refunds.
Excluding refunds, gross margin expanded 120 basis points. Lower markdowns and tariff rates, higher non-merchandise sales and improved supply chain productivity supported the expansion.
However, higher freight and fuel costs, continued investments in affordability and an unfavorable sales mix partially offset those gains.
Quarterly results included $301 million in pretax tariff refund benefits within gross margin and operating income.
Merchandise and Advertising Sales
Merchandise sales rose 6.9% to $26.45 billion, while non-merchandise sales jumped 19.3%.
Food and beverage sales increased 7% to $6.41 billion. Household essentials sales rose 5% to $4.75 billion, while apparel and accessories generated $3.69 billion.
Beauty sales climbed 9% to $3.53 billion. Hardlines, or Fun 101, sales surged 27% to $4.05 billion.
Growth in Roundel advertising revenue, Target Circle programs and the Target+ marketplace fueled the increase in non-merchandise sales.
Cash Flow and Shareholder Returns
Capital expenditures rose to $1.4 billion, reflecting investments in store remodels and new locations.
Operating cash flow totaled $5.73 billion during the first nine months of the year.
Target ended the quarter with $4.46 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $14.19 billion in long-term debt.
During the quarter, the retailer paid $527 million in dividends and repurchased $251 million of its shares.
Target Raises 2026 Forecast
Target raised its fiscal 2026 net sales growth forecast to about 6%. It also expects an operating margin of about 6.2%, including a 110-basis-point benefit from tariff refunds recognized through the third quarter.
The updated sales forecast implies revenue of $111.07 billion, up from $110.02 billion and above the $110.37 billion analyst estimate.
Target raised its GAAP and adjusted EPS forecasts to $10.65-$11.40 from $9.90-$10.90.
The updated ranges exceed the GAAP and adjusted earnings estimates of $10.52 and $10.55 per share, respectively.
The earnings forecast includes about $2.14 per share in tariff refund benefits but excludes any potential future refunds.
Looking ahead, Target expects capital expenditures of $5 billion to $6 billion in 2027.
TGT Price Action: Target shares were up 0.68% at $160.61 during premarket trading on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

GAAP diluted earnings rose to $2.65 per share from $1.51 a year earlier. Adjusted earnings increased to $2.65 per share from $1.78.

Tariff refunds contributed $228 million to net earnings and 50 cents per share to both GAAP and adjusted earnings.

Excluding the tariff refund benefit, adjusted earnings of $2.15 per share exceeded the $2.07 analyst estimate.

Operating income rose to $1.67 billion from $948 million, while operating margin expanded to 6.2% from 3.8%.

Gross margin increased to 30.5% from 28.2%, including a 110-basis-point benefit from tariff refunds.

Excluding refunds, gross margin expanded 120 basis points. Lower markdowns and tariff rates, higher non-merchandise sales and improved supply chain productivity supported the expansion.

However, higher freight and fuel costs, continued investments in affordability and an unfavorable sales mix partially offset those gains.

Quarterly results included $301 million in pretax tariff refund benefits within gross margin and operating income.

Merchandise and Advertising Sales

Merchandise sales rose 6.9% to $26.45 billion, while non-merchandise sales jumped 19.3%.

Food and beverage sales increased 7% to $6.41 billion. Household essentials sales rose 5% to $4.75 billion, while apparel and accessories generated $3.69 billion.

Beauty sales climbed 9% to $3.53 billion. Hardlines, or Fun 101, sales surged 27% to $4.05 billion.

Growth in Roundel advertising revenue, Target Circle programs and the Target+ marketplace fueled the increase in non-merchandise sales.

Cash Flow and Shareholder Returns

Capital expenditures rose to $1.4 billion, reflecting investments in store remodels and new locations.

Operating cash flow totaled $5.73 billion during the first nine months of the year.

Target ended the quarter with $4.46 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $14.19 billion in long-term debt.

During the quarter, the retailer paid $527 million in dividends and repurchased $251 million of its shares.

Target Raises 2026 Forecast

Target raised its fiscal 2026 net sales growth forecast to about 6%. It also expects an operating margin of about 6.2%, including a 110-basis-point benefit from tariff refunds recognized through the third quarter.

The updated sales forecast implies revenue of $111.07 billion, up from $110.02 billion and above the $110.37 billion analyst estimate.

Target raised its GAAP and adjusted EPS forecasts to $10.65-$11.40 from $9.90-$10.90.

The updated ranges exceed the GAAP and adjusted earnings estimates of $10.52 and $10.55 per share, respectively.

The earnings forecast includes about $2.14 per share in tariff refund benefits but excludes any potential future refunds.

Looking ahead, Target expects capital expenditures of $5 billion to $6 billion in 2027.

title: NEAR Price Squeezed Into a 29-Cent Range by Three Levels
description:
Summary Price sits just above the 0.618 retracement. The 100-day SMA near $3.52 caps rebounds. Candles are testing the channel’s […]
The post NEAR Price Squeezed Into a 29-Cent Range by Three Levels appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Summary

  • Price sits just above the 0.618 retracement.
  • The 100-day SMA near $3.52 caps rebounds.
  • Candles are testing the channel’s upper edge.
  • Moving-average order still favors the longer trend.

On the daily NEAR/USDT chart from Binance, the token trades at $3.34, down 1.59% on the day after opening at $3.40 and moving between $3.31 and $3.43.

Where the reference points come from

Every level that matters here traces back to one move. NEAR bottomed near $1.52 in August and ran to a high close to $5.99 by mid-October, nearly quadrupling in about two months.

Stretch a Fibonacci grid over that rally and the map fills in. The 0.236 sits near $4.93, the 0.382 around $4.28 and the 0.5 near $3.76. Lower down, the 0.618 lands close to $3.23, with the 0.786 around $2.48.

The top took weeks to form. Through late September and most of October, NEAR chopped between the 0.382 area and levels above the 0.236, tagging its high near $6 along the way. It was a grind, not a spike and a crash.

A channel of lower highs

Then the selling got organized and from late October, price slid inside a descending parallel channel, with each bounce peaking below the last one and each low undercutting the one before it.

Volume never screamed panic. The decline inside the channel came without a capitulation-sized spike, and today’s 9.37 million NEAR is moderate. This was steady selling, not a forced flush.

Mid-November brought the real stress test. NEAR slipped below the 0.618, then climbed back over it within days. Traders watch that line closely. It’s the deepest standard retracement that still reads as a pullback inside a bigger advance, and past it only the 0.786 stands between price and losing most of the rally.

Three levels inside 29 cents

The bounce off the 0.618 ran straight into the channel’s upper boundary. The last two sessions sit on that line or just above it. Today’s small red candle shows sellers defending it.

Just overhead waits the 100-day SMA at $3.52, the first ceiling for any rebound. So the squeeze is tight. The 0.618 sits underneath, the 100 SMA above, and the channel line cuts right through the current candles, all within a $0.29 range.

One session poking over a trendline isn’t a breakout. A run of daily closes clearly outside the channel would be. Closes above the 100 SMA would make that case far harder to argue with.

READ MORE:

Why a 5% Stablecoin Return Can Still Cost Holders Money

Bent trend, not a broken one

The 50-day SMA carries the bearish half of the story. At about $4.42, it has rolled over and now slopes down, well above price. That’s the plainest evidence that the medium-term trend has turned against buyers.

Further down, the picture changes. The 200-day SMA at $2.72 is still rising. And the averages haven’t crossed: the 50 still sits above the 100, which still sits above the 200. A bearish crossover would mean a shorter average dropping under a longer one, and none has happened yet. The structure built during the rally is dented, not dismantled.

Momentum backs that read. The 14-day RSI prints 39.65, under the 50 midline, so sellers keep the edge for now. Yet it has hooked higher and sits above its own moving average at 37.02. Through the whole decline, it stayed above the oversold line at 30.

Beyond each edge of the band

Either side can give way first. Here’s what the chart has waiting.

Break above $3.52

A daily close over the 100 SMA, with price outside the channel, brings the 0.5 near $3.76 into view. Past that, the 0.382 around $4.28 and the falling 50 SMA at $4.42 stack into a thicker resistance zone.

Slip below $3.23

If sellers reject the channel top and price loses the 0.618 near $3.23, the rising 200 SMA at $2.72 is the first level in the way. The 0.786 around $2.48 sits beneath it.

What decides the label: neither path is a forecast. As long as NEAR holds the 0.618 and the 200 SMA keeps climbing, the drop from $5.99 still reads as a deep correction of the $1.52 rally. A sustained move below both would turn it into a broken trend.

The first signal won’t be dramatic. It’s a run of daily closes clearly above the channel line, not one candle. If those closes arrive with the RSI back over 50, buyers would hold the momentum edge as well as the structure. Until then, the channel still sets the terms.

title: XRP Trading Is Seeing a Major Shift: Here’s Why It Matters for Price
description: Binance's XRP futures volume is now 5.6 times spot volume, leaving derivatives traders with greater influence over market activity.
fullContent:
XRP’s derivatives market is gaining ground against spot trading, with data from the largest crypto exchange by volume, Binance, pointing to weaker liquidity and a growing reliance on leveraged positions.

And with the Ripple token struggling to hold $1, analysts are warning that this combination could leave it more exposed to sudden price swings.

XRP Futures Volume Now 5.6X Times Spot Trading

In a November 18 update on CryptoQuant, analyst Amr Taha shared that the XRP Spot-to-Futures Volume Ratio on Binance had dropped by more than 34%, going from about 27.2% earlier in the month to just under 18%.

This makes the XRP futures trading volume around 5.6x bigger than that of spot trading at current levels, showing that derivatives activity is growing in dominance.

The shift is happening with XRP changing hands around the psychologically important $1 threshold, and according to Taha, it could make the token more susceptible to leveraged positioning and forced liquidations around price levels that are closely watched.

“A recovery in the ratio would indicate stronger relative participation from the spot market, while further declines could reinforce the dominance of derivatives trading,” concluded the analyst.

And that’s not all that has gone down. As market watchers at Arab Chain pointed out earlier today, the 30-day liquidity index for XRP on Binance has also taken a hit, falling to roughly 0.041, the lowest it has been in three months.

That means there has been quite the deterioration in the XRP market’s liquidity condition when compared to other periods in the past, with historical data showing much higher readings for the index, especially between the tail end of 2025 and the early months of 2026, when it made several gains.

Their conclusion was almost similar to Taha’s:

“The persistence of the index at these low levels could make XRP more sensitive to sudden market movements, as reduced liquidity may increase the price impact of large buy or sell orders.”

As such, were trading activity to increase suddenly, it could potentially cause much larger fluctuations in XRP’s price compared to what would happen when liquidity conditions are stronger.

Leverage Was Already Draining Out

Earlier in the week, Taha had drawn attention to the fact that XRP had recorded its biggest daily liquidation imbalance since October 2025, with approximately $44 million more in longs liquidated on Binance, Bybit, and OKX than short positions.

At the same time, the derivatives market has also been shedding speculative exposure. XRP futures open interest, also on Binance, fell to around $325 million after it had reached $1.5 billion earlier this year. Its estimated leverage dropped to its lowest reading since November 2024 at 0.13, with Arab Chain saying the two declines were evidence that speculative activity was cooling, something that could help reduce the volatility often caused by forced liquidations.

Indeed, at around $1.00 at the time of writing, XRP showed a rise in its price of over 4% in the last 24 hours, even though other timeframes were stuck in the red, with losses of more than 7% across the last week and about 25% in the past 30 days.

title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike
Bitcoin price traded near $64,000 Wednesday morning as Fed Governor Christopher Waller floated a half-point December rate hike, offsetting a lift from Nvidia earnings.
This post Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike

Bitcoin price traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, according to Bitcoin Magazine data, as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point rate hike is probably needed in December. The bitcoin price had slipped below $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon. It climbed back to about $65,000 that evening after Nvidia beat earnings estimates, then faded through the U.S. morning.

The bitcoin price is down about 21% from a month ago, when it traded above $81,000.

Waller floats a half-point hike

Waller told CNBC in a live interview that the Fed probably needs a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He said the central bank should reverse its three quarter-point cuts from last year and may need to do more. “You might need to, like, shock people,” Waller said.

“I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” he said. Waller said the Fed should deliver the larger move if it is not prepared to signal a faster pace of hikes in the coming months. He also said about 70% of items in the core services basket are running above 3%, which has nothing to do with oil.

The 2-year Treasury yield rose more than 4 basis points to 4.83% after his comments. The dollar hit a 19-month high, and gold dropped 2.5% to its lowest level in more than a year. Futures markets fully price a quarter-point hike in December and another increase in January, CNBC reported. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem suggested Tuesday that as many as four hikes could come by spring.

Minutes from the Fed’s Oct. 27-28 meeting are due Wednesday afternoon. Policymakers held rates at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote, with Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike.

Nvidia lifts tech stocks

Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion after the bell Tuesday, more than double a year earlier and above the $109.1 billion analysts expected. Data center revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion, and the company guided to about $130 billion for the current quarter. Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will remain “disciplined in how we commit capital.” The board said it would not reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO last week.

Nvidia shares were up about 2.6% in premarket trading. Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.8% and S&P 500 futures rose 0.3%, but the bitcoin price did not follow tech higher. IREN (IREN), the bitcoin miner turned AI cloud provider, rose between 8% and 10% in extended trading along with CoreWeave and Nebius, and was recently up about 3% premarket. Strategy (MSTR) closed down 6.3% at $96.50 on Tuesday and was little changed before the open, while Coinbase (COIN) closed down 4% and was up about 0.5% premarket.

What comes next for the bitcoin price

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed a net $239.9 million on Tuesday, a day after snapping a seven-session outflow streak. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for $209.5 million of that. Anthropic is expected to price its IPO Wednesday evening, with shares set to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT. The company marketed 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, and sources told CNBC on Tuesday that the deal will likely price above that range.

President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. AI chip exports are a key issue.

A break of the weekend low near $62,000 would put last week’s flush back in view for the bitcoin price.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $63,800.

This post Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

Staking sits in the same account as the rest of BetFury. The pools are replenished from the platform’s gaming revenue, so activity across BetFury feeds back into staking rewards, while a monthly buyback and burn steadily reduces the BFG supply. title: South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says
South Korea's Financial Services Commission plans to release guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms invest in bitcoin and other crypto, News1 reported.
This post South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission plans to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday. The guidelines will be released alongside the government’s draft of the Digital Asset Basic Act, the country’s planned framework for the crypto industry, according to the report. The FSC plans to convene its Virtual Asset Committee to coincide with the release.

The FSC itself has not publicly announced a date for either release. If it lands next week, the move would come one year and nine months after the regulator laid out its roadmap for corporate crypto access in February 2025.

A roadmap that stalled

That plan opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell. Since June 2025, Korean nonprofits have been able to cash out crypto they receive as donations, and World Vision made the first such trade, selling donated ether on Upbit.

Exchanges have also been allowed to sell their own holdings to cover operating costs. Coinone and DigitalX, formerly Korbit, have done so several times after filing disclosures. The second stage, which lets listed companies and firms registered as professional investors trade crypto for investment, was slated for the second half of 2025. It never arrived.

The holdup is market plumbing. Corporate orders are large, and even Korea’s biggest exchanges have limited room to absorb them without moving prices. “If companies come into the market and trade 5 billion won each, even an exchange like Upbit would struggle to take that volume,” an unnamed industry official told News1. Large trades would normally run through over-the-counter desks, and Korea does not yet have rules governing how those desks operate.

What the Basic Act adds

The Digital Asset Basic Act is meant to close that gap. It would split crypto service providers into separate business types and set entry and conduct rules for OTC desks, brokers and other operators, the report said. The government’s draft is expected to go to the National Assembly next week.

Lawmakers want it passed quickly. The Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee aims to process the bill by January, timed to the implementation of the U.S. GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law. Rep. Min Byung-duk of the Democratic Party said at a recent forum that he intends to “wrap it up by Jan. 9.”

The 5% question

The report did not describe what the corporate guidelines will contain. In January, *Seoul Economic Daily* reported that a draft would cap a company’s annual crypto investment at 5% of equity capital and limit purchases to the top 20 coins by market value. The FSC responded the next day that key items, including investment limits and eligible assets, had not been finalized.

Analysts said at the time that corporate flows would likely concentrate in bitcoin, the largest crypto asset by market value, even with a wider menu of coins. Jeonbuk Bank said in October it would offer bitcoin-backed loans. Korea has also pushed back its 22% crypto tax to 2029, the fourth delay, while the Bank of Korea has lobbied to write stablecoins into foreign exchange law.

Retail investors in Korea have been able to trade crypto for years. Domestic demand has at times pushed local bitcoin prices above global levels, a gap known as the kimchi premium. title: South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says
South Korea's Financial Services Commission plans to release guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms invest in bitcoin and other crypto, News1 reported.
This post South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission plans to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday. The guidelines will be released alongside the government’s draft of the Digital Asset Basic Act, the country’s planned framework for the crypto industry, according to the report. The FSC plans to convene its Virtual Asset Committee to coincide with the release.

The FSC itself has not publicly announced a date for either release. If it lands next week, the move would come one year and nine months after the regulator laid out its roadmap for corporate crypto access in February 2025.

A roadmap that stalled

That plan opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell. Since June 2025, Korean nonprofits have been able to cash out crypto they receive as donations, and World Vision made the first such trade, selling donated ether on Upbit.

Exchanges have also been allowed to sell their own holdings to cover operating costs. Coinone and DigitalX, formerly Korbit, have done so several times after filing disclosures. The second stage, which lets listed companies and firms registered as professional investors trade crypto for investment, was slated for the second half of 2025. It never arrived.

The holdup is market plumbing. Corporate orders are large, and even Korea’s biggest exchanges have limited room to absorb them without moving prices. “If companies come into the market and trade 5 billion won each, even an exchange like Upbit would struggle to take that volume,” an unnamed industry official told News1. Large trades would normally run through over-the-counter desks, and Korea does not yet have rules governing how those desks operate.

What the Basic Act adds

The Digital Asset Basic Act is meant to close that gap. It would split crypto service providers into separate business types and set entry and conduct rules for OTC desks, brokers and other operators, the report said. The government’s draft is expected to go to the National Assembly next week.

Lawmakers want it passed quickly. The Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee aims to process the bill by January, timed to the implementation of the U.S. GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law. Rep. Min Byung-duk of the Democratic Party said at a recent forum that he intends to “wrap it up by Jan. 9.”

The 5% question

The report did not describe what the corporate guidelines will contain. In January, *Seoul Economic Daily* reported that a draft would cap a company’s annual crypto investment at 5% of equity capital and limit purchases to the top 20 coins by market value. The FSC responded the next day that key items, including investment limits and eligible assets, had not been finalized.

Analysts said at the time that corporate flows would likely concentrate in bitcoin, the largest crypto asset by market value, even with a wider menu of coins. Jeonbuk Bank said in October it would offer bitcoin-backed loans. Korea has also pushed back its 22% crypto tax to 2029, the fourth delay, while the Bank of Korea has lobbied to write stablecoins into foreign exchange law.

Retail investors in Korea have been able to trade crypto for years. Domestic demand has at times pushed local bitcoin prices above global levels, a gap known as the kimchi premium. Corporate money has been the missing piece. Under the roadmap, about 3,500 companies would become eligible once the guidelines take effect.

The guidelines’ release would not on its own open trading. The FSC still has to say when listed companies can place their first orders.

title: Why Sandisk Stock Is Climbing Wednesday
description:
Sandisk Corp. (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock rose about 2% in Wednesday’s premarket session after artificial intelligence chipmaker NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) reported stronger-than-expected quarterly results and issued an upbeat growth outlook.
A broader recovery in technology stocks also supported the gains. Nasdaq futures rose 0.82%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.37%.
NVIDIA Earnings Lift Memory And Storage Stocks
NVIDIA’s strong third-quarter results and optimistic outlook for computing demand helped ease concerns about spending on AI infrastructure.
The results also lifted sentiment toward memory and storage suppliers, including Sandisk, as expanding AI workloads increase demand for high-capacity, high-performance storage solutions.
AI data centers require substantial storage capacity to manage training datasets, model checkpoints and growing volumes of data generated during inference.
Sandisk’s gains also reflect improving investor sentiment after a steep pullback from its September peak.
Technical Analysis
Despite gaining 225.50% over the past 12 months, Sandisk remains in a corrective phase.
The stock trades 23.7% below its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) and 42% below its 50-day SMA. It also trades 44.7% below its 100-day SMA and 36.6% below its 200-day SMA.
Trading below all four major moving averages suggests persistent selling pressure.
Meanwhile, the moving average convergence divergence (MACD) indicator remains below its signal line, with a negative histogram. Both indicators point to weak near-term momentum.
The 20-day SMA remains below the 50-day SMA, reinforcing the bearish short-term trend. However, the 50-day SMA remains above the 200-day SMA, suggesting some longer-term technical strength.
The stock reached a swing high in September before hitting a swing low in November. The MACD turned bearish in February following a bullish crossover in December 2025.
Key Resistance: $965
Key Support: $804
A sustained recovery above key moving averages could signal improving momentum. However, a break below $804 could expose the stock to further downside.
Analyst Outlook
Sandisk carries a consensus Buy rating with an average price forecast of $2,176.43. Recent analyst actions include:
Fox Advisors: Downgraded the stock to Equal-Weight on Nov. 2.
Rosenblatt: Maintained a Buy rating and a $2,400 price forecast on Oct. 30.
Wells Fargo: Maintained an Equal-Weight rating and lowered its price forecast to $1,300 on Oct. 30.
Top ETF Exposure
Sandisk accounts for a significant portion of several exchange-traded funds, including:
Invesco S&P 500 Pure Growth ETF (NYSE:RPG): 6.94%
Invesco S&P Spin-Off ETF (NYSE:CSD): 6.08%
First Trust US Equity Opportunities ETF (NYSE:FPX): 5.85%
Significant fund inflows or outflows could influence buying and selling activity in Sandisk shares.

fullContent:
WASHINGTON—Claiming that such monitoring efforts had been a waste of government resources, Federal Bureau of Investigation officials announced Friday that the agency would discontinue its longstanding practice of tracking serial killers.

Though the FBI’s Violent Criminal Apprehension Program has historically enjoyed bipartisan approval for its role in the capture of murderers like the Golden State Killer and Samuel Little, the bureau has come under scrutiny in recent months amid the Trump administration’s ongoing efforts to downsize federal agencies. Director Kash Patel has repeatedly argued that Americans should stop expecting the government to hunt down every serial killer who binds and gags victims before tossing their bodies in the trunk of a car. 

“Today we are ending the senseless and inefficient tracking of America’s homicidal maniacs,” said Patel, who stated that the decision to no longer collect information related to serial killers was driven primarily by the high costs associated with processing DNA evidence, identifying human remains, and prosecuting federal murder charges. “The fact is, if a crazed necrophile is chasing you through the woods with a pair of hedge shears, it’s not the taxpayers’ job to bail you out. Those kinds of handouts might have flown with the socialist Biden FBI, but not anymore.”

“Our common-sense position is that these depraved, gratification-seeking murderers aren’t the government’s problem,” Patel added.

Despite Patel’s dismissive attitude toward murders and bloody, violent crime scenes, some experts have voiced concerns that ending federal investigations of active killers such as the San Diego Strangler and the Alabama Ripper could allow rates of serial homicides to rebound to levels not seen since the 1970s. According to reports, the FBI has ceased to archive dozens of human fingers mailed to them by uncaptured serial killers and has sold off its forensics laboratory at Quantico to a Trump-linked condominium developer. Critics argue this move could leave the bureau without the institutional capacity to hunt down any violent psychopaths obsessed with constructing a suit out of human skin who may arise in the future.

Despite these criticisms, a number of Americans expressed concerns about government overreach infringing on the civil liberties of anyone who kills for their own personal pleasure and gratification. 

“I don’t know why these woke liberals are so afraid of serial killers,” said Idaho resident Mike Howe, who noted that there were millions of acres of forest where the decapitated remains of victims were buried and claimed that it was “none of our business.” “There’s things we can do without spending millions of dollars to track down every single mentally unstable auto mechanic targeting brunette women who resemble his domineering mother.”

While the decision to curtail federal investigation of serial killers so far appears to have garnered widespread disapproval from law enforcement agencies and public safety groups, the policy shift nevertheless has its staunch defenders.

 “I get why some people are opposed to this change, but I’m glad the Trump administration is letting me collect more slaves to serve me in the afterlife,” said the Ouroboros Killer, an as-of-yet unidentified murderer who has repeatedly voiced his support for the FBI’s actions in numerous cryptographic ciphers mailed to news-
papers across the country. “It feels so good when I slide that knife in, but even better is when the president takes a knife to wasteful government spending.”

 “Government efficiency is the ultimate thrill,” the Ouroboros continued. “I am not afraid of death because I know that in paradise all the tax dollars Trump has saved by slashing government bloat will be waiting for me. Ouroboros = 31, inefficient federal bureaucracy = 0.”

title: The Chopping Block: Crypto's Brutal Week With FalconX's Josh Lim, CZ vs. Star, the Anthropic IPO, and Should Jensen Huang Come Back?
description:
Welcome to The Chopping Block, where crypto insiders Haseeb Qureshi, Tom Schmidt, Tarun Chitra, and Robert Leshner chop it up about the latest in crypto. This week they are joined by Joshua Lim, Global Co-Head of Markets at FalconX.

Six red weeks in a row, BTC down to 65K, the fear and greed index at 10, and a $20 billion contraction in stablecoins. Josh walks through what his desk saw: a hidden buildup in leverage, end-of-year hedges in IBIT puts, and a weekend sell-off concentrated on Coinbase. The hosts react to the Situational Awareness 13F coming out down 92%, and Haseeb calls it the Multicoin of AI. Josh says the numbers don't support Star's claim that Binance is dumping on the market, and Haseeb explains how far back the CZ and Star feud goes. Then the Anthropic IPO: Tarun asks whether a flop would actually be better for crypto, Haseeb bets newly liquid Anthropic employees buy crypto, and Robert says Anthropic's unlock schedules are bringing the weirdness back. Tom asks what crypto's next catalyst is, and Haseeb and Tarun argue over whether past bear markets ever had a narrative. They close on Jensen Huang's exit from NVIDIA: Robert says he crossed a major line, Tarun makes the case that he willed NVIDIA into existence, and Haseeb says tech is misreading the moment.

title: Robinhood Eyes $130 as Mizuho Brushes Off Kalshi’s Stock-Trading Threat
description:
Robinhood (NASDAQ:HOOD) is bouncing back toward $70 Wednesday after Mizuho stuck with its $130 price target, arguing Kalshi’s push into stock trading won’t dent Robinhood’s business.
Management Downplays the Kalshi Threat
Mizuho analysts led by Dan Dolev met with CEO Vlad Tenev and CFO Shiv Verma Tuesday and came away unconvinced that Kalshi’s potential move into equities poses a real strategic risk. 
Management framed its edge as "product depth over breadth," pointing to more than a decade of product refinement and strong customer retention as harder to replicate than a new trading feature. 
Mizuho kept its Outperform rating and $130 target, implying roughly 86% upside from Tuesday’s $69.19 close, a price that leaves the stock down about 40% for the year.
Prediction Markets Still Growing Fast
Robinhood is also pushing back on Kalshi directly, working to improve pricing on prediction markets and expand beyond its dominant sports category, a shift that should benefit Gold subscribers and make the broker more competitive in complex contracts as it routes less volume through Kalshi. 
Non-sports contracts already made up 30% of Robinhood’s third-quarter prediction market volume, double the 15% share from the prior quarter, while total event contracts traded hit 5.9 billion in October, up 5% from September and 136% from a year earlier.
Mizuho also pointed to banking, cards and retirement accounts as the next lever for pulling more customer cash onto the platform, where Robinhood can earn interest on the balances, noting the company already holds more than $35 billion in retirement assets and counts over 1.3 million Gold Card holders.
HOOD Stock: Key Levels to Watch
Shares are up about 1.5% premarket, trying to reclaim the $70 support they lost in the prior session, though the stock remains roughly 44% below September’s peak near $126 with the broader downtrend still intact. 
Holding above $70 to $72 during regular trading could support a push toward $75, then $80, with tougher resistance near $85, where the 20-day EMA and a bearish Supertrend signal converge. 
If the bounce fades instead, $67.25 marks the first downside level, followed by the $63 to $65 support zone. 
The stock remains below all four major daily EMAs, so the rebound hasn’t yet flipped the broader trend.

Another day, another security scare. This time, Etherscan is warning users after detecting unauthorized access attempts against its customer support system that might have been hacked. But the timing could hardly be worse for an industry already dealing with a growing list of cyberattacks.

The warning comes just days after hackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely, injecting malicious code into websites operated by 178 organizations. The affected names included HSBC, BBC, Ledger, IKEA, Salesforce, Zoom, and CNN.

Meanwhile, crypto platforms have faced separate attacks involving compromised API keys, protocol vulnerabilities, and stolen customer information. Traditional banking has not escaped either, with a French bank recently losing approximately €100 million to hackers.

So what kind of security era are we entering? The problem is no longer confined to crypto exchanges or experimental DeFi protocols. Banks, technology companies, payment providers and blockchain businesses are increasingly exposed to the same interconnected digital infrastructure.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Etherscan, Optimizely and 178 Websites Hacked: Nobody Seems Safe

Etherscan disclosed just a few minutes ago that attackers had attempted to gain unauthorized access to its Freshworks customer support and ticketing system. The company is investigating and has introduced precautionary measures. It has not confirmed that customer records were successfully accessed, but warned users about suspicious support communications, unexpected links, and requests for sensitive information.

The concern is particularly relevant because support impersonation remains an effective way to steal crypto and your money. An attacker posing as an Etherscan representative could exploit a user’s existing support request to make a phishing message appear legitimate.

But Etherscan is hardly the only name facing security questions this week. Just two days ago, hackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely’s Web Experimentation signup process. They injected malicious JavaScript into customer projects, allowing the code to run on websites using the affected software.

Security researchers identified 178 organizations whose websites carried the malicious code. The list included HSBC, BBC, Ledger, Zoom, Salesforce, CNN and Equifax. The injected script attempted to replace crypto wallet addresses with attacker-controlled alternatives. It also targeted payment-card information, cookies and screenshots, while attempting to deliver exploit code against older iPhones.

Optimizely confirmed the vulnerability and said it had removed the injected code and fixed the flaw. Its November 17 incident report said the unauthorized party exploited the signup process rather than stealing customer administrator passwords.

The financial damage remains unclear. It is reported that investigators could not establish how many visitors were affected or whether the attempted thefts succeeded.

The uncomfortable takeaway is that attackers did not need to breach 178 separate companies. They exploited one software provider whose code was embedded across hundreds of websites.

Crypto Exchanges and Banks Are Both Taking Hits

Crypto’s security problems extend beyond Etherscan and the Optimizely incident. DeFiLlama’s hack tracker recorded several attacks during the week, including a $10.39 million incident involving Lighter Perps on November 16. The attacker exploited a compromised trader API key, enabling unauthorized withdrawals.

Lighter said its protocol and smart contracts were not compromised. It temporarily suspended withdrawals and activated Guardian mode to prevent further unauthorized activity.

Another incident hit MORE Markets, where an attacker exploited a lending mechanism to drain approximately $308,000 in WFLOW. B18 TimeBank also suffered an exploit on November 17, losing $404,540 in USDC through its reward voucher redemption mechanism.

These incidents show different weaknesses across crypto infrastructure. Not every loss comes from a broken smart contract. Compromised credentials, vulnerable applications and flawed authorization mechanisms can be equally damaging.

Traditional finance faces its own problems. French lender Crédit Mutuel Arkéa disclosed a cyber heist earlier in November, with hackers stealing approximately €100 million through fraudulent transactions originating from the bank’s own accounts. The bank said customer assets were not affected, although some transactions were temporarily suspended.

Deutsche Bank also made headlines on November 17 after confidential internal documents surfaced through an international journalistic investigation. It was a document leak, not a confirmed breach of its current banking systems.

Deutsche Bank said security testing found no indication that its current IT environment, account information, login credentials, or payment data had been compromised. Yet, it has greater effects to geopolitics.

Banking institutions are not immune to major security incidents simply because they operate under traditional financial regulations.

Is Crypto Actually Less Safe Than Traditional Banking?

Crypto has suffered enormous losses. The October Binance incident alone involved $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, making it one of the largest cryptocurrency heists on record. Yet, traditional finance also faces attacks involving payment infrastructure, third-party service providers, and internal transaction systems.

The Optimizely incident is particularly revealing. Both HSBC and Ledger appeared among the affected organizations. The vulnerability did not care whether visitors were interacting with a traditional financial institution or a crypto company.

Neither system offers complete protection. The real question is whether companies can secure the increasingly complex infrastructure connecting their services. A single compromised vendor can expose hundreds of organizations, while one stolen credential can bypass otherwise sophisticated security systems.

Crypto users have every reason to demand stronger protections. But traditional banking customers should not mistake regulation and familiar branding for immunity.

With Etherscan possibly being hacked, the data provider is now joining the growing list of companies investigating security incidents.

title: Why Is CoreWeave Stock Gaining Wednesday?
description:
CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) stock rose nearly 4% in Wednesday’s premarket session after NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) reported stronger-than-expected quarterly results and issued an upbeat outlook.
The chipmaker’s strong performance eased concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) demand and lifted investor sentiment toward specialized AI cloud infrastructure providers, also known as neocloud companies.
On Tuesday, NVIDIA reported revenue of $115.84 billion, exceeding the $109.08 billion analyst estimate. Adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share beat the Wall Street estimate of $2.48, according to Benzinga Pro.
Other AI infrastructure stocks also gained following the results. In Tuesday’s after-hours session, Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ:NBIS) rose 5.44% to $111.76, while IREN Ltd. (NASDAQ:IREN) gained 3.89% to $16.42.
CoreWeave Reports Strong Revenue Growth
CoreWeave recently reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, exceeding the $3.55 billion analyst estimate and marking a 168% year-over-year increase.
The company reported an adjusted loss of 95 cents per share, narrower than the $1.16 loss analysts expected. Meanwhile, CoreWeave’s revenue backlog reached $132.5 billion, reflecting strong demand for its AI infrastructure services.
Wall Street Remains Bullish Despite Forecast Cuts
CoreWeave carries a consensus Buy rating with an average price forecast of $102.83.
However, several analysts lowered their price forecasts on Nov. 12:
Barclays: Maintained an Equal-Weight rating and lowered its price forecast to $85.
Macquarie: Maintained an Outperform rating and lowered its price forecast to $120.
Argus Research: Maintained a Buy rating and lowered its price forecast to $100.
Technical Analysis
Despite Wednesday’s gains, CoreWeave continues to trade below its key moving averages, signaling persistent weakness.
The stock trades 3.6% below its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) of $53.82. It also sits 26.7% below its 50-day SMA of $70.81 and 41.4% below its 200-day SMA of $88.58.
The moving averages reinforce the bearish outlook. The 20-day SMA remains below the 50-day SMA, which sits below the 200-day SMA. This pattern aligns with the “death cross” that formed in July.
However, the moving average convergence divergence (MACD) indicator suggests selling pressure is easing. The MACD remains above its signal line, while the positive histogram indicates improving momentum.
CoreWeave trades near the lower end of its 52-week range of $40.58 to $138.25. A sustained move above the 20-day SMA could provide an early recovery signal.
Additional resistance lies between $66.53 and $70.81, where the 50-day exponential moving average (EMA) and SMA sit, respectively.
Key Resistance: $53.82, corresponding to the 20-day SMA.
Key Support: $40.58, the 52-week low recorded in November.
CRWV Price Action: CoreWeave shares were up 3.97% at $51.87 during Wednesday’s premarket session, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Cognizant and Qualys Redefine AI-Era Managed Security Service
description: Cognizant will use the full Qualys portfolio to bring its clients what the frontier AI era demands: AI-speed detection, hyper-prioritization, and confident remediation for every zero-day. When a critical zero-day goes public, security leaders ask two questions: which assets are affected, and how fast can we safely fix them? For most enterprises, the current answer […]
fullContent:
Cognizant will use the full Qualys portfolio to bring its clients what the frontier AI era demands: AI-speed detection, hyper-prioritization, and confident remediation for every zero-day.

When a critical zero-day goes public, security leaders ask two questions: which assets are affected, and how fast can we safely fix them? For most enterprises, the current answer is days, then weeks.

Frontier AI makes that remediation timeframe dangerous. Microsoft’s November Patch Tuesday alone carried 1,093 vulnerabilities, up from 93 in November 2025 before frontier AI models arrived. AI-assisted attackers can weaponize a new advisory in four to twelve hours, while scan-driven detection often takes 24 to 36 hours just to show which assets are affected. The risk is already real: Cognizant’s 2026 Cybersecurity Pulse Poll found that 83% of participating U.S. enterprises had an AI-related security incident in the past 24 months.

Knowing what to fix is only half the gap. Every step from finding to fix is still gated by people, for one reason: fear that a patch will break production, that a reboot will take down a critical system, or that there is no fast way back. Teams will not hand fixes to automation they do not trust.

Cognizant helps the world’s largest enterprises scale with AI, through its AI Builder approach, and recognizes that its clients need security that moves at machine speed. Already running managed services on Qualys ETM, Cognizant is now expanding to the full Qualys portfolio, including TruRisk Eliminate. That is why I am excited to welcome Cognizant to the Qualys Global mROC Alliance.

Managed detection is table stakes. This is the dawn of the 24-hour autonomous remediation service, run from Qualys ETM: a zero-day disclosed, detected, prioritized, and remediated within a day.

Why the Qualys Platform Fits Cognizant’s Approach

Running zero-day response as a service, at enterprise scale, puts specific demands on the platform underneath. Cognizant needed three capabilities working as one:

  • One record for every asset, across every tool, built from Qualys and non-Qualys sources, so there is no reconciling data across disparate tools before anyone can act.
  • Exploit validation in each client’s own environment, so every hour of the client’s team’s time goes to risk that is real.
  • Remediation with confidence, so automation can be trusted within production systems.

Qualys delivers all three on one platform, with the agentic AI to run them at machine speed.

Cognizant brings what a platform alone cannot: Cyber Vulnerability Management services and threat intelligence, delivery experience inside large enterprises, and a view of risk in financial terms for the board. Its operators run the Risk Operations Center, powered by Qualys ETM to navigate inside each client’s own tools, change windows, and approvals. Clients keep control of what gets fixed and when. Cognizant carries the daily work.

“Our 2026 Cybersecurity Pulse Poll shows that strength in one control, such as detection or remediation, still leaves enterprises exposed in the AI era. Together with Qualys, we are connecting detection, prioritization and remediation into one managed operating model, helping clients reduce risk, strengthen resilience and scale AI with confidence.”
— Vishal Salvi, SVP and Global Head of Cybersecurity, Cognizant

Cognizant will deliver four mROC services on the Qualys platform:

  • Cyber risk quantification and advisory services. Cyber risk for business applications shown in dollars, with a personalized risk plan and a report for the board.
  • Onboarding and integration. The security tools a customer already owns connected into one record for each asset, with data quality checked from day one.
  • Risk monitoring as a managed service. AI-speed alerts on new CVEs, a validated queue instead of noise, and a weekly exposure review, using InstaScan, Agent Val, and ROCky.

Risk remediation as a managed service. A wave-based plan built from the Risk Elimination Playbook, zero-touch remediation where it is safe, and proof the fix held, using TruRisk Eliminate, TruConfidence, and Agent Sara.

AI-Speed Detection: Every Exposure Known in Minutes

Frontier AI has changed the rhythm of disclosure. Vulnerabilities now land in volume, and attackers act on them in hours, well inside any scan cycle.

Qualys InstaScan, delivered by Agent Insta, closes that gap. It turns the inventory and telemetry a client already has, from Qualys and non-Qualys sources, into high-confidence findings within minutes of disclosure. No new scan, no new agent.

On November’s Patch Tuesday, InstaScan delivered 90% of detections within minutes. The first landed about 40 minutes before Microsoft’s own release notes went live. With Cognizant, that speed turns into action. Through its risk monitoring service, Cognizant analysts watch for new disclosures every day, confirm each exposure, and route it to the right asset owner with context. The client’s team no longer chases owners or rebuilds asset lists every time a new CVE trends.

Hyper-Prioritization: Proven Exploitability

More vulnerabilities do not mean more risk. Of the 48,172 vulnerabilities disclosed in 2025, the Qualys Threat Research Unit found only 357 (0.74%) confirmed remotely exploitable and actively weaponized. No team can work the full list, and none should have to.

Agent Val and TruConfirm test what is actually exploitable in the client’s own environment, with existing controls counted. Critical on paper but blocked by a control? It leaves the urgent queue. Exploitable on a PCI-scoped server? It goes to the top.

Cyber Risk Quantification (CRQ) then puts validated risk in dollars, by business application, so the CISO can show the board what each fix is worth.

With Cognizant, the short list becomes a working rhythm. Through its risk monitoring and advisory services, Cognizant keeps each client’s validated queue current and reviews it with them every week. The client’s team stops triaging noise and starts each week knowing exactly what to fix first.

Autonomous Remediation: Remediate with Confidence and Maintain Operational Resiliency

That fear is why the global mean time to remediate sits at about 30 days. TruRisk Eliminate, with TruConfidence, removes it by protecting operational resiliency before, during, and after every change.

  • Before: TruRisk Eliminate chooses the safest fix for each finding: patch, mitigate, isolate, or uninstall. A patch reliability score decides what deploys automatically and what goes ring by ring.
  • During: Changes roll out in waves, starting with low-risk rings. System health is watched through each wave, and rollback restores a known-good state if health drops.
  • After: AI-powered patch failure analysis pinpoints why a change failed and the corrective actions, and automated rollback restores a known-good state.

Showing clients the 1% that matters

Cognizant can open every client engagement with a Risk Elimination Playbook, powered by TruConfidence and built for that client’s environment. It narrows the backlog to the 1% that must be fixed now and moves the rest into planned software updates. It also benchmarks the client’s mean time to remediate against peers, and shows how much of the backlog autonomous remediation can close, and how much faster.

It becomes the plan behind every remediation wave and the baseline for every review.

Where Managed Security Goes Next

The three pillars together provide a new kind of service: 24-hour autonomous remediation, run from ETM. Cognizant can take a critical zero-day from disclosure to remediation within a day, for every client, with operational resiliency built in at every step.

Managed security is moving from raising alerts to closing risk. Cognizant is among the first to deliver that at enterprise scale, and I expect it to set the bar enterprises hold every provider to. That is what the Global mROC Alliance was built for: the platform, the certification path, and the operating model to run the Risk Operations Center as a service.

Attackers already move at AI speed. This expanded partnership helps tip the balance back toward the defense.

To learn more, visit the Qualys Global mROC Alliance page, read the press release, or contact your Cognizant or Qualys account team.

title: Arbitrum Price Drops 19% in Seven Days Despite $7.4M Revenue and USDG Growth
description: Arbitrum booked $7.4 million in revenue and USDG lending passed $153 million, yet ARB fell 19% in a week. Buyers now need to defend support near $0.11.
fullContent:
Arbitrum's latest revenue report shows a network earning steady income from several sources, with stablecoin demand climbing alongside it.

ARB holders have little to show for it. The token kept sliding with a weak crypto market this week. Traders now want to know whether stronger fundamentals can ever lift a token that earns no direct share of fees.

Arbitrum Books $7.4M as USDG Lending Passes $153M

Arbitrum reported $7.4 million in recent revenue in a post on the network's official X account. The haul lifts its 2026 total above $13.6 million. For a layer 2 network that sells faster and cheaper Ethereum transactions, that is a meaningful income line.

The money comes from five separate streams. Transaction fees make up one source, and treasury management makes up another. Spreading income across several channels means the network leans less on any single business.

Stablecoin activity is also growing. Adoption of USDG, a dollar-pegged token, keeps rising on Arbitrum. Lending of USDG on Morpho, a decentralized lending protocol, now holds more than $153 million in total value locked. That figure measures the deposits users have committed to the market, and it signals growing trust in the asset.

Arbitrum has also built ties with traditional finance. The network counts Cross River Bank and SBI Digital Markets as partners. Both firms give the ecosystem a bridge to regulated banking and capital markets, which could draw more institutional users over time.

A Broad Crypto Selloff Swallows the Good News

Those revenue numbers arrived at an awkward moment. Crypto markets are in a broad retreat, and bitcoin is leading the way down. Bitcoin has dropped about 13% over the past week, dragging most major tokens with it.

ARB has fared worse. The token fell roughly 19% over the same seven days. That gap is common for layer 2 tokens, which tend to swing harder than bitcoin in both directions. When traders cut risk, smaller and more speculative assets usually get sold first.

The network's design also limits the boost from good news. Arbitrum's income flows to its DAO treasury, the pool of funds governed by token holders. ARB holders receive no direct share of those fees.

Treasury Gains While Token Holders Wait

The split between network income and token price creates clear winners and losers.

  • DAO and treasury: Steady revenue pays for operations and funds grants without forcing large token sales.
  • ARB holders: The token has lost about 31% over the past month. For now, those price losses outweigh any comfort from stronger fundamentals.
  • USDG issuers and Morpho lenders: Rising stablecoin demand brings more deposits, more borrowing and more fee income.
  • Rival layer 2 networks: Competitors face pressure to show income of their own, or risk looking weaker to builders and investors.

$0.11 Becomes the Floor Bulls Cannot Lose

Arbitrum (ARB) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

ARB trades near $0.13, down about 3% in the past day. The token sits below its 50-day average near $0.16. It also trades under its 200-day average. Both lines now act as ceilings, which keeps the broader trend in sellers' favor.

Momentum is weak as well. RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads 35. That is weak but short of oversold, so there is still room for further selling before buyers typically step in. The MACD indicator also points down.

On the daily chart, the green line marks support near $0.11. Holding that level is the main job for buyers. A clean break would expose the next support around $0.083, a much deeper drop.

Any rebound faces the red line near $0.15. That level matches the 200-day average, which makes it a tough barrier to clear.

What Could Turn ARB Around Next

Three things could shift the picture for ARB in the coming weeks.

  • Revenue and USDG growth: Another strong income update, plus rising USDG deposits on Morpho, would show the network keeps gaining users.
  • Bitcoin's direction: If bitcoin steadies, selling pressure on altcoins like ARB could ease.
  • A close above $0.17: A daily close past that level would signal buyers have returned with real conviction.

title: Nvidia’s China Exit Could Trigger a Bull-Bear Showdown: 6 Leveraged ETFs to Watch Wednesday
description:
Nvidia Corp’s (NASDAQ:NVDA) China retreat has handed traders a fresh reason to reassess their bets on the world’s most valuable chipmaker. With the company halting H200 shipments to China, tighter U.S. export controls and a leadership shake-up adding to the uncertainty, leveraged Nvidia ETFs could see heightened trading interest on Wednesday.
The announcement came during Nvidia’s first earnings call since co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down, with interim CEO Colette Kress confirming that the company was no longer shipping licensed Hopper-generation data center products to China. Nvidia had generated $2.4 billion from licensed Hopper products in the quarter ended October 25, although the company did not clarify whether the suspension would be permanent. 
The bigger concern is whether the latest restrictions could eventually affect Nvidia’s access to customers beyond mainland China. New U.S. rules targeting data centers serving Chinese customers remotely could push some operators toward alternative chip suppliers, potentially challenging Nvidia’s dominance in AI infrastructure.
Moreover, Jefferies estimates that the new restrictions could shave $44 billion to $62 billion off Nvidia’s data center revenue next year.
But the bearish case is not straightforward. Kress argued that demand for next-generation chips, including Vera Rubin, remains strong enough to offset the impact of export restrictions. Nvidia also expects $130 billion in revenue for the current quarter, with its guidance assuming no data center compute revenue from China.
Leveraged NVDA ETFs to watch
The competing narratives could put bullish and bearish single-stock ETFs in the spotlight:
GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA Daily ETF (NASDAQ:NVDL): A potential vehicle for traders betting that AI demand and Nvidia’s revenue outlook will outweigh China-related concerns. The fund is already up almost 5% in pre-market trading, Wednesday.
Direxion Daily NVDA Bull 2X ETF (NASDAQ:NVDU): Another leveraged bullish play that could benefit from a rebound in Nvidia shares. The fund is trading 4.5% higher in pre-market trading, Wednesday.
T-REX 2X Long NVIDIA Daily Target ETF (BATS:NVDX): Worth watching if traders look to buy into a recovery. The fund is up 5.4% in pre-market hours.
GraniteShares 2x Short NVDA Daily ETF (NASDAQ:NVD): Offers the opposite trade, targeting twice the inverse of Nvidia’s daily performance.
T-REX 2X Inverse NVIDIA Daily Target ETF (BATS:NVDQ): Another bearish vehicle that could attract attention if selling pressure intensifies. The fund dipped mopre than 5% pre-market.
Tradr 1.5X Short NVDA Daily ETF (NASDAQ:NVDS): Gives traders an additional way to position for a potential decline.
What Should Traders Watch Wednesday?
The immediate test will be whether Nvidia shares can hold their ground as investors digest the China developments. A sustained recovery could revive demand for bullish leveraged ETFs, while renewed selling could put inverse products in focus.
Importantly, Nvidia’s China exposure needs perspective. The $2.4 billion in licensed Hopper sales represented only a small portion of its overall business, and the company has already factored zero China data center revenue into its current-quarter outlook. 
For traders, Wednesday’s action is less about betting on the end of Nvidia’s AI dominance and more about determining whether export restrictions and leadership uncertainty are enough to disrupt its momentum.
Leveraged ETFs reset daily, so their returns over multiple sessions can diverge significantly from the stated daily multiples. Traders should watch volatility and price levels closely rather than treating these funds as straightforward long-term bets.

title: Lowe's Delivers Resilient Quarter Despite Challenging Housing Market
description:
Lowe’s Companies Inc. (NYSE:LOW) stock fell nearly 5% in Wednesday’s premarket session despite the home improvement retailer beating third-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings and revenue estimates and raising its annual sales forecast.
A CNBC report said Lowe’s has previously flagged pressure on home improvement spending as inflation and economic uncertainty strain household budgets. The retailer also faces a sluggish housing market and elevated mortgage rates.
Despite these headwinds, Lowe’s demonstrated resilience as continued demand across its Pro, online and home services businesses helped extend its comparable sales growth streak to six consecutive quarters.
The retailer’s decision to raise its annual sales forecast further underscored the resilience of its Total Home strategy.
Revenue rose 9.3% year over year to $22.756 billion, surpassing the Wall Street estimate of $22.408 billion. 
Adjusted earnings of $3.10 per share exceeded the analyst estimate of $2.88.
Earnings Growth and Tariff Refund Impact
GAAP diluted EPS increased to $2.98 from $2.88 a year earlier, while adjusted EPS rose 1.3% to $3.10. Net earnings reached $1.67 billion, up from $1.62 billion.
Results included approximately $250 million in pretax benefits from International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariff refunds, adding 34 cents to both GAAP and adjusted EPS.
Lowe’s also recorded $96 million in pretax amortization expenses related to its Foundation Building Materials and Artisan Design Group acquisitions.





Read Also:

Home Depot Taps CFO Richard McPhail to Lead, Narrows Profit Outlook





Comparable Sales Growth and CEO Outlook
Comparable sales rose 1.8%, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of growth. Online sales increased 17.4%, while Pro and home services delivered solid performance.
Gross margin narrowed to 32.95% from 34.19%, while operating margin declined to 11.32% from 11.92%.
“We just delivered our sixth consecutive quarter of positive comp sales driven by continued growth across Pro, Online, and Home Services. These results reflect the resiliency of our Total Home strategy,” said CEO Marvin Ellison.
In a Wednesday CNBC interview, Ellison said Lowe’s and Home Depot Inc. (NYSE:HD) could both outperform, noting that the two companies account for less than 30% of the $1 trillion U.S. market, according to Benzinga Pro.
Ellison also told CNBC that employees using AI tools improve shopper satisfaction, while customers using AI tools achieve three times the conversion rate.
Cash Flow and Capital Allocation
For the first nine months, operating cash flow reached $8.69 billion, compared with $8.30 billion a year earlier. Capital expenditures totaled $1.66 billion.
Lowe’s ended the quarter with $3.43 billion in cash and equivalents and $37.55 billion in total debt.
As of Oct. 30, 2026, Lowe’s operated 1,762 stores spanning 197 million square feet of retail selling space.
Fiscal 2026 Outlook
Lowe’s raised annual revenue guidance to $92.5 billion from $92 billion, above the $92.093 billion analyst estimate, and increased its comparable sales growth forecast to 0.5% from flat.
However, it lowered operating margin guidance to 11.1% from 11.2% and adjusted operating margin guidance to 11.5% from 11.6%.
Lowe’s reaffirmed GAAP EPS guidance of approximately $11.75, below the $11.85 estimate, and adjusted EPS guidance of approximately $12.25, below the $12.28 estimate.
LOW Price Action: Lowe’s Companies shares were down 4.74% at $210.01 during premarket trading on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.
