title: XRP Eyes $1 Recovery as Major Banks Disclose ETF Holdings
description:
XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) has gained nearly 2% over the past 24 hours but remains below the $1 mark, even as major banks disclosed significant XRP ETF holdings.  
The banks’ filings highlight growing participation in XRP-linked investment products across traditional financial institutions, although the size and structure of their positions vary considerably.
Some banks hold spot XRP ETFs, while others use futures-based products, leveraged funds or options-income strategies.
Major Banks Expand XRP ETF Exposure
Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS) reported $144 million in XRP and XRP-linked ETF holdings as of Sept. 30, up from $87 million in Q2. 
The increase comes amid the bank disclosing positions across five spot XRP funds, including products from Franklin Templeton, Bitwise and Grayscale.
Seven other major banks reported $29.4 million in combined XRP-linked ETF holdings in filings submitted between Nov. 9 and Nov. 16.
Intesa Sanpaolo: $27.21 million across Grayscale and Bitwise XRP ETFs.
UBS (NYSE:UBS): $1.91 million across futures, leveraged and income-focused XRP products.
Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS): $116,097 across Franklin, REX-Osprey and Bitwise funds.
Bank of America (NYSE:BAC): $106,610 in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF.
JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM): $8,996 in the Bitwise XRP ETF.
National Bank of Canada: $5,485 in Bitwise XRP ETF shares.
Bank of Montreal (NYSE:BMO): $4,267 across REX-Osprey and ProShares Ultra XRP.
Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) disclosed 668 Bitwise XRP ETF shares worth $11,109 as of Sep. 30, compared with 787 shares valued at $9,177 at the end of June. Although its share count declined 15.1%, the position’s value increased 21.1%, reflecting a higher ETF valuation.
What’s Next For XRP
CryptoQuant data shows XRP’s spot-to-futures trading volume ratio fell 34% over the past seven days, signaling growing reliance on leveraged trading rather than spot demand.
This makes the altcoin more vulnerable to sharp price swings, particularly below $1.

title: Stephen A. Smith calls out critics demanding he fact-check Trump 'on the spot' in interviews
description: Stephen A. Smith lambasted critics of his White House interview with President Donald Trump who claimed he didn't fact-check the president enough times.
fullContent:
ESPN personality and "Straight Shooter" host Stephen A. Smith pushed back against critics Tuesday who accused him of not adequately fact-checking President Donald Trump during his White House interview last week.

Smith said that though his interview had been largely well-received, some "people who have been in this industry before" have called him out for not pushing back against Trump. The sports host took issue with this critique by pointing out that the interview would not have happened had he focused on fact-checking the president.

"You don't walk into the White House and talk to the President of the United States and plan on fact-checking him on the spot or interrupting him every sentence that he utters out of his mouth," Smith said. "You know why? Because you won't get through the damn interview. That's why."

JOE ROGAN SAYS PODCASTERS HAVE NO BUSINESS AT TRUMP PRESS CONFERENCES ALONGSIDE REAL JOURNALISTS

Smith noted that Trump often "filibusters," goes off track, and embellishes his comments during interviews and calling them out would either take too much time or risk Trump ending the interview early.

"I wanted to be able to challenge and push back in certain respects, but in the same breath, keep him in the damn chair because he does have the potential to just get up and walk off as he has done to people before," Smith said.

Though he is not against pushing back against interviewees, including the president, Smith emphasized the need to pick and choose where to respond.

THE ‘CROOKED’ CHARGE AGAINST NBC: WHY THE DONALD TRUMP-KRISTEN WELKER SLUGFEST WENT OFF THE RAILS

"The goal, at least for me, is not to fact-check them on the spot in most instances," Smith said. "It's to make sure that they're quoted for the record so we always have them on the record about what their positions are. That way when we go back to double- and triple-check the facts, we're able to say, 'Hey, that wasn't true.'"

Smith then spent the rest of the video fact-checking some of Trump's statements and urged people on both sides to "stop the BS."

"Ladies and gentlemen, this is chess, it ain't checkers. And if every politician had to get fact-checked in real time, you wouldn't get interviews. I can give you plenty of Democrats that don't want to show up and get fact-checked. And Republicans, for that matter. Let's not act like we don't know any better," Smith said.

STEPHEN A SMITH DEBRIEFS INTERVIEW WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP, WARNS DEMOCRATS FACE STEEP CHALLENGE

Fox News Digital reached out to Smith's representatives and the White House for comment.

Smith, who has criticized both Democrats and Republicans in the past, has repeatedly defended meeting with Trump despite disagreeing with his politics.

"There are so many people that have this mentality, ‘Why even waste time talking to him?’ Whether you like him or not, he’s the President of the United States of America. He’s not going away until 2028. At least. He’s not going away," Smith said last month on "The View."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Newsbusters Managing Editor Curtis Houck agreed with Smith that interviewing high-profile subjects like the president is a "balancing act."

"A constant state of antagonistic fact-checks or baboonish hectoring can derail an interview and prevent it from creating headlines other than its combative nature. As much as liberal, elitist journalists claim otherwise, so many love being the headline. With this President, he can often make headlines in sit-downs when he's allowed time to speak. There is absolutely merit to what Stephen A. Smith said," Houck said.

title: Sam Leavitt was asked about finishing LSU’s season. His answer explains why college football is lost
description: College Football Playoff rankings leave LSU out of the top 25 as QB Sam Leavitt's press conference answers spark debate over NIL and the transfer portal.
fullContent:
The newest batch of College Football Playoff rankings came out Tuesday night, and I'm fairly certain LSU is the only SEC program NOT in the top 25 at this point.

If that doesn't show you just how poorly Lane Kiffin's first season in Baton Rouge is going, I don't know what will.

The Tigers are currently 6-4, losers of two in a row, and well out of the playoff picture with two weeks left in the regular season. It's been an awful year for LSU. It's been an awful year for Kiffin.

CURT CIGNETTI SLAMS CFP OVER INDIANA SLANDER, DAKICH BACKS UP THE HOOSIERS HEAD COACH - LISTEN NOW

And, it's been a really awful year for QB Sam Leavitt, who has been at the center of some pretty big scrutiny all week after walking off the field after Saturday's loss to Texas before singing the alma mater.

Obviously, it doesn't help that Leavitt has played pretty terribly this season. IT really doesn't help that this is his third team in three years, and he's currently getting paid roughly $4.5 million.

And it really, really, really doesn't help when he gives answers like this:

Lordy. It's just the worst set of answers I think I've heard in the history of press conferences. Just back-to-back whiffs. Horrible. I'd imagine the poor SID in the corner couldn't get Leavitt off that podium fast enough. He (or she) must've been SWEATING bullets the entire time.

On the motivation for the rest of the season: "One, I just think as a man, you go to work, put your best foot forward and finish everything that you start. That's definitely a thing for me. For everyone, whether you want to go to the NFL, come back here or transfer, whatever you put out on the field is going to give yourself the best opportunity for next year. That's kind of my talk to the whole team."

And, of course, on leaving the field early after last week's loss to Texas: "Oh yeah, I mean I don't even know what you're referring to. Like staying and singing the song after, you're saying? I don't know what anyone's really saying to be honest. I'm not even on any socials, so. I mean, but yes they are."

The first answer was bad. The second one was just Leavitt playing dumb. We all know Sam Leavitt "is on socials." He's a 21-year-old with millions of dollars in the bank.

He's on socials, folks. He's on socials that you and I don't even know exist. He knew exactly what the reporter was referring to, even though — to be fair — it was a horrible question. Just spit it out!

I've already harped on Leavitt leaving the field earlier this week. I wrote about it two days ago and don't need to rehash it here.

Instead, I'd like to break down that first answer about playing the rest of the season ...

"For everyone, whether you want to go to the NFL, come back here or transfer, whatever you put out on the field is going to give yourself the best opportunity for next year. That's kind of my talk to the whole team."

If you didn't think college football was completely lost before, you have to see it now, right? It's now the NFL. It's professional football. It's a transactional league.

A MAJOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL PROBLEM WAS ON FULL DISPLAY THIS WEEKEND, NICK SABAN WARNED US & AT&T LILY RETURNS!

Do you know who Sam sounds like? He sounds like every single player in the NFL playing on a terrible team who's asked about coming to work every day.

They do it because there are 31 other teams watching, and one of them could potentially sign them in the offseason. That's what they say. That's the reality of the NFL.

They are not playing for their current employer. They're playing for their next one.

HERE'S WHY NICK SABAN AND NOTRE DAME'S PETE BEVACQUA ARE WRONG ABOUT NIL RUINING COLLEGE FOOTBALL

That's the motivation now for Sam Leavitt and everyone else in college football over these next few weeks.

And it's disgusting.

Nowhere in that clip did Leavitt talk about LSU. Or playing for LSU. Or playing for the fans, the students, the teachers, or the town. He didn't mention the school once.

He mentioned playing out the rest of the season so he could put something on tape for his next team, or for the next league. That's the reality of college football in 2026, folks. These players have no connection to the schools they play for anymore. None.

Of course Sam Leavitt's going to leave the field early after a loss and not stick around for the song. He doesn't know the song! None of them do. These aren't guys who grew up in Baton Rouge and have spent the last three years working their way up the LSU depth chart.

These are guys who are on their third team in three years, and eyeing their fourth next season because this year didn't work out.

That's what the transfer portal has created. That's what NIL has created.

Leavitt's answer — while horrible — wasn't wrong. It wasn't a lie. It wasn't a bunch of spoon-fed BS to a group of local reporters.

It was, unfortunately, a very honest look at the college football landscape.

title: Far-left groups cheer Mamdani for disbanding elite NYPD protest team
description: Groups in Neville Roy Singham's network, including the Party for Socialism and Liberation, celebrate Zohran Mamdani's move to dissolve the NYPD's SRG unit.
fullContent:
Far-left radical groups, including some within tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham’s pro-CCP network, are cheering New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s decision to dissolve an elite NYPD unit responsible for handling protests.

After Mamdani announced Monday morning that he would disband the elite police department's Strategic Response Group, applause came in rapid succession from nonprofit organizations that regularly mobilize protests of ICE, Israel, capitalism and America in general.

"The mass movement has won the disbanding of NYPD’s Strategic Response Group — but the fight continues," the Party for Socialism and Liberation posted to X following the announcement.

MAMDANI PREPARES TO FULFILL PROMISE TO AXE NYPD UNIT RESPONSIBLE FOR CONTROLLING PROTEST VIOLENCE

"For everyone who has been kettled, beaten, pepper-sprayed or dragged onto a bus by the SRG, this is a real victory. But it was not handed down from City Hall. It was won by a mass movement that refused to let a campaign promise die quietly. The work of turning this victory into lasting change for working people is just beginning," the post added.

The Party for Socialism and Liberation is part of a protest network of activist groups tied to Singham, a Shanghai-based tech tycoon married to far-left CodePink co-founder Jodie Evans. A Fox News Digital analysis found that Singham funneled $278 million into six nonprofits, including $22.4 million to the People's Forum, the Manhattan organizing hub that works closely with the Party for Socialism and Liberation on protests.

SHANGHAI-BASED TYCOON NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S 'SQUAD,' BERNIE SANDERS DONATIONS RESURFACE

Fox News Digital has witnessed protest foot soldiers and field marshals from the Party for Socialism and Liberation enter and leave the People's Forum headquarters on W. 37th Street, their signs, wagons and loudspeakers in tow.

The Party for Socialism and Liberation also shares leadership with Singham-funded groups. Claudia De la Cruz, a 2024 presidential candidate for the Party for Socialism and Liberation leader, was on the People's Forum's founding board alongside Evans.

Longtime organizer Brian Becker, a self-described communist, helped build the People's Forum into a base for the Party for Socialism and Liberation and the ANSWER Coalition, and his son, Ben Becker, is editor-in-chief of the Singham-funded BreakThrough News, which also shares a home at the People’s Forum headquarters on W. 37th Street.

SINGHAM-BACKED, PRO-CHINA GROUP DROPS HUGE SUM ON MANHATTAN HQ AS FEDS PROBE SHADOWY NETWORK

By early morning, self-declared Marxist influencer and Twitch streamer Hasan Piker weighed in, saying he was "glad" the unit had been disbanded.

At 11:16 a.m., Piker posted a response to Mamdani’s message, skipping capitalizations as he wrote: "one of the hardest problems for NYC mayor is police reform. The SRG is a ‘counter terrorism’ unit that has primarily been deployed on protestors. glad the mayor is moving on this promise to disband."

HASAN PIKER NAMES PRO-CCP TYCOON SINGHAM AS FINANCIER OF 'POLITICAL MOVEMENTS' DESPITE NONPROFIT VENEER

By the afternoon, at 2:55 p.m., Nerdeen Kiswani, an anti-Israel activist who founded the organization Within Our Lifetime, responded to the announcement by calling for consequences for NYPD officers who subdued protests, while saying the disbanding is "overdue and welcome news" in a post on X.

"The settlement gave us a way to challenge the NYPD when it violated protesters’ rights, and officers violated it anyway," Kiswani wrote. "The limits Mamdani announced today give us more specific rules to point to when we challenge police conduct. We’ll see whether the NYPD actually follows them when we’re back in the streets, especially when we’re protesting something the people in power would rather we stay quiet about."

Mamdani previously joined Kiswani in an anti-Israel protest, where calls to "globalize the intifada" rang out from the protesters in the crowd. Within Our Lifetime is not a registered nonprofit, so its tax filings and funding aren’t available to the public. Fox News Digital hasn’t identified any direct ties to the Singham network aside from joining member groups in demonstrations.

Mamdani’s announcement fulfilled a campaign promise he made to disband the group. While the Party for Socialism and Liberation says "the mass movement has won," it’s unclear whether the organization had any impact on the mayor’s decision.

MAMDANI GUTS ELITE NYPD TACTICAL UNIT, BACKS 'CIVILIAN-LED APPROACH' TO RESPONDING TO PROTESTS

"New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat," Mamdani told reporters in a news conference announcing the changes. "We are establishing a new, civilian-led approach that prioritizes dialogue, engagement and de-escalation."

Former NYPD officers weighed in on Mamdani’s decision, saying the move would empower criminals and promote anarchy.

POLICE GROUPS CONDEMN MAMDANI OVER AXING ELITE NYPD UNIT

"I think it’s one more step towards emboldening the criminals, emboldening the anarchists and emboldening the terrorists," said James Gagliano, a retired FBI supervisory special agent and Fox News contributor who spent years working alongside the NYPD.

"New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat," Mamdani told reporters in a news conference announcing the changes. "We are establishing a new, civilian-led approach that prioritizes dialogue, engagement and de-escalation."

Mamdani said the disbanding of the NYPD unit would be replaced with split responsibility between a civilian-led division and new police units.

title: US launches unarmed ICBM with Trump in Asia in routine test
description: The Air Force says it carried out a "routine" test launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile, shortly before President Trump arrived in China.
fullContent:
The U.S. military carried out a test launch of an unarmed Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) as President Donald Trump was traveling aboard Air Force One to China.

The Air Force Global Strike Command said the "routine test" late Tuesday at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, outside of Los Angeles, "was scheduled years ago and is not in response to world events."

"The ability to conduct these rigorous, realistic tests relies on the dedication of our Airmen and is foundational to ensuring the safety and surety of the Minuteman system," U.S. Air Force Gen. S.L. Davis, commander of Air Force Global Strike Command, said in a statement.

"Test opportunities, including this most recent launch, assess the entirety of the ICBM enterprise and provide various government agencies data to inform ICBM sustainment, engineering, and lifecycle analysis efforts," Air Force Global Strike Command added. "AFGSC has completed over 300 Minuteman III test launches to date."

US RAMPS NUCLEAR WEAPONS PRODUCTION TO COLD WAR LEVELS AS CHINA PURSUES ‘UNPRECEDENTED’ BUILDUP

Following the test launch, Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted Trump as he arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday.

The Air Force describes the LGM-30G Minuteman III missile as the "land-based component of the U.S. nuclear triad, providing a responsive and survivable strategic deterrent.

"The current force consists of 400 Minuteman III missiles dispersed at F.E. Warren Air Force Base, Wyoming; Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana; and Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota," the Air Force said.

NORTH KOREA MISSILE COULD PUT GUAM IN RANGE AS KIM REBUFFS TRUMP OUTREACH: EXPERT

"Missile combat crews, consisting of two officers, are on alert around the clock in underground Launch Control Centers. A robust and redundant communications network ensures the president and U.S. Strategic Command have reliable, direct contact with each crew," the Air Force also said, noting that the Minuteman III system was first deployed in 1970 and has "evolved to meet new security challenges through more than 60 years of continuous service."

The last unarmed Minuteman III test launch happened on May 20 at Vandenberg Space Force Base.

"This launch allows us to authenticate the complete performance profile of the Minuteman III," Lt. Col. Karrie Wray, commander of the 576th Flight Test Squadron, said at the time. "It confirms the precision of the system, ensuring the reentry vehicle can be delivered to its target with pinpoint accuracy."

Fox News' Lucas Tomlinson contributed to this report.

title: 3,300-year-old bronze sword emerges from Italian lake and still has a 'sharp edge'
description: Archaeologists recovered a 3,300-year-old bronze sword from Lake Mezzano, a volcanic lake in Italy, and it's still sharp after 33 centuries underwater.
fullContent:
Italian officials recently announced the remarkable discovery of a 3,300-year-old bronze sword in a volcanic lake — and it's still sharp, roughly 33 centuries later.

The discovery, made at Lake Mezzano, was announced by the Superintendence of Archaeology, Fine Arts and Landscape for the Province of Viterbo and Southern Etruria (SABAP-VT-EM) earlier in October.

Lake Mezzano — once the crater of an ancient volcano — is located in central Italy's Lazio region, near the town of Valentano.

STUDENT 'ACCIDENTALLY' FINDS 'EXTREMELY RARE' CRUSADER-ERA SWORD AFTER CHASING OFF SUSPECTED THIEVES

Archaeologists were excavating a submerged Bronze Age village on the bottom of Lake Mezzano when they recovered the sword.

In a statement, officials said the sword dates back to the 13th century B.C., during a period Italian archaeologists call the Recent Bronze Age — which is roughly equivalent to the Late Bronze Age.

The sword "comes from an area of the southern shore of the lake that had previously seen limited investigation," officials said in a translated statement.

Pictures released by officials show the dark, straight bronze blade resting on the rocky lake floor.

REAL-LIFE EXCALIBUR? MAN ON A HIKE UNCOVERS GOLD SWORD RELIC HIDDEN UNDER TREE

Officials also noted that the sword is so well-preserved that it "still features a sharp edge."

The artifact "represents an important acquisition for understanding the communities that frequented the lake basin more than 3,000 years ago," the translated statement added.

"It is the third sword found at the Mezzano site since the 1970s — a fact of extraordinary interest that confirms the exceptional archaeological importance of the context and offers new elements for exploring how the lake area was frequented and used during the Late Bronze Age," the statement added.

Archaeologists also found axes, arrowheads, pins, spearheads and a razor — objects officials say appear to have been intentionally thrown in as part of a ritual or cultic practice.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"At Mezzano, the proximity between the recovered sword and a bronze razor is of particular interest, as it recalls associations documented in other Bronze Age contexts and attributable to individuals of high social status, likely belonging to warrior elites," the translated statement said.

"Precisely for this reason, each new discovery takes on a value that goes well beyond the single object, contributing to the understanding of symbolic behaviors on the part of protohistoric communities," officials added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Archaeologists noted that the metal artifacts were found at remarkably consistent depths across the lakebed, helping them piece together how the objects ended up in the water.

"Extending underwater stratigraphic excavation activities, integrated with the use of advanced technologies for documenting and spatially analyzing finds, will allow for a deeper understanding of the distribution of artifacts and the formation of the archaeological deposit," the statement added.

Looking ahead, officials plan to continue underwater research at the lake while preparing an upcoming exhibition to display the bronze artifacts.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Mezzano sword is the latest in a string of remarkable weapon discoveries across Europe.

Earlier this summer, archaeologists in the Czech Republic announced the discovery of a Bronze Age hoard of intentionally damaged tools and weapons — including a sword blade struck apart with a single powerful blow.

At around the same time, a metal detectorist in northern Poland discovered a remarkably preserved, 2,700-year-old bronze sword standing upright in the ground.

title: Unexpected Lakers player matches Kobe Bryant mark as Los Angeles pulls out overtime victory
description: Quentin Grimes dropped a career-high 47 points and 10 3-pointers, joining Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers ever to hit 10 threes in a single game.
fullContent:
Kobe Bryant stands alone when it comes to some NBA and franchise records over the course of his storied career. In some people’s minds, he’s considered to be the best basketball player of all-time.

Tuesday night, an unexpected Los Angeles Lakers player forced his way into a club in which Bryant was alone for several years. Quentin Grimes had the game of his life against the Charlotte Hornets as the Lakers outlast their opponent 118-114 in overtime.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Grimes scored 47 points in the win – a career-high. He was 16-of-24 from the field, including 10-of-14 from 3-point range. He is the second Lakers player ever to make 10 3-pointers in a single game since Bryant, who achieved the feat on Jan. 7, 2003.

Grimes scored 21 points in the fourth quarter and made the shot that forced overtime.

"I was like, 'Oh yeah, that's cash,'" Grimes told reporters of the game-tying shot after the game, via ESPN. "I was too open, I was like, 'Yeah, that's cash right there.'"

Grimes played college ball for Kansas and Houston before turning pro in 2021. The Los Angeles Clippers selected him with the No. 25 overall pick of the 2021 draft but he was traded to the New York Knicks before he stepped onto the floor with the Clippers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

He spent about three seasons with the Knicks before he made his way to the Detroit Pistons, Dallas Mavericks and later the Philadelphia 76ers – where he spent the past two seasons. He signed a multi-year contract with the Lakers before the 2026-27 season began.

He’s a career 36.5% 3-point shooter and it showed against the Hornets.

"Q got us back in the game," Luka Doncic said. "I was trying to get him the ball, as he deserved. What an amazing game from him ... it was unbelievable to watch."

Doncic scored 36 in the win as Los Angeles moved to 13-2 on the year.

Charlotte fell to 4-10 with the loss. Brandon Miller led the way with 28 points.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Trump’s grip on GOP faces major post-election test as his hand-picked leader faces challenge from within
description: President Donald Trump is working to save RNC Chair Joe Gruters from a re-election challenge by co-Chair KC Crosbie after GOP midterm election losses.
fullContent:
President Donald Trump's handpicked leader of the Republican National Committee (RNC) is facing a challenge from within his own leadership team after Republicans suffered sweeping losses in the midterm elections that saw even historically deep red seats flip blue in states like Texas, Mississippi and South Carolina.

RNC Chair Joe Gruters, who is seeking a full two-year term running the national party committee, will face-off with co-Chair KC Crosbie of Kentucky after Democrats captured sizable majorities in both the House and Senate and prepare to retake control in January.

Crosbie, a staunch Trump supporter, launched her bid just days after the elections, seeking to capitalize on frustration among Republicans over the party's losses and build support for a change in leadership.

"I hope to speak with each of you before then. I want to hear what you saw in your states, what you think we need to change, and how we can put our Party in a stronger position for the next election," Crosbie wrote in a letter to the 168 RNC committee members, who will vote for the next chair when the party holds its winter meeting in Arizona in mid-January.

FIRST ON FOX: PENCE LEAVES DOOR OPEN TO 2028 WHITE HOUSE RUN

Some party insiders tell Fox News that Gruters is expected to win re-election, thanks to support from President Trump — but others familiar with the mood of the RNC membership said support for Crosbie is growing.

Trump, who installed Gruters as party chair 15 months ago after he urged then-Chair Michael Whatley to run for the Senate in North Carolina, quickly endorsed him in the days after the midterms to earn a full term at the helm.

"Joe Gruters should return as Chairman of the RNC to continue to build our Party, and be a trusted partner as we MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN, and ensure Free and Fair Elections," Trump wrote on social media.

A source confirmed to Fox News Digital that the president has been working behind the scenes to shore up support for Gruters and also confirmed an Axios report that the president threatened retribution against the RNC if the chair isn't re-elected.

WILL TRUMP AVOID MAKING AN ENDORSEMENT IN THE 2028 GOP NOMINATION RACE?

An aide in Gruters' political orbit told Fox News Digital that the chairman is hitting the phones and reaching out to committee members — and the calls are going well. They highlighted how the RNC had historic fundraising over the past year under Gruters' leadership and that he made over 40 campaign stops in 14 states during the midterm election's final stretch while working directly with members and state party chairs on a daily basis.

Fox News Digital has also confirmed an AP report regarding Gruters' letter to RNC members last week, when he defended specific expenditures that have raised concerns among the party membership.

Nevada GOP Chair Michael McDonald told Fox News Digital that "it comes down to this. President Trump has made his choice. He's the leader of our party. This is who they want to go with, and we have to get behind our leaders and regroup."

McDonald praised Gruters for his "personal touch" and said, "KC's a dear friend, so I don't have anything bad to say about her."

But he added, "We have to focus on looking out and not looking in and having internal fights. So I hope everybody comes together on this and gets behind Joe ... we have to move this party forward behind what the president wants."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

In the wake of the ballot box setbacks, no party-led autopsy appears to be in the works. And Crosbie, in her letter to committee members, pointed to the midterms and emphasized "we lost races in places we have long counted on. We owe ourselves an honest account of why."

"Voters were focused on the cost of living and the direction of the country. Our improvements in field operations, voter contact, and election-integrity infrastructure were valuable, but they did not answer those concerns or deliver the results we needed," she emphasized. "Some voters who supported us in 2024 stayed home or voted differently in 2026. We must ask whether we addressed the issues that mattered most to them, gave our candidates the support they needed, and nominated candidates who could win the races before them."

RNC member Oscar Brock of Tennessee, who is supporting Crosbie’s candidacy, told Fox News Digital "the goal of the national party is to elect Republicans and that’s true across the country."

"While we have traditionally deferred to the president to suggest who should be the national committee chairman, in this case we would hope the president would change his mind, because those of us who are supporting KC Crosbie for national chairman see Joe as having failed to do a successful job," Brock said.

Sue Cienki, an RNC committee member from Rhode Island, said KC is a member's member. She's done a great outreach the past couple of years" and added, "I don't think the members know Joe as well as they know KC.

We had a devastating loss on Election Day and I think people are looking for some sort of change," Cienki added. "It's not, in any way, shape or form, an insult to the president. I think that we're all in the 168 supportive of his policies, and we want to make sure the next two years go as smoothly for him as possible. But we are a separate entity from the White House."

But Gruters supporters highlighted his fundraising and organizational efforts.

RNC committee member from Maine Lauren LePage told Fox News Gruters was "incredibly responsive this cycle...he’s raised a ton of money for the party and supported candidates up and down the ballot ... although we suffered some losses, Chairman Gruters certainly did his job."

LePage, whose father, former two-term Maine Gov. Paul LePage, captured a Democrat-controlled open congressional seat in a rare midterm flip for the GOP, said that the RNC "made enormous investments in the ground game in Maine that resulted in a victory in CD 2."

In neighboring New Hampshire, RNC committee member Bill O'Brien pointed to Gruters and Crosbie and said, "I think there are two good candidates. I like them both."

But O'Brien, a former state House speaker, said, "2028 starts now, and Joe Gruters is the leader we need at the RNC to win."

"We need to build our war chest, strengthen our state parties, and protect the ballot. I’m proud to support Joe’s reelection as RNC chairman," O'Brien added. "We need proven leadership so we can fire on all cylinders and stay in the fight."

Another RNC committee member, who asked to remain anonymous to speak more freely, said "I’m with Joe. Nobody’s happy with the election, but it’s nothing against Joe. It’s nothing Joe could control."

"When your party has the White House, with all due respect to the chair, the RNC is an arm of the White House and so if people have a beef or a grievance, it’s with the White House, not with Joe. And so I think it would be unfair to hold Joe accountable," the committee member emphasized.

Since Trump's first election to the White House a decade ago, the RNC has experienced significant membership turnover, with those coming on board seen as loyal supporters of the president.

Former longtime RNC committee member from Mississippi Henry Barbour, who left the committee two years ago after serving for nearly two decades, told Fox News Digital, "Historically, anytime the White House has a candidate for RNC chair, they win, and I expect that Gruters will win."

"But I do think we need to have a discussion about the future of the party and what’s at stake and how do we get back on a winning path," Barbour added. "The only job of a political party is to win elections. That’s the number one job, and we’re failing at it."

title: Cathie Wood’s ARK Sells $85 Million In Nvidia While Buying $40 Million In Crypto Stocks — What’s Behind The Shift?
description: Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest has made a striking portfolio adjustment, selling approximately $84.8 million in Nvidia shares while purchasing nearly $40 million in cryptocurrency-related stocks. The transactions come as Bitcoin ETFs face renewed market pressure, raising an important question: are institutional investors beginning to identify opportunities in crypto-related businesses despite the broader market downturn? According […]
fullContent:
Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest has made a striking portfolio adjustment, selling approximately $84.8 million in Nvidia shares while purchasing nearly $40 million in cryptocurrency-related stocks. The transactions come as Bitcoin ETFs face renewed market pressure, raising an important question: are institutional investors beginning to identify opportunities in crypto-related businesses despite the broader market downturn?

According to ARK’s November 16 trading disclosures, the investment firm sold 543,092 Nvidia shares across its ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) and ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW).

Using Nvidia’s closing share price of $156.14, the transaction was valued at approximately $84.8 million. The actual proceeds could differ because the trade disclosures report share quantities rather than execution prices.

Meanwhile, ARK increased its exposure to several companies operating within the cryptocurrency and digital payments industries.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Makes A $40 Million Crypto Stock Bet

ARK’s purchases included 277,523 shares of Block, the financial technology company associated with Jack Dorsey and Bitcoin-focused payment products.

Those shares represented an estimated $23 million investment, making Block the largest crypto-related equity purchase disclosed for the session.

The firm also acquired 180,534 shares of stablecoin issuer Circle, worth approximately $10.4 million, alongside 53,760 shares of Coinbase, valued at around $6.4 million.

Combined, the purchases totaled approximately $39.9 million.

Interestingly, all three companies experienced share-price declines during the trading session. Block fell 1.92%, Circle declined 7.29%, and Coinbase dropped 6.11%.

Rather than waiting for prices to recover, ARK increased selected positions while market sentiment remained weak.

However, these transactions involved publicly traded companies, not direct purchases of Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies.

Why Did ARK Sell Nvidia While Buying Crypto Companies?

The timing is particularly interesting because Nvidia has become one of the most recognizable companies associated with artificial intelligence infrastructure.

ARK’s decision to reduce its Nvidia exposure while increasing selected cryptocurrency-related positions may suggest an effort to rebalance exposure across different technology sectors.

However, interpreting the move as a complete departure from artificial intelligence would be misleading.

ARK had purchased additional Nvidia shares earlier in November and continued to maintain a substantial position after the latest sale.

The investment manager also acquired approximately $52 million worth of SpaceX shares during the same trading session.

Furthermore, ARK reduced its holdings in Bullish and sold units of Ethereum and Solana staking exchange-traded funds.

These transactions suggest a more selective investment approach rather than an unrestricted shift into cryptocurrency assets.

ARK’s own research provides another perspective. In its November 17 newsletter, the firm described Block as an AI company, highlighting the increasingly blurred boundaries between financial technology and artificial intelligence.

What Could This Mean For Bitcoin And Institutional Adoption?

Although ARK’s purchases do not represent direct Bitcoin demand, they demonstrate continued institutional interest in businesses connected to digital assets.

Block’s involvement in Bitcoin payments, Circle’s stablecoin infrastructure, and the expansion of regulated cryptocurrency investment products all contribute to the broader digital asset economy.

This comes as BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF activity continues to attract attention from institutional investors.

The distinction between investing in cryptocurrency directly and purchasing shares in companies supporting the industry remains important.

A crypto-related stock may respond to company earnings, regulation, equity-market conditions, and investor sentiment differently from Bitcoin itself.

Nevertheless, investment in financial infrastructure could support the industry’s long-term development by expanding payment services, custody capabilities, and access to digital assets.

ARK’s activity also arrives amid evidence of increasing interest from traditional financial institutions, including Wells Fargo’s reported Bitcoin ETF exposure.

Is Cathie Wood Positioning For A Crypto Recovery?

ARK’s latest transactions are noteworthy, but a single trading session cannot establish a lasting change in investment strategy.

The firm regularly adjusts portfolio allocations, and its daily trade disclosures do not establish whether proceeds from specific sales funded particular purchases.

What the numbers do demonstrate is that ARK was willing to increase selected crypto-related equity positions during a period of market weakness.

For Bitcoin investors, the development offers an interesting perspective on institutional positioning. Even when cryptocurrency prices experience significant volatility, investment firms may continue identifying opportunities in the businesses supporting digital asset adoption.

The next important signal will be whether ARK maintains or expands these positions in subsequent trading disclosures.

For now, the November 16 transactions suggest that Cathie Wood’s firm remains engaged with cryptocurrency infrastructure, even as it adjusts exposure across the broader technology sector.

description:

Now, investors want to know whether the correction has run its course, and what 2027 could bring. Why Gold Fell to a 14-Month Low Gold is a precious metal
The post Gold Falls to a 14-Month Low Near $3,760. Will 2027 Finally Bring a Recovery? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Gold fell to its lowest level in 14 months on November 18, trading near $3,770 per ounce. The metal briefly plunged to $3,660 before partially recovering.

Now, investors want to know whether the correction has run its course, and what 2027 could bring.

Why Gold Fell to a 14-Month Low

Gold is a precious metal that investors often treat as a safe haven. However, it pays no interest, so it becomes less attractive when yields rise.

That dynamic explains much of the current slide. Gold hit its lowest level since September 2025 amid a firm dollar and rising rate expectations. It now trades roughly 32% below its early-2026 peak near $5,600.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

As a result, the metal is on track for its weakest annual performance since 2015. US Treasury yields have climbed above 5%, which raises the cost of holding non-yielding assets.

Moreover, traders see another Federal Reserve rate hike in December as nearly certain. As Bloomberg noted, persistent inflation pressure keeps that outlook in place. The selloff also reflects profit-taking after gold’s record run earlier this year.

Meanwhile, central banks and some ETFs have kept buying. Still, elevated real yields and the broader rates environment continue to dominate short-term price action.

Will Gold Recover in 2027?

Many banks think so, although they have trimmed their near-term targets. Goldman Sachs recently cut its end-2026 forecast to $4,150.

The bank also lowered its end-2027 projection to roughly $4,650 to $4,800. Even so, it expects central banks to keep buying about 60 tonnes per month.

According to Goldman, gold could gain more strongly once the Fed pivots to rate cuts later in 2027. Lower rates would reduce the opportunity cost of holding the metal. In addition, a weaker dollar could revive demand from overseas buyers.

Other institutions see even higher prices. UBS targets $5,000 to $5,400 by mid-to-late 2027. Bank of America projects an average of $4,800 to $5,000 next year, while CIBC sees about $5,200.

Both banks cite structural demand and possible renewed de-dollarization concerns. Separately, a Reuters poll puts the median 2027 forecast at $4,650.

“We expect prices to consolidate and recover in the coming months,” said Standard Chartered’s Suki Cooper, cited by Reuters.

For now, volatility remains high. The quick rebound from $3,660 shows that buyers still step in at lower levels. Whether that support holds could decide gold’s next move.

The post Ransomware Gang Claims Visa and JPMorgan Chase as Victims, Sets 48-Hour Leak Deadline appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
A newly emerged ransomware gang has listed Visa and JPMorgan Chase as alleged victims and threatens to leak stolen data within 48 hours.

The gang, which goes by the name n0n, has given the two companies 48 hours to negotiate, reports Cybernews.

Visa says it is aware of the claims and that the incident involved a third-party service provider in the Asia Pacific region.

Says a Visa spokesperson,

“Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. There is no indication that payment data such as card numbers have been affected.”

Visa has not said which third-party service providers were hit.

Meanwhile, JPMorgan Chase is separately dealing with a service outage that it blames on a software bug.

The bank says there is “no evidence” linking the disruption to a cyberattack.

The bank has not said whether the outage has any connection to the gang’s claims.

The n0n gang was first tracked in mid-September.

The gang claimed last week that it stole billions of traveler records from Expedia.

The attackers have offered few details about what they claim to have stolen from Visa and JPMorgan Chase.

The Daily HODL previously reported that JPMorgan Chase and other major US banks suffered a major outage that involved login failures and missing account balances.

title: XMR Gets a Clean Audit From zkSecurity as Monero Eyes 150M-Strong Anonymity Sets
description: Monero's bulletproofs code passed a zkSecurity audit with no serious flaws. XMR trades near $505, below its 50-day average, with the 200-day line as key support.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Monero's generalized bulletproofs code passed a zkSecurity audit with no high- or medium-severity findings.
  • XMR trades below its 50-day average while sellers still control momentum.
  • The 200-day average now serves as the line between a correction and a broken trend.

Monero's privacy upgrade cleared a key test this month. An outside review of the cryptography behind Full-Chain Membership Proofs found no serious flaws, and the team backed it with formal math proofs.

The market has shrugged so far. XMR kept sliding through the week, and sellers still set the pace. Traders want to know whether a stronger protocol can pull buyers back before the longer-term trend gives way.

zkSecurity Finds No Serious Flaws in Monero's Generalized Bulletproofs

Security firm zkSecurity found no high- or medium-severity flaws in Monero's generalized bulletproofs code. The firm reviewed the generalized-bulletproofs crate in monero-oxide, the project's Rust cryptography library, over ten working days. It flagged 4 low-severity issues and 3 informational items. Monero-oxide developers answered all seven.

MAGIC Grants, which contracted zkSecurity in June, announced the result on Nov. 12. Monero confirmed it on Nov. 18. Researchers Mathias Hall-Andersen and Suneal Gong led the review.

The work went beyond a standard code check. The team wrote a new proof of knowledge soundness and formalized the protocol in the Lean theorem prover. That process verified completeness, zero-knowledge and soundness, and the proofs sit publicly on GitHub.

This clears a major hurdle for FCMP++, or Full-Chain Membership Proofs. The upgrade would replace ring signatures and could widen anonymity sets to about 150 million outputs.

Several steps remain. MAGIC Grants announced a Trail of Bits review in August. The Community Crowdfunding System set aside 500 XMR for an integration audit, and a developer requested 45 XMR in October for three months of work. A second beta stressnet has run since May 6, starting at block 2,997,100.

Good News Meets a Price Stuck Under Its 50-Day Line

Monero (XMR) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Monero traded near $505 on Tuesday, little changed over the past 24 hours. The audit news landed during a slide, and the price has yet to respond to it.

XMR lost about 10% over the past seven days. Over 30 days the drop is closer to 16%. A clean security review lowers long-term risk for the network, but traders have kept selling anyway.

The moving averages show where the coin stands. A moving average smooths daily prices into one line, and traders use it to judge the trend. XMR now sits below its 50-day average near $557. That line tracks the medium-term trend, and the price falling under it means recent buyers are mostly sitting on losses. The 50-day level now acts as a ceiling that sellers can lean on.

Over a longer horizon, XMR looks healthier. XMR still holds above its 200-day average, around $474. That average measures the trend over most of a year, so the broader uptrend remains intact for now. The coin is caught between a weakening medium trend and a long trend that has not broken.

Tuesday's quiet session matters too. A flat day after a weekly loss suggests sellers are taking a break. It does not show buyers taking control. A real turn would need XMR to climb back toward the 50-day line.

Sellers Still Steer the Momentum

Momentum gauges tell the same story as the averages. RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits at 38 on the daily chart. That reading is weak. It still sits above the oversold zone below 30, where selling often runs out of steam. XMR has room to slide further before buyers would see it as stretched.

The MACD adds to that view. It remains below its signal line, which means momentum is still pointing down. A separate trend-strength reading confirms a real trend, and sellers are the ones driving it.

Together, these signals set a high bar for any recovery. Traders would want to see momentum turn up and hold for several sessions before calling a bottom. Until then, short rallies look more like pauses inside a downtrend.

Why $535 Matters More Than the Distant Floor

Resistance sits close by, near $535. That level caps the first leg of any bounce. A daily close above it would put the 50-day line back in play as the next test. Clearing both would mark the first real sign that buyers are returning.

The support picture looks very different. The nearest listed floors sit far below the market, around $169 and then $145. Levels that distant offer little guidance for traders watching daily moves.

That leaves the 200-day average as the working cushion. It has held so far. A decisive drop through it would remove the last nearby support. That would open space toward the much lower floors.

Two Paths for the Next Three Days

Two setups stand out, and each hinges on a level already flagged above.

  • Bullish: A daily close above that nearby resistance would open the way toward the 50-day line. Momentum would need to turn up to support the move. The setup fails if XMR slips back under Tuesday's trading price.
  • Bearish: A clean break below the 200-day average would signal deeper losses, with little support close underneath. This view fails if buyers push XMR back above that nearby resistance.

A Stronger Protocol Still Waiting for Buyers

The audit gives Monero's privacy roadmap a stronger footing. Formal proofs and zero serious findings make FCMP++ look more credible to long-term holders. The price still argues for patience until XMR clears resistance.

Risks remain on both fronts. Further audits stand between the code and a release date, so FCMP++ timing is still open.

title: Singapore Opens Agentic Money Sandbox for AI Digital Payments
description:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Future of Finance Institute (FFI) outlined an Agentic Money Sandbox on November 18, 2026, at the Singapore FinTech Festival. The testbed lets banks try AI agents that start digital-money payments and treasury moves. Agents must stay inside set authority, limits, and safeguards before any live rollout. The […]
The post Singapore Opens Agentic Money Sandbox for AI Digital Payments appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Future of Finance Institute (FFI) outlined an Agentic Money Sandbox on November 18, 2026, at the Singapore FinTech Festival. The testbed lets banks try AI agents that start digital-money payments and treasury moves. Agents must stay inside set authority, limits, and safeguards before any live rollout.

The joint MAS and FFI release ties the sandbox to Singapore’s National AI Missions for financial services. Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, who chairs MAS, named the third mission as enabling safe agentic transactions. In his SFF 2026 keynote, he said greater autonomy for agents must come with clear responsibility. Agents work inside set authority and limits. Institutions and enterprises stay accountable for actions taken on their behalf.

What the Agentic Money Sandbox Is Testing

FFI will run the sandbox as a shared lab, not a public retail product. Banks can build and exercise the controls AI agents need to move digital money safely. The release names early use cases as agent-initiated payments and treasury management across participating banks.

The stake is practical. An AI agent can pay a supplier, sweep idle cash, or settle an invoice without a human click on every step. That only helps if the bank can prove who authorized the agent, what it could spend, and who owns the loss if it misfires. The sandbox is where those proofs get stress-tested before live books take the hit.

MAS and FFI also named FFI’s bank launch partners at SFF 2026: DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered, and UOB. Those banks sit with technology and research partners on the broader National AI Missions programme, not only on the money sandbox.

How Purpose-Bound Limits Are Meant to Constrain Agents

Gan’s keynote put one concrete control path on the table: purpose bound money. In that framing, conditions ride with the funds. An agent can move money only when preset rules are met. His examples are blunt. An agent could pay a contract once the terms have been checked. Or it could finish a purchase for a user inside limits already written into the money.

That is the mechanism in plain order. First the money carries a purpose, a cap, and a permission set. Then the agent checks whether those conditions hold. Then the payment fires. The trials must also examine identity, authority, accountability, and interoperability before wider use.

For AI and blockchain readers, the interesting split is not “AI decides” versus “a human clicks.” It is whether programmable limits on digital money can make an autonomous payment look more like a constrained instruction than an open wallet. Purpose-bound rails are the candidate answer MAS is willing to test. They are not a claim that every Singapore bank deposit is already programmable that way.

Why a Sandbox Matters Before Live Agentic Payments

Agent-led payments change the failure mode. A mistaken human transfer is usually one bad click. A mistaken agent can repeat a bad rule at machine speed across banks. Gan’s speech frames the upside as faster cash management and machine-led commerce. The same speech refuses to detach that upside from accountability under financial regulation.

The sandbox therefore has a dual job. It asks what value agents can create in payments and treasury. It also asks which safeguards must exist before those agents leave the lab. Banks need shared ways to prove identity, grant authority, assign accountability, and work across institutions.

Xinhua independently reported the same Wednesday package. FFI is establishing the Agentic Money Sandbox so banks can test AI agents that conduct digital-money transactions inside defined limits and safeguards. The wire matches the MAS fact pattern. It does not add a go-live date or production volumes.

What Is Demonstrated, and Where the Catch Sits

What the primary record shows today is a named testbed and a policy frame. MAS and FFI announced the Agentic Money Sandbox. Initial cases are agent payments and treasury management. Purpose bound money is an explicit trial area in the chairman’s keynote. Four large banks are listed as FFI launch partners. The sandbox’s stated job is to test controls before live deployment.

What remains unproven is harder and more important. The release does not publish a start date for live agent traffic. It also skips a schedule of which payment rails will sit under the sandbox, and it shows no results from completed agent payment drills. Embedding conditions into money can constrain an agent’s spending. It does not prove the agent’s judgment about a contract, an invoice, or a treasury move was correct. Verification of permission is not verification of good decisions.

The mental model to keep is simple. Singapore is not declaring that AI agents already run the country’s digital payments. It is building a controlled room where banks practice letting agents move digital money under purpose-bound limits, identity checks, and clear accountability. Only then will they decide what is safe to take live.

The post Singapore Opens Agentic Money Sandbox for AI Digital Payments appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.

title: Donald Trump Just Found a New Way to Challenge China's AI Ambitions
description:
The Trump administration weighs forcing US companies to disclose Chinese AI use. See who is exposed before the Xi summit.
The post Donald Trump Just Found a New Way to Challenge China's AI Ambitions appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Ask Airbnb’s customer service bot a question, and a Chinese AI model writes the answer. The Trump administration may soon make companies like Airbnb admit that on their own websites, three people told Reuters.

It would not be a ban. The goal is to discourage Chinese AI without new rules that anger industry or Beijing. For shareholders, a public label means fresh scrutiny.

Why Are American Companies Choosing Chinese AI?

It costs less. Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2.5 charges about a quarter of what OpenAI’s GPT-5.2 does per token. Yet both score the same on one independent benchmark.

So says a March paper from the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC), a congressional advisory panel. It cites an Andreessen Horowitz partner who estimated that 80% of US startups build on Chinese models.

“China has opted to go all in on an open-source approach to AI,” an excerpt in the paper reads.

Open-source means anyone can download and adapt the model for free. In October, Chinese models were the three most used on OpenRouter, a marketplace where developers buy AI access.

Airbnb runs Alibaba’s Qwen, Reuters reported. A DoorDash co-founder said the delivery app sends some internal tasks through Kimi.

What Happens to a Stock When Washington Points at China?

Webull found out in October. Its stock fell 19% after a House panel tied the trading app to China.

Republican Representatives Andrew Garbarino and John Moolenaar have already sent letters to Airbnb and DoorDash over their Chinese AI use.

On the other side sits Alibaba. It expects selling AI models to become its biggest cloud business, and it just released a cheaper Qwen4 Max.

Still, nothing is final. Treasury and White House officials have discussed the plan, but it may never become a rule. Airbnb declined to comment to Reuters.

The Plan Lands a Day Before Trump Meets Xi

On Wednesday, the USCC’s annual report named China’s open AI models and Taiwan among its top worries, Barron’s reported.

On Thursday, Xi hosts Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. Alibaba reports earnings the same day.

Days ago, Washington closed China’s chip loophole. This plan would go after the AI models instead.

The post Donald Trump Just Found a New Way to Challenge China's AI Ambitions appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Important Binance Announcement Concerning Turkish Users: Details Inside
description: The delisting is scheduled for November 20.
fullContent:
The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange conducted its first review of all listed spot trading pairs after the record $6.3 billion hack it suffered toward the end of October.

As a result, it decided to delist five pairs, the majority of which are primarily associated with Turkish clients.

Goodbye to These Ones

Binance revealed that the spot trading pairs GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY, and ZAMA/TRY will no longer be available from November 20. Trading bot services for the aforementioned pairs will also be discontinued, and the exchange advised users to update and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots before the delisting to avoid potential losses.

“The delisting of a spot trading pair does not affect the availability of the tokens on Binance Spot. Users can still trade the spot trading pair’s base and quote assets on other trading pair(s) that are available on Binance,” the company clarified.

What stands out is that four of the five pairs set to be removed are based on the Turkish lira. Turkey is one of the world’s biggest and most active crypto markets and an important user base for Binance.

The assets included in the delisting effort did not suffer any significant price turbulence. Usually, major declines occur when the company terminates all services for a certain cryptocurrency, not just trading pairs. Such was the case in mid-October when Binance said goodbye to Epic Chain (EPIC) and QuickSwap (QUICK), triggering double-digit drops.

The Hack and the Latest Updates

Binance made the headlines in the last week of October after becoming a victim of a whopping $6.3 billion hack. This turned out to be the biggest cybersecurity incident in the history of the cryptocurrency industry.

The company reacted swiftly, temporarily halting deposits and withdrawals, and promised to fully reimburse affected users. Several agencies, including the FBI, pointed to the North Korean hacking collective “TraderTraitor” as the attacker.

Binance began restoring withdrawals in early November, and the first phase included popular networks such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, XRP, Dogecoin, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, and Sui. A few days ago, the exchange said it had reinstated withdrawals for 87 networks and pledged to reopen the rest by the end of this week.

The company also completed coverage of assets impacted by the security incident and promised to publish a new Proof of Reserves snapshot where users can verify that their funds are backed at a minimum 1:1.

Meanwhile, the hackers have used various tricks to launder the stolen crypto, such as creating fake meme coins. Just a few hours ago, Lookonchain reported that the wrongdoers began laundering the 602,402 ETH they hold by swapping it for BTC via THORChain.

title: Can Decentralized Derivatives Exchanges Operate Within U.S. Regulatory Frameworks?
description: As real-world assets move on-chain, decentralized trading platforms are exploring how to combine blockchain-based settlement with the compliance requirements of traditional financial markets.
fullContent:
As real-world assets move on-chain, decentralized trading platforms are exploring how to combine blockchain-based settlement with the compliance requirements of traditional financial markets.

Decentralized finance was built around the idea that anyone with a crypto wallet could access financial markets without relying on traditional intermediaries. But as blockchain platforms expand into derivatives tied to equities, commodities, and other real-world assets, that model faces a more complicated regulatory environment.

In the United States, derivatives markets are subject to requirements involving trading venues, clearing, customer protection, and market oversight. For decentralized exchanges, the challenge is determining how these obligations apply when trading infrastructure operates through smart contracts rather than conventional financial intermediaries.

The question is becoming increasingly relevant as developers look beyond cryptocurrency derivatives and toward financial instruments linked to traditional markets.

Where Decentralization Meets Regulation

A decentralized exchange can make transactions transparent and reduce reliance on centralized infrastructure, but those characteristics do not automatically remove regulatory obligations.

In particular, derivatives platforms must consider who can access their markets, how positions are managed, and which entities may be responsible for operating or facilitating trading.

This creates a tension between permissionless access and the eligibility requirements commonly associated with regulated financial products.

One potential approach involves separating decentralized transaction processing from participant eligibility. Under this model, blockchain infrastructure can support execution and settlement while identity-based controls determine whether a participant is permitted to access particular markets.

However, technical restrictions alone do not establish regulatory compliance. Depending on the products and activities involved, additional registration, operational, and supervisory requirements may still apply.

DeepSigma's Approach to On-Chain Derivatives

DeepSigma, a company developing a decentralized perpetual futures exchange for real-world assets, is exploring this approach through an architecture designed to incorporate participant eligibility controls and auditable on-chain settlement.

Its public demonstration platform currently supports paper trading across 77 perpetual markets linked to equities, commodities, indices, and other traditional financial assets.

The planned infrastructure combines a central limit order book with a clearing layer responsible for managing positions, collateral, margin, and settlement.

Built on the Cypherium blockchain, the platform is also being developed with decentralized identity-based permissioning intended to support participant verification and jurisdiction-specific restrictions.

The objective is to retain elements of decentralized trading infrastructure while introducing controls that may be necessary when dealing with regulated financial instruments.

These capabilities remain part of the platform's development roadmap, rather than evidence of regulatory authorization to operate a live derivatives exchange.

A $10 Million Offering Highlights the Next Development Phase

The regulatory question has gained additional relevance following DeepSigma's November 10 announcement of a token offering on Republic targeting up to $10 million.

The offering is structured under Regulation D Rule 506(c) for verified accredited investors in the United States and Regulation S for eligible investors in offshore transactions.

According to the company, the proceeds are intended to support the development of its matching engine, integration with Cypherium, identity-based eligibility infrastructure, and independent security audits.

Importantly, the regulatory framework governing the token offering is separate from the requirements that may apply to operating a derivatives exchange.

Conducting a securities offering under Regulation D or Regulation S does not constitute authorization from the Securities and Exchange Commission or Commodity Futures Trading Commission to provide derivatives trading services.

DeepSigma remains in its demonstration phase, with live trading dependent on further technical development and applicable regulatory requirements.

On-chain exchanges went from 2% to 10% of perpetuals volume in two years. By early July 2026, roughly $31 billion in real-world assets had been tokenized. Traders are getting comfortable with on-chain exchanges as traditional assets move on-chain. DeepSigma brings 77 markets across U.S. stocks, indexes, sector ETFs, commodities, and Treasuries on-chain. If you already trade BTC perps, you know how to get started. Next time you're looking at Nvidia, gold, or the S&P 500, you can trade that market directly from the same terminal.

— DeepSigmaDEX (@deepsigmadex) November 17, 2026

 

 

Can On-Chain Settlement Work Within Traditional Market Rules?

Beyond participant eligibility, decentralized derivatives platforms face technical challenges that are less common in cryptocurrency-only markets.

Traditional assets follow different trading schedules, rely on external pricing sources, and can experience periods of limited liquidity. These characteristics complicate the management of perpetual contracts, particularly when trading is intended to operate continuously.

For platforms developing real-world asset derivatives, reliable pricing, collateral management, liquidation mechanisms, and settlement records become essential components of the infrastructure.

Blockchain-based settlement may improve transaction traceability and make certain market activities easier to audit. However, transparent records do not independently satisfy regulatory obligations involving clearing, market surveillance, or customer protection.

The broader challenge is therefore not simply moving derivatives onto a blockchain, but determining which parts of traditional financial market infrastructure can be automated and which still require regulatory oversight.

The Next Phase of Decentralized Derivatives

As the market for tokenized financial assets develops, decentralized derivatives platforms may increasingly move toward models that combine on-chain infrastructure with identity verification and market-specific access controls.

DeepSigma's development illustrates one possible direction, although its proposed architecture has yet to demonstrate how these mechanisms will operate in a live trading environment.

The long-term question is whether decentralized platforms can preserve the transparency and efficiency associated with blockchain technology while meeting the legal and operational standards expected of financial markets.

For developers entering the real-world asset derivatives sector, regulatory compatibility may become as important as trading performance itself.

description:

The post The Economist’s 2027 Warning: What It Means for Bitcoin? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
The Economist expects 2027 to be a year of strain. Its annual outlook, The World Ahead 2027, warns that “something, somewhere, will have to give.”

With debt, AI spending, and geopolitics all under pressure, Bitcoin’s fixed supply could face its biggest test yet.

What The Economist Predicts for 2027

The World Ahead is The Economist’s yearly forecast of the trends likely to shape the coming year. Deputy editor Tom Standage edits the edition.

According to the official release, the post-Trump era is beginning. After the Democrats’ midterm wins, Standage expects Trump to become “even more aggressive and mercurial.”

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

Debt is another major concern. IMF data shows that average 10-year G7 bond yields rose more than 110 basis points between February and September. That pushed them to their highest level in nearly two decades.

Meanwhile, France’s finance ministry expects public debt to reach about 122% of GDP in 2027. A Marine Le Pen victory could also unsettle investors.

AI financing adds further risk. Goldman Sachs expects cloud giants to issue $420 billion in debt in 2027, up about 60% from this year. The Economist warns that opaque financing structures raise the danger of a crash.

In addition, the World Bank expects food commodity prices to rise 7% next year amid the Middle East conflict. The magazine also flags Taiwan as a flashpoint.

Former CIA Director William Burns has said that Xi Jinping instructed his military to be ready to invade by 2027. Still, US intelligence sees no current invasion plan.

Could Bitcoin Benefit if Something Gives?

The Economist’s warnings arrive at a fragile moment for Bitcoin. According to BeInCrypto data, Bitcoin trades near $64,600, down about 25% so far in 2026. It also sits roughly 49% below its $126,080 all-time high from October 2025.

Still, those warnings could cut both ways. Over the long run, Bitcoin’s fixed supply of 21 million coins stands out, since no central bank can print more.

That feature gains weight as public debt keeps climbing. If governments fund deficits by creating money, fiat currencies would lose purchasing power. In that case, scarce assets like Bitcoin could look far more compelling.

Bank stress offers another angle. When Paraguay began a resolution process against Ueno Bank, Bitcoin traded at a 1.7% local premium. Self-custody means its holders do not depend on any bank’s solvency.

However, the short-term picture looks less friendly. Bitcoin fell alongside AI stocks this month, as Grayscale noted. A broader AI correction could therefore drag it lower first.

Persistent inflation could also keep interest rates high, which tends to weigh on risk assets. Similarly, a geopolitical shock would likely spark an initial risk-off reaction.

Politics adds further uncertainty. The strategic Bitcoin reserve and the GENIUS Act boosted crypto. Yet a hostile Congress and the post-Trump race could slow that agenda.

title: Standard Chartered Sees LINK at $200 by 2030, but Chainlink First Has to Hold $7
description: Standard Chartered sees Chainlink's LINK at $200 by 2030 on tokenized asset growth. The chart still favors sellers, with support near $7.83 and $7 in focus.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Standard Chartered says LINK could reach $200 by 2030 on the back of tokenized asset growth.
  • The chart still favors sellers, with LINK stuck below both of its key moving averages.
  • Traders are watching whether the token can hold the $7 area if nearer support gives way.

Standard Chartered has set a long-range target for Chainlink's LINK, betting that tokenized assets will drive demand for its cross-chain services. The call lands while the token sits deep in a monthlong slide.

Bank pilots keep coming, yet they have not turned into fees for token holders. Spot ETF investors have started pulling money, too. Traders now face a simple question: can buyers defend the lows long enough for adoption to catch up?

A $200 Call Arrives as Partnerships Stay on Testnet

Standard Chartered expects Chainlink's LINK token to reach $200 by the end of 2030. That would mean a gain of nearly 22x from today's level. The bank ties the call to tokenized assets growing to $4 trillion by the end of 2028. Chainlink sells the plumbing that moves data and value between blockchains, so more tokenized assets could mean more demand for its services.

Big names are already testing that plumbing. Moody's launched a credit-data pilot on Nov 10 that uses Chainlink's CCIP to send ratings across networks, though it runs on testnet only. Korean broker Hanwha Investment & Securities integrated CCIP for its tokenization platform on Oct 29. None of this generates fees for the token yet.

ETF investors have grown impatient. Cumulative net inflows into the spot funds GLNK and CLNK slipped to $174.4 million by Nov 16. That followed four straight days of outflows. Total net assets fell about 30%, to $157.5 million. LINK now sits 82.7% below its $52.70 record.

Both Key Averages Now Sit Overhead

Chainlink (LINK) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

LINK traded near $9.14 on Tuesday, down about 2% over the past day. The token has lost roughly 24% in a month. That slide leaves the chart in a weak spot.

The drop has been steady. LINK changed hands near $12 on Oct 21. It fell below $9 by mid-November. That move set the range traders now watch, with the October high as the ceiling and the mid-November lows as the floor.

A moving average smooths out daily prices over a set number of days, so it shows the general direction. The 50-day average tracks the recent trend and sits near $11.08. The 200-day average tracks the longer trend and sits near $10.88.

LINK trades below both lines. Analysts read that as a bearish setup, because each average now acts as a ceiling that sellers can defend. Rallies toward those levels tend to meet supply from holders looking to exit near their entry price.

The 50-day average also sits above the 200-day. That gap shows how fast the recent selling erased gains from earlier months.

A daily close back above the 200-day line would be the first sign of repair. That would tell traders that buyers have taken back the longer trend. Until then, any bounce looks like a pause inside a downtrend.

Sellers Still Hold the Momentum Edge

Momentum readings back up what the averages show. RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 33. That reading is weak, though it has not yet reached the oversold zone below 30. In plain terms, sellers still have room to push before the market looks stretched.

LINK dropped about 11% over the past week, and buyers have not stepped in with any force.

MACD, a tool that compares short and longer price trends, stays below its signal line. That means momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings also confirm a real trend, and sellers are the ones leading it.

$7.83 Is the Last Floor Before $7

Support sits near $7.83, with no mapped level below it. A clean break there would leave the $7 area from the headline as the next real test. Losing that area would push the bank's target further out of reach.

Buyers have a shorter list of hurdles on the upside. The first resistance sits near $10.27, where recent bounces have stalled. Above that, the next ceiling stands near $10.91, almost on top of the 200-day line.

A rally would have to clear two sell zones packed close together. Until LINK closes above both, sellers keep control of the range between these levels.

Where the Next Three Days Could Lead

Two paths stand out for the coming sessions, and each depends on one level breaking first.

  • Bullish: A daily close above first resistance would open the way to the next ceiling, the one sitting almost on the 200-day line. That would hint that buyers are starting to absorb supply. The setup fails if LINK slips below its current support.
  • Bearish: Losing that support would put the headline floor in play as the next target. Sellers would then be pressing toward lows not seen in this slide. A move back above first resistance would cancel this view.

Adoption Needs a Floor to Stand On

The bank's tokenization thesis still holds on paper, and the pilots show real interest. The chart tells a harder story. Sellers keep the edge until LINK reclaims the nearest resistance and the 200-day line.

Spot funds remain the main risk. Another run of ETF outflows could add supply and speed a break of support.
