title: Michael Saylor Says Banks Are Bringing Bitcoin To Clients — But Who Really Owns The $2.35 Billion?
description: Michael Saylor has drawn attention to a remarkable shift in Wall Street’s relationship with Bitcoin, highlighting how Wells Fargo’s brokerage businesses more than doubled their holdings of BlackRock’s Bitcoin exchange-traded fund during the third quarter. But behind the impressive numbers lies an even more interesting question: who is actually accumulating Bitcoin exposure? The comments arrive […]
fullContent:
Michael Saylor has drawn attention to a remarkable shift in Wall Street’s relationship with Bitcoin, highlighting how Wells Fargo’s brokerage businesses more than doubled their holdings of BlackRock’s Bitcoin exchange-traded fund during the third quarter. But behind the impressive numbers lies an even more interesting question: who is actually accumulating Bitcoin exposure?

The comments arrive shortly after Bitcoinist reported that Wells Fargo and its associated investment businesses disclosed approximately $2.35 billion in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) shares.

While the headline figure suggests substantial institutional participation, the underlying regulatory filing reveals a more nuanced development that could be particularly important for Bitcoin’s long-term adoption.

Rather than representing a single corporate investment, much of the reported exposure is associated with brokerage and wealth-management operations.

Michael Saylor Highlights A Major Shift In Bitcoin Ownership

Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor recently took to X to highlight the growing role of traditional banks in connecting customers with Bitcoin.

Saylor pointed out that two Wells Fargo brokerage businesses reported approximately 42 million shares of BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of September, compared with roughly 20 million shares at the end of June.

The increase represents approximately 110% growth in reported shares over three months.

The figures are particularly interesting because the two brokerage businesses account for the majority of Wells Fargo’s overall IBIT position.

According to the company’s official SEC filing, Wells Fargo and its associated investment managers reported 49,577,094 IBIT shares as of September 30.

That compares with 24,396,222 shares at the end of June, representing an increase of approximately 103%.

However, these figures should not be interpreted as Wells Fargo purchasing $2.35 billion in Bitcoin for its own corporate treasury.

The filing includes positions associated with different investment-management entities, including securities managed or held for clients.

This distinction could be even more significant than the headline number itself.

Why Brokerage Clients Could Become Important For Bitcoin

For years, institutional Bitcoin adoption was closely associated with corporate treasury purchases and investment funds.

Companies such as Strategy helped establish Bitcoin as an asset that corporations could hold on their balance sheets.

However, the expansion of regulated Bitcoin ETFs has created another route for investors to access the cryptocurrency.

Instead of purchasing Bitcoin through specialized exchanges, investors can obtain exposure through conventional brokerage accounts, financial advisers, and wealth-management platforms.

Wells Fargo’s latest filing provides an example of how substantial this distribution channel has become.

Its two largest brokerage-related IBIT positions accounted for approximately 84.7% of the group’s reported shares.

This suggests that the growth of Bitcoin exposure through traditional financial services deserves closer attention.

Nevertheless, the filing does not identify every underlying investor or establish how much of the reported increase came from new retail customers rather than existing institutional accounts.

What it does demonstrate is that Bitcoin-linked securities are becoming an increasingly established part of conventional investment infrastructure.

The $2.35 Billion Figure Tells Only Part Of The Story

Another important consideration is the difference between the number of ETF shares held and their reported market value.

Wells Fargo’s aggregate IBIT share count increased approximately 103% between June and September.

However, the reported value of those shares increased from approximately $812 million to $2.35 billion, a gain of roughly 189%.

The difference reflects both the higher share count and changes in IBIT’s market valuation.

This distinction matters because a rising reported position value does not necessarily represent an equivalent amount of new capital entering Bitcoin.

Furthermore, the September 30 filing represents a historical snapshot.

It cannot establish whether Wells Fargo’s associated accounts maintained, reduced, or expanded their exposure during Bitcoin’s more recent market correction.

As Bitcoinist previously highlighted, BlackRock’s IBIT experienced a period of withdrawals before attracting renewed inflows on November 16.

The contrast between earlier quarterly accumulation and more recent ETF volatility demonstrates why institutional adoption should be evaluated over longer periods rather than through individual trading sessions.

Could Wall Street Distribution Become Bitcoin’s Next Major Growth Driver?

Saylor’s comments arrive as Bitcoin continues navigating a challenging market environment.

Although price volatility has affected investor sentiment, the expansion of traditional investment channels remains an important structural development.

Banks and brokerage platforms already maintain relationships with millions of customers, providing infrastructure that could make Bitcoin exposure more accessible to investors who prefer familiar financial products.

This does not mean every brokerage customer will purchase Bitcoin, nor does it guarantee that ETF demand will consistently increase.

Indeed, recent Bitcoin ETF withdrawals demonstrate that investors can reduce exposure just as quickly as they increase it.

However, the growing availability of regulated Bitcoin products represents a meaningful difference from earlier cryptocurrency market cycles.

Bitcoin no longer depends exclusively on specialized trading platforms to reach potential investors.

What Happens Next For Bitcoin Institutional Adoption?

We believe the most important takeaway from Saylor’s comments is not simply that Wells Fargo reported billions of dollars in Bitcoin ETF exposure.

It is that traditional brokerage infrastructure has become an important channel through which investors can participate in the Bitcoin market.

The next quarterly disclosures will help determine whether the growth reported in September continued during the subsequent period of market volatility.

For now, the latest figures reinforce a constructive long-term trend: Bitcoin is becoming increasingly accessible through established financial institutions.

And while short-term price movements remain uncertain, the expansion of traditional distribution channels could become one of the most important developments shaping Bitcoin adoption over the coming years.

title: Coinbase Brings ChatGPT Into Crypto Trading as Pancake Rebrand Signals Binance Rivalry
description:
Coinbase brings crypto trading to ChatGPT as Pancake drops Swap from its name, raising the stakes in the race against Binance DeFi ecosystem.
The post Coinbase Brings ChatGPT Into Crypto Trading as Pancake Rebrand Signals Binance Rivalry appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Coinbase is bringing crypto trading directly into ChatGPT as competition for AI-powered financial services intensifies. Meanwhile, PancakeSwap has dropped “Swap” from its name, expanding beyond decentralized trading. The two developments show how Coinbase and Binance-linked crypto projects are positioning themselves for the next phase of digital finance.

Coinbase announced its ChatGPT integration last night, allowing users to connect accounts and manage portfolios. Users can check balances, analyze holdings, and place eligible trades using everyday language. And every order requires explicit approval before execution.

The timing coincides with Pancake’s attempt to reposition itself beyond its original decentralized exchange business.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Coinbase Brings Crypto Trading Directly Into ChatGPT

The Coinbase plugin allows eligible users to trade crypto and equities without leaving ChatGPT. Users can request market or limit orders through conversational instructions.

Before execution, ChatGPT displays an interactive confirmation card showing order details. Users must approve the transaction before Coinbase processes it through its Advanced Trade platform. Standard trading fees, eligibility requirements, and account limits still apply.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong described the integration as another step toward an emerging agentic economy. The idea involves AI assistants handling increasingly complex financial tasks for users. But Coinbase still keeps humans responsible for approving individual trades for now.

The integration also builds on Coinbase’s AI infrastructure. Its Coinbase for Agents toolkit provides developers with connections to trading accounts and market data. The ChatGPT launch brings those capabilities into a more accessible consumer interface.

As of today, the official integration currently remains limited to eligible U.S. Coinbase users. It also depends on ChatGPT account and workspace availability.

Pancake Rebrand Takes Binance’s DeFi Ecosystem Beyond Swaps

While Coinbase expands through ChatGPT, Pancake is changing how users perceive its decentralized trading ecosystem. Formerly known as PancakeSwap, the platform announced its rebrand today. The new identity reflects six years of expansion beyond its original token-swapping business.

Pancake now operates across more than 11 blockchain networks. The platform reports over 208 million users and more than $4.4 trillion in cumulative trading volume.

Pancakeswap (CAKE)
24h7d30d1yAll time

Its services now include perpetual contracts, tokenized stocks, ETFs, yield products, and developer infrastructure. The project is also preparing a dedicated mobile application. Its CAKE ticker and contract address remain unchanged, with existing staking positions unaffected.

Pancake’s relationship with Binance makes this rebrand interesting. Binance Labs announced a strategic investment in CAKE in June 2022. The investment supported the decentralized exchange’s development within the BNB Chain ecosystem.

Coinbase and Binance Compete for the Future of AI Trading

The rivalry becomes clearer when looking beyond the latest announcements. Binance has already introduced its own AI infrastructure through Binance Agent OS. Launched in August 2026, the platform connects compatible AI applications with Binance trading, market data, wallet, and payment capabilities.

Its Model Context Protocol server supports compatible AI agents, including ChatGPT. Developers can build applications that access supported Binance services through user-controlled permissions.

Pancake is also developing its position in this emerging market. In July, the platform partnered with BNB Chain’s Agent Studio to help developers deploy autonomous agents.

These agents can interact with Pancake’s liquidity pools, rebalance positions, and execute trading strategies. Its AI tools also include portfolio planning and assistance across DeFi products.

This creates an interesting contrast between the two ecosystems. Coinbase is bringing AI-powered trading directly to consumers through ChatGPT. Binance is building infrastructure that allows developers and AI agents to interact with its services. Pancake adds a decentralized execution layer to the wider BNB Chain ecosystem.

The next battle in crypto may not be about which exchange attracts the most human traders. It could be about which infrastructure becomes the preferred destination for AI-powered financial activity.

title: Why a 5% Stablecoin Return Can Still Cost Holders Money
description:
Key TakeAways A steady peg doesn’t protect euro value. A 10% euro rise cancels 10% yield. Two conversion fees push […]
The post Why a 5% Stablecoin Return Can Still Cost Holders Money appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key TakeAways

  • A steady peg doesn’t protect euro value.
  • A 10% euro rise cancels 10% yield.
  • Two conversion fees push the hurdle higher.
  • EU rules ban interest on e-money tokens.

In September 2026, the European Banking Authority urged the Commission to consider regulating crypto-asset lending, the kind of business that sits behind stablecoin yields offered to Europeans.

For anyone who swapped euros to earn one, that yield has a catch. Our earlier piece showed why a perfect dollar peg can still cost holders euros. This one works out how much return it takes to cover that gap, where a return can legally come from in the EU, and what the extra dollar yield is really paying for.

A 5% return that ends €455 short

Start with €10,000 and an exchange rate of 1.10, so one euro buys $1.10. Ignore fees for now. The saver receives 11,000 tokens, each redeemable for $1.

A lending product then adds 5% over twelve months, lifting the balance to 11,550 tokens. The peg never slips.

The euro moves instead. By year-end EUR/USD sits at 1.21, and those 11,550 tokens convert back to €9,545.45. That leaves the saver €454.55 down after a year of positive returns.

The currency side of this is the trap our earlier piece walked through: a 10% euro rise cuts a dollar balance’s euro value by about 9.09%. What changes here is the yield. With no return, the saver would have ended at €9,090.91. The 5% claws back half of that damage. Half.

The return you need just to get your euros back

With the peg intact and no costs, one line covers it:

Required return = exit rate ÷ entry rate – 1

Here that’s 1.21 ÷ 1.10 – 1, or 10%. Earn less and the saver loses money in euro terms, however good the dollar figure looks.

Fees lift the bar. Assume 0.5% goes on the way in and another 0.5% on the way out, round numbers chosen for illustration rather than taken from any provider’s price list. Only €9,950 gets converted, buying 10,945 tokens, and the exit fee trims whatever comes back. Both deductions enter the formula:

Required return = (exit rate ÷ entry rate) ÷ (0.995 × 0.995) – 1

At 1.21, the hurdle rises to about 11.11%. The same 5% year now returns €9,450.24. Swap in your own platform’s fees and the formula still works.

Euro weakens to 1.00

No yield, no fees: €11,000.00

5% yield, no fees: €11,550.00

5% yield, with fees: €11,434.79

Yield needed after fees: none

Rate stays at 1.10

No yield, no fees: €10,000.00

5% yield, no fees: €10,500.00

5% yield, with fees: €10,395.26

Yield needed after fees: about 1.01%

Euro strengthens to 1.21

No yield, no fees: €9,090.91

5% yield, no fees: €9,545.45

5% yield, with fees: €9,450.24

Yield needed after fees: about 11.11%

Hypothetical scenarios calculated by the Coindoo team for €10,000 converted at 1.10 and held for one year. Tokens stay at $1, fees are 0.5% per conversion, and the figures exclude taxes and inflation.

A weaker euro gives the saver a currency gain with no yield at all. A flat rate makes fees the main obstacle, small but real. A stronger euro is the case that hurts, and it turns a respectable 5% into a loss.

Real routes rarely cost a neat 0.5%. Trading fees, exchange spreads, network charges and bank fees stack up, and fixed charges bite harder on small balances. Redemption has its own catch. Under Circle’s EEA redemption policy, retail USDC holders need an account that can receive dollars, and Circle warns that banks may charge for incoming payments or currency conversion. A $1 redemption claim tells you very little about the euros that finally land in your account.

Breaking even also has a narrow meaning here: the same number of euros back. It ignores inflation. And it skips the obvious question of what those euros could have earned without ever leaving the currency.

What the extra dollar yield pays for

Dollar returns tend to sit above euro returns because US policy rates do. The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on October 28. A day later, the ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.50%.

That gap of roughly 1.25 to 1.5 percentage points isn’t free money. A saver who wanted the dollar return without the currency exposure would have to hedge it, and in currency markets the cost of hedging tracks the interest-rate difference between the two currencies. Economists call this covered interest parity. In plain terms: remove the currency risk and most of the extra yield goes with it.

Skip the hedge and the saver keeps the premium, along with the risk the cards above show. Part of any dollar stablecoin yield above euro rates is payment for carrying that risk, whatever the platform calls it.

Crypto lending rates don’t move one-for-one with central banks. Borrower demand sets them, and they can swing far from policy rates. The currency trade-off stays the same either way.

READ MORE:

The World Bank’s USDC Plan Has a Problem Nobody Mentions

In the EU, the issuer can’t pay you that 5%

So where does a European’s stablecoin return come from? Not from the token. Circle’s EU white paper for USDC describes a token backed by dollar-denominated assets and redeemable 1:1 for dollars. Holding it earns nothing.

MiCA Article 50 closes the obvious shortcut. It bars e-money-token issuers and crypto-asset service providers from granting interest on those tokens, and it counts any reward linked to how long you hold them as interest, whatever the label. A regulated EU exchange can’t pay you for simply keeping USDC in your account.

Any advertised yield therefore points somewhere else: a lending arrangement, a DeFi protocol, or a platform operating outside that rule. Every one of them puts your tokens in someone else’s hands. Ask who borrows them, what secures the loan, whether withdrawals can be paused, and whether the rate is fixed or resets daily. The 5% in our example is a completed year’s return, while an advertised annual rate can change long before the year is out.

That lending business, including activity linked to DeFi, is exactly what the EBA wants brought under rules. MiCA doesn’t cover it today.

When dollars fit, and when EURC makes more sense

None of this makes a dollar balance a mistake. If you have a dollar invoice to pay or dollar income coming in, you already hold the right currency, and the euro rate barely touches you.

Euro spenders face a different test. Circle describes EURC as redeemable 1:1 for euros, which takes the currency mismatch off the table. Switching currency leaves issuer, custody and platform risk where they were. What it removes is the exchange-rate line from the calculation.

Before converting, write down three numbers: the rate you get in at, the total cost of the round trip, and the return the product has actually paid in the past rather than the one on the banner. The yield left after fees is the size of euro rally the balance can absorb. A bigger rally eats the gain, however many tokens you’ve added.

The post Why a 5% Stablecoin Return Can Still Cost Holders Money appeared first on Coindoo.

title: Wall Street Bought at $80,000. What Now?
description:
Monday’s Bitfinex Alpha set a base case for bitcoin to trade between $61,800 and $69,400 this week, with risks skewed towards a retest of the 15 November low of $62,029.…
The post Wall Street Bought at $80,000. What Now?  appeared first on Bitfinex blog.
fullContent:
Monday’s Bitfinex Alpha set a base case for bitcoin to trade between $61,800 and $69,400 this week, with risks skewed towards a retest of the 15 November low of $62,029. In the two sessions since, it has traded in the lower half of that range and within the July $61,300 to $67,000 base range where it spent almost seven weeks after the cycle low of $57,803 on 1 July.

If macro pressure eases and bitcoin still fails to recover, that would reinforce the signal from the week’s first two sessions that spot demand, rather than macro, is the key constraint. The probability of a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December has now fallen to 3.5 percent. The two-year Treasury yield has also eased from 4.88 percent to about 4.8 percent and Nvidia’s Q3 results came in ahead of forecasts, which should be supportive for risk assets. Bitcoin, however, closed 17 November at $64,952, 0.7 percent below Sunday’s weekly close of $65,386.

Figure: Target Rate Probabilities for the December FOMC hint towards a certain 25 bps hike. (Source: FedWatch CME)

For this issue we ask: where is spot demand for bitcoin coming from? With corporate treasury companies and Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) providing no net buying over the past month, we have turned to quarterly Form 13F filings of US institutional investment managers with more than $100 million in listed securities to see who bought spot ETFs during the third quarter. 

Institutional Holdings: Bank Clients and Hedge Funds Bought the Third-Quarter Rally

The filings indicate that the third-quarter recovery was bought largely by two groups: wealth-management clients of large banks and hedge funds returning after two quarters of selling. US spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $6.36 billion over the quarter and their holdings rose by about 75,800 BTC to 1.30 million BTC. The largest reported changes in the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) between 30 June and 30 September were:

  • Wells Fargo: 24.4 million to 49.58 million shares, worth $2.35 billion, making it the largest reported holder. Across all funds its position rose from 15,917 to 30,553 BTC, with about 85 percent of its IBIT shares booked at its two brokerage arms on behalf of clients.
  • Bank of America: 1.72 million to 14.48 million shares, worth $685 million.
  • Brevan Howard and Millennium: 7.2 million to 22.4 million shares and 9.7 million to 20.8 million shares respectively.
  • Harvard: unchanged at 3.04 million shares.

Goldman Sachs also lifted its spot bitcoin ETF holdings from about $580 million to $1.28 billion. By our estimate, the increases at these five firms alone equal a little over half of the bitcoin the ETFs added in the quarter.

Figure: Reported IBIT holdings in Form 13F filings, 30 June against 30 September 2026 (Source: SEC filings).

It is worth being clear about the significance of these positions. Individually, they are a gauge of institutional sentiment rather than a force on price. Wells Fargo’s increase of about 14,600 BTC was spread across a full quarter, while the five firms together added roughly 42,000 BTC over 64 sessions, or about 650 BTC a session. Filers of Form 13F as a group held only 22.4 percent of ETF assets at the end of June, leaving most demand outside these findings. The ETFs now hold about 1.26 million BTC, and last week’s outflows averaged about 2,900 BTC a session, more than four times the pace at which these firms bought. The filings are therefore most useful for identifying the marginal ETF buyer.

Cost Basis: Third-Quarter Buyers Are Underwater

The filings do not disclose entry prices, but daily flow data allows us to estimate them, indicating that most of this buying took place near the top of the advance. Of the $6.36 billion of net inflows in the quarter, $5.76 billion, or 91 percent, arrived between 17 August and 25 September. Weighting each day’s net flow by the Bitfinex daily close gives an average entry price of about $80,070 for that period. Only $685 million of the quarter’s net inflow arrived on days when bitcoin closed below the 17 November close of $64,952.

Figure: Bitfinex BTC/USD daily close against the flow-weighted entry of third-quarter ETF inflows, the ETF cost basis and the July Base (Source: Bitfinex; Farside Investors; Checkonchain).

Buyers in that window are therefore about 19 percent below cost, while the whole quarter’s flow-weighted entry price of $78,300 implies a 17 percent loss. The wider holder base is similarly exposed: its average cost basis since launch in January 2024 is $84,872, giving a price-to-cost-basis ratio of 0.76 on 17 November, or a 24 percent unrealised loss.  

Apart from one day last week, that ratio has been lower only during the period between June and mid-August, when it reached a record low of 0.69 on 30 June.

ETF Flows: About Half of the Third-Quarter Buying Has Been Sold

A 13F is a snapshot of 30 September, so it does not tell us whether these institutions still hold their positions. Flows since then indicate that about half of the third-quarter buying is still in place, leaving it as potential supply if the July Base fails. Net outflows in the fourth quarter to 17 November total $3.09 billion, equal to 49 percent of third-quarter inflows. The selling has been concentrated in the 13 sessions since 30 October, 11 of which recorded outflows, for a net $3.22 billion, the largest 13-session total since 11 June.

Figure: US spot bitcoin ETF daily net flows and cumulative total, 1 July to 17 November 2026 (Source: Farside Investors).

The seven-session run of ETF outflows described in Monday’s report ended on 16 November with a net inflow of $7.9 million, but selling resumed on 17 November with a net outflow of $239.9 million, of which IBIT accounted for $209.5 million. The flat session was therefore a pause rather than a return of demand. The test set in the 4 November Intelligence Update remains three consecutive sessions of inflows comparable in size to the outflows that preceded them before we can become confident in any change in sentiment.

The decline in ETF bitcoin holdings between May and July offers a guide to the scale of the current outflows.During that decline, ETF holdings fell from 1.351 million BTC on 6 May to 1.218 million BTC on 13 July, a reduction of 9.9 percent. They bottomed 12 days after bitcoin’s 1 July low and did not begin to recover until mid-August. Holdings are now down about 3.2 percent from their 21 October peak of 1.305 million BTC. We would therefore expect ETF demand to lag price again, leaving a potential price bottom unconfirmed by flows for several weeks. 

Figure: US spot bitcoin ETF holdings in BTC and bitcoin price relative to the average ETF cost basis, 2026 (Source: Checkonchain).

Futures and Treasuries: The Other Institutional Channels Are Also Shrinking

ETFs are one of three channels through which institutions hold bitcoin. The other two, CME futures and corporate treasuries, also indicate weakening demand. Monday’s report noted that CME open interest (OI), the number of futures contracts outstanding on the venue most used by US institutions, had remained steady. It has since fallen from 102,100 BTC on 13 November to about 97,100 BTC on 18 November, while aggregate OI across all venues is little changed at about 648,000 BTC. This indicates that regulated accounts are now reducing exposure while offshore leverage has not cleared further, so the reset in positioning we set out on Monday remains incomplete.

Figure: Aggregate btc-notional open interest across perp and futures pairs (Source: Coinglass)

Corporate treasury demand is small relative to the selling. Strategy bought 485 BTC for $33.4 million in the week to 15 November, according to its 16 November filing, while $206.3 million of the $244.7 million it raised from share sales went towards repurchasing its STRC preferred stock. The treasury channel is therefore not offsetting ETF outflows that averaged $213 million a day last week.

On-chain data also indicates selling pressure has not eased. The short-term holder Spent Output Profit Ratio (STH-SOPR), which compares the price at which coins younger than 155 days are sold with the price paid for them, fell to 0.964 on 16 November, its lowest reading since 7 February and below the June low of 0.966. A recovery towards 1, which Monday’s report identified as the sign that loss-driven selling is fading, has not yet begun.

Altcoins: Bitcoin Led the Latest Leg Lower

Altcoin behaviour is consistent with our view that the latest decline was driven by spot selling of bitcoin itself. Between the 8 November close and the 15 November low, bitcoin fell 17.1 percent while the median of 17 large altcoins on Bitfinex fell 19.2 percent, a ratio of 1.1 times. Across the six pullbacks between July and October, that ratio averaged 1.6 times given that altcoin declines are normally amplified by leverage. This suggests that much of the leverage in altcoins has been removed, consistent with their earlier under-performance. Since 30 September the same basket is down 36.4 percent against 22.3 percent for bitcoin, with ether down 32.1 percent, SOL 36.4 percent and XRP 34.0 percent.

Figure: Bitcoin against 17 large altcoins, 30 September close to 17 November close and 8 November close to 15 November low (Source: Bitfinex).

The rebound in the last few days shows a similar pattern, with moves in bitcoin amplified in the altcoin complex. From the 15 November low to the 17 November close the median altcoin gained 8.4 percent against 4.7 percent for bitcoin, 1.8 times as much and above the 1.3 times average of earlier rebounds. This is more consistent with short covering in the assets that had fallen furthest than with new demand, given that ether ETFs recorded net outflows of $957 million over the 13 sessions since 30 October. If bitcoin retests the $61,300 lower edge of the July Base, about six percent below the 17 November close, the historical range of ratios implies a fall of roughly six to nine percent for the median altcoin. ETH/BTC holding above its 14 November low of 0.0276 is the first sign we would look for that relative selling has ended.

Macro: Relief Arrived and Bitcoin Did Not Respond

Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion against expectations near $109 billion after the close on 17 November and its shares rose more than four percent in extended trading, yet bitcoin gained less than one percent. The US Dollar Index remains above 103, the level set in Monday’s report. Two events remain this week: the Fed minutes at 19:00 UTC on 18 November, and the Anthropic listing, which prices on 18 November and trades on 19 November.

Outlook: A Holder Base Under Pressure Keeps Risks Skewed Lower

Base case. We expect bitcoin to remain inside the July Base, between about $60,100 and $68,600, the range implied by options for the 27 November expiry, with risks still skewed towards a retest of $62,029 and the $61,300 lower edge of the Base. Since Monday, the macro constraint has eased but the spot-demand constraint has become clearer: the institutions that bought in the third quarter are underwater, about half of that buying remains in the funds and CME positioning is now being reduced.

What would confirm it? ETF flows that stay flat or negative, CME OI continuing to fall and STH-SOPR holding below 0.98 would indicate that institutional holders are still reducing their positions. On macro, Fed minutes today showing wider support for a hike than October’s two dissents implied, with the US Dollar Index above 103, would keep pressure on non-yielding assets.

What would invalidate it? To the upside, three consecutive sessions of ETF inflows with CME OI stabilising and STH-SOPR recovering towards 1 would indicate that institutional selling has ended and bring $69,400 and then $72,700 into view. To the downside, acceptance below $61,300 with ETF outflows above $300 million a day would point to the $57,803 cycle low.

What to watch. ETF flows for 18 to 20 November and CME open interest carry the most weight. The Fed minutes on 18 November, the first day of Anthropic trading on 19 November, the options expiry on 20 November, ETH/BTC against 0.0276, Strategy’s next filing on 23 November and its MSCI removal on 30 November are secondary.

The post Wall Street Bought at $80,000. What Now?  appeared first on Bitfinex blog.

title: Stocks prepare to bounce as bond yields set to spike again: What will Bitcoin do?
description: Nvidia Q3 earnings results and strong growth expectations calmed the decline in the AI sell-off. Futures markets are auguring an upside surge on Wednesday. In the face of this the U.S. 10-year yield is setting up for another big spike. With Bitcoin languishing around $64K, will it be a bounce or a further slide to come?
fullContent:
Nvidia Q3 earnings results and strong growth expectations calmed the decline in the AI sell-off. Futures markets are auguring an upside surge on Wednesday. In the face of this the U.S. 10-year yield is setting up for another big spike. With Bitcoin languishing around $64K, will it be a bounce or a further slide to come?

Nasdaq futures back above major support

Source: TradingView

The Nasdaq 100 E-mini Futures chart shows that the tech/AI heavy index has regained the major ascending trendline that began at the end of March 2026. What’s more, it has successfully retested a smaller descending trendline and is back above the main horizontal supports. With Nvidia (NVDA) having come through its earnings release after the market closed on Tuesday with flying colours, the Nasdaq is likely to witness a decent price recovery on Wednesday.

U.S. 10-year yield set to surge higher again

Source: TradingView

The short-term chart for the U.S. 10-year yield illustrates the head and shoulders pattern that initially stopped the meteoric rise in the yield that topped at 5.36%. A choppy descent then followed which bottomed out at 4.8%. Since then the 10-year yield has spiked again, getting back over 5%. We now have what is to all intents and purposes a bull flag while the yield consolidates. It is probably to be expected that this bull flag breaks out and the yield heads much higher. 5.4% is the target of the measured move.

While the $BTC price can gain from a rising U.S. stock market, a spiking 10-year bond yield is another matter. This suggests that interest rates are going to continue to rise - not a good environment for Bitcoin.

Flag or pennant?

Source: TradingView

It can be seen in the 4-hour chart for $BTC that the price action is continuing to morph into different patterns. Starting with a pennant, and then becoming a flag, the price action may have shifted back to a pennant. A flag is still shown in the faint dotted lines, but if this is the dominant pattern it looks much better for the bulls, given that the tilt is to the downside rather than the typical upward slope of a bear flag. On the other hand, if the pennant is the more likely pattern, this favours the bears and yet another downside break.

A monster bear flag?

Source: TradingView

Zooming right out into the weekly time frame we get a better view of the giant ascending channel and how it possibly interacts with previous large structures. That said, this channel dwarfs any of the bull/bear flags of the previous bull and bear markets.

So if this is a legitimate structure, what is the $BTC price potentially going to do inside of it? From here, it’s a straight choice. Either the pattern breaks down and the price goes below, or there is a bounce that possibly eventually takes the $BTC price all the way up to the top of the channel and a conceivable breakout. It must also be borne in mind that the top of the channel is in fact the neckline of a massive inverse head and shoulders structure.

The ascending channel could also be interpreted as a behemoth of a bear flag. However, it’s very arguable whether the flag pole can be taken from the top of the last bull market given the huge kink of a bear flag in the middle of it. Just for giggles, a measured move out of this monster and you get a price of $20K. Which of these scenarios will be the one that ultimately takes place?

title: Gate Founder Dr. Han Speaks At The Oxford Union On 13 Years Of Building
description:

The post Gate Founder Dr. Han Speaks At The Oxford Union On 13 Years Of Building  appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
On November 12, 2026, Gate Founder and CEO Dr. Han was invited to speak at the Oxford Union, where he delivered a keynote address titled “Start Alone” and engaged in discussions with the audience.

Reflecting on his 13-year entrepreneurial journey, from founding Gate independently in 2013 to leading it into a digital asset platform with a global business presence, Dr. Han shared his thoughts on innovation, competition, team management, and entrepreneurial opportunities in the AI era.

During the speech and subsequent Q&A session, he also discussed a range of industry topics, including the value of cryptocurrency trading platforms, stablecoins and central bank digital currencies, AI-driven cybersecurity challenges, the tokenization of real-world assets (RWA), and the future of centralized and decentralized finance. These discussions further demonstrated his multifaceted perspective on the evolving digital asset industry.

Starting Alone: From a Solo Entrepreneurial Beginning to Building a Global Team

Gate’s founding was inspired by Dr. Han’s personal experience of suffering losses while trading through online forums in his early years. Recognizing the shortcomings of the digital asset trading environment at the time, particularly in terms of trust and security, he decided to build a more trustworthy digital asset trading platform himself.

In 2013, Gate was launched without external venture capital backing, with Dr. Han initially driving the business on his own. Over the following 13 years, Gate navigated multiple industry cycles, market fluctuations, and business challenges, gradually growing through continuous innovation and adaptation while establishing a business presence and team spanning global markets.

This journey also reflects the principle he outlined in his speech: entrepreneurship can begin with one person, but achieving long-term business growth requires continuously expanding the boundaries of what a company can do.

Innovation in the AI Era: Accelerating Learning While Maintaining Deep Thinking

In his speech, Dr. Han identified innovation and execution efficiency as two important factors in maintaining a company’s competitiveness. He noted that in an increasingly competitive market, businesses need not only to keep generating new ideas but also to accelerate product development, launches, and iterations. Achieving this first requires improving the efficiency of learning.

In the past, entrepreneurs typically had to search for information through search engines, read various articles and research reports, and gradually develop an understanding of new technologies and industry concepts. In the fast-changing crypto industry, where new developments emerge constantly, traditional methods of information retrieval and reading alone are often insufficient to meet the demands of rapid learning. AI offers a new approach. By asking AI questions directly, entrepreneurs can more easily familiarize themselves with unfamiliar concepts, organize complex knowledge, and obtain relevant information, thereby reducing the time required to learn.

However, Dr. Han particularly emphasized that while AI can accelerate information access and knowledge acquisition, it cannot replace deep thinking. Innovation cannot simply follow competitors, nor can it be achieved by copying other people’s ideas wholesale. Information can be obtained through the internet and AI, but truly valuable innovation must still be grounded in independent thinking, enabling businesses to identify directions that differ from existing market solutions.

Therefore, while rapidly absorbing new knowledge, entrepreneurs also need to set aside time for independent thinking and actively explore what they can do next, where existing products can be improved, and how to develop solutions that differentiate them from competitors. Once a clear direction has been identified, businesses must also have the ability to turn ideas into reality quickly. Dr. Han summarized this process as a combination of sustained effort, deep thinking, and efficient execution, emphasizing that businesses need to move forward in a faster, more stable, and smarter way.

From Solo Entrepreneurship to Team Collaboration: Building an Efficient Remote Organization

As a company grows, its innovative ideas ultimately need to be put into practice through its organization and team. Taking Gate’s team management as an example, Dr. Han explained how a business can maintain operational efficiency in a global, remote-working environment.

Today, Gate’s team members collaborate remotely online. For a global team of this scale, ensuring effective coordination among employees working in different locations is an important management challenge. This is particularly true for product development, where teams must not only be able to develop and launch products quickly, but also ensure product quality and continuously improve their offerings.

Dr. Han stated that businesses need to further improve organizational efficiency, enabling research and development, product teams, and other business functions to work together effectively and deliver products faster and with higher quality.

Only by establishing efficient organizational collaboration mechanisms can innovative ideas be translated into market competitiveness. Entrepreneurship can begin with one person, but long-term business growth requires bringing more people together. After taking the first step, entrepreneurs must also find like-minded partners and build a team united by shared goals and capable of driving the company’s continued growth together.

The Distinct Value of Professional Crypto Trading Platforms as Traditional Finance Enters the Market

During the live Q&A session, the host noted that traditional financial institutions have also begun offering cryptocurrency purchasing services. The host then asked what long-term value specialized crypto trading platforms could offer as traditional financial institutions increasingly enter the market.

In response, Dr. Han pointed out that traditional financial platforms provide users with more convenient access to digital assets, but specialized crypto trading platforms still have a clear advantage in terms of transaction costs. Citing trading fees as an example, he noted that cost differences between platform types can be significant for users who trade frequently. 

For professional traders who trade frequently, differences in fees directly affect their overall trading costs, making specialized crypto trading platforms a compelling option. For users who hold assets over the long term and trade less frequently, traditional financial platforms can also be an alternative.

This perspective reflects the increasingly diverse service landscape taking shape in the digital asset market. As traditional financial institutions and the crypto industry become more integrated, different types of platforms can offer differentiated services based on user needs. Meanwhile, transaction costs, product depth, and professional trading capabilities will remain important competitive advantages for crypto-native platforms.

Stablecoins and the Digital Pound: Competition Among Digital Currencies Is Going Global

Discussing the digital pound being explored by the Bank of England and its relationship with stablecoins, Dr. Han focused on the global nature of stablecoins. He noted that the market capitalization of US dollar stablecoins has already exceeded $300 billion, equivalent to approximately 1% to 2% of the US M2 money supply. Stablecoin use cases have also gradually expanded beyond digital asset trading into everyday payments, demonstrating their potential as digital payment instruments.

In his view, the digital pound will not only face competition within the UK’s domestic monetary system, but also from US dollar stablecoins that already circulate widely across the global internet. Unlike traditional fiat currencies, which primarily rely on domestic financial systems, stablecoins can circulate across borders through the internet, with their use not limited to any single country or region.

Therefore, the development of the digital pound will need to consider how it can establish competitiveness in the global digital currency market, particularly given the strong market acceptance that US dollar stablecoins have already achieved. This also reflects how competition among digital currencies is expanding beyond technological innovation alone to encompass payment use cases, global circulation capabilities, levels of market adoption, and more.

AI-Driven Cyberattacks Escalate: Digital Asset Security Requires Continuous Defense and Proactive Protection

The rapid development of AI has also made cybersecurity an important topic of discussion. Drawing on his own experience of being targeted by hackers in the early days, Dr. Han observed that cyberattacks have become significantly more sophisticated. Attackers are now using AI to identify platform vulnerabilities rapidly and coordinate attacks through multiple AI Agents, making the attack process more efficient and intensive while increasing the difficulty of platform defense.

In response to these changes, digital asset platforms need to establish more comprehensive security protection systems. Security management cannot focus solely on the trading system itself; it must also cover internal corporate working environments, VPN networks, and other infrastructure. Every part of these systems could become a potential security risk, requiring professional teams to monitor, inspect, and maintain them.

At the same time, AI can also serve as an important tool for defense teams. Dr. Han explained that Gate has established a collaborative security testing mechanism involving red teams and blue teams, and uses AI to simulate hacker attacks and conduct security tests on the platform in advance to help identify potential risks and strengthen defensive capabilities. It also demonstrates that AI does not inherently give attackers or defenders an absolute advantage. What matters is whether businesses can keep pace with technological developments and apply them effectively to security testing, risk identification, and system protection.

RWA and 24/7 Trading: Blockchain Is Expanding How Traditional Assets Circulate

Discussing real-world assets (RWA) and round-the-clock markets, Dr. Han expressed an optimistic view of the long-term prospects for asset tokenization. Traditional stock markets are generally subject to trading-hour restrictions, meaning investors often cannot trade through conventional channels on weekends or outside regular market hours. However, as real-world assets such as stocks and gold are increasingly brought on-chain through blockchain infrastructure, investors are gaining access to more trading hours and channels for asset circulation.

Dr. Han believes this development can provide more options for investors with immediate liquidity needs. For example, if investors need to sell some of their assets over the weekend to meet other funding requirements, 24/7 trading mechanisms can offer additional opportunities to access liquidity. Of course, the liquidity of on-chain assets outside traditional market hours is currently still lower than that of daytime markets, and the relevant infrastructure has room for further improvement. However, as more real-world assets enter on-chain markets and the number of market participants continues to grow, on-chain trading liquidity and trading models are also expected to mature further.

From this perspective, the value of RWA lies not only in creating new trading channels for traditional assets, but also in using blockchain technology to improve the efficiency of asset circulation and provide investors with more flexible ways to participate in the market.

From a Crypto Trading Platform to a Money App: Meeting a Broader Range of User Needs

When the host asked how Gate would position itself in a future where crypto technology becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life, to the point that users may no longer be aware of the underlying technology, Dr. Han shared Gate’s long-term vision. He pointed out that users may not trade every day, but they need to use money every day, whether for everyday payments, asset management, or wealth growth. Therefore, Gate aims to gradually evolve from a platform centered on digital asset trading into a Money App that serves a wider range of financial needs.

This direction goes beyond trading itself, incorporating payments, earnings, and everyday money management into Gate’s long-term plans, allowing users to handle more of their financial needs on a single platform. This vision is also closely connected to Gate’s assessment of the industry’s future.

Dr. Han explained that in the past, much of the activity in the crypto market was concentrated on asset speculation and trading, with users seeking returns by buying low and selling high. However, as the industry matures, the value of blockchain is extending beyond trading activities alone and increasingly into the realm of financial infrastructure. More traditional financial institutions are exploring ways to bring assets such as stocks, gold, and commodities onto blockchain-based markets. One important reason is that blockchain can enable faster and lower-cost asset transfers and transactions.

For ordinary users, understanding the underlying technologies of cryptocurrencies or blockchain is not necessarily a prerequisite for benefiting from more efficient trading and management of traditional assets through on-chain infrastructure. In Dr. Han’s view, this is an important direction for the future of the crypto industry: blockchain technology will gradually become a key part of financial infrastructure, creating long-term value through practical applications.

Decentralization and Security: Balancing User Choice with Risk Protection

During the Q&A session, a representative of the Oxford Blockchain Society raised questions about blockchain decentralization, government regulation, and platform responsibility, bringing into focus one of the central issues facing the digital asset industry: how to strike a balance between openness and security.

Dr. Han believes that decentralization is one of the most defining features of blockchain. By reducing reliance on a single centralized institution, blockchain can lower certain trust costs and enable participants to collaborate through technological mechanisms. Bitcoin’s continued operation for more than 15 years is an important demonstration of the long-term viability of this model and the trust it has established in the market.

However, decentralization can also be exploited by wrongdoers. As security incidents involving the theft of digital assets continue to occur, protecting user assets while preserving the open nature of blockchain has become an issue the industry must address. Citing cases in which stablecoin issuers have frozen funds in response to specific security incidents, Dr. Han noted that appropriate risk controls are practically meaningful when illegal activities and user asset security are involved. In particular, when stolen funds could potentially be used to support other illegal activities, measures taken by relevant institutions to protect broader public interest are understandable.

On the boundaries between regulation and individual choice, Dr. Han pointed out that one of blockchain’s key values lies in providing users with diverse options, allowing them to choose digital assets and services with different operating mechanisms and management models according to their own needs. Compared with mandatory controls that leave users with no alternative options, an open blockchain ecosystem gives users greater freedom of choice. He believes that protecting user security and respecting individual choice are both important considerations that the industry must take into account as it develops.

First-Mover Advantage and Industry Competition: Long-Term Conviction Must Be Accompanied by Continuous Review

Discussing industry competition and business management, Dr. Han shared his views on first-mover advantages and market dynamics. He pointed out that in the early stages of an industry’s development, businesses that are able to establish scale advantages ahead of their competitors have the opportunity to attract greater market attention, user resources, and capital support, further strengthening their position. This cumulative effect created by a first-mover advantage can give leading businesses a stronger resource base in subsequent competition.

He cited major internet companies and crypto trading platforms as examples, explaining that once a market matures, it becomes increasingly difficult for later entrants to compete with established leaders. Even with greater investment or talented teams, newcomers may not be able to easily change the existing market landscape. For entrepreneurs, the ability to identify critical stages in an industry’s development and seize opportunities to establish a competitive advantage can have a far-reaching impact on a company’s long-term growth.

Reflecting on his own experience, Dr. Han candidly shared that he started his business immediately after graduating from university and had no prior experience working at a large corporation. As a result, he made a number of mistakes in business operations and decision-making. Some early decisions also led to significant financial losses, which took years to gradually recover from. These experiences gave him a deeper understanding of judgment, risk, and long-term business management throughout the entrepreneurial process.

He believes that while maintaining long-term conviction is essential, businesses must also regularly review their decisions, identify problems in a timely manner, and adjust their direction in response to market developments and actual conditions. Entrepreneurs need both the determination to stay committed to long-term goals and the ability to learn from past experience, develop better approaches, and avoid repeating mistakes, continuously refining their strategies in response to changes in the external environment.

The Future of CEXs and DEXs: Different Models Could Become Complementary

On industry regulation, Dr. Han stated that centralized exchanges (CEXs) and decentralized exchanges (DEXs) differ significantly in their operating models and regulatory approaches. Centralized exchanges are operated by companies with clearly identifiable business entities, making them easier to incorporate into regulatory frameworks through licensing, compliance systems, and operational requirements.

During his speech, Dr. Han noted that Gate has obtained relevant licenses or approvals in multiple jurisdictions, with business coverage across 47 U.S. states, as well as markets in Europe, Dubai, and Japan. By comparison, DEXs typically operate through on-chain smart contracts. Some protocols can continue to function without being directly operated by a traditional corporate entity, creating additional challenges for regulators in identifying responsible parties and implementing oversight.

As for the future of these two models, Dr. Han does not believe that either will completely replace the other. Instead, he believes CEXs and DEXs could gradually develop a complementary relationship. Centralized platforms have advantages in user access, trading speed, and service processes, while decentralized platforms provide users with greater freedom of choice and opportunities for open participation. As regulatory frameworks continue to develop and blockchain technology advances, how these two models leverage their respective strengths and work together will become an important part of the evolution of crypto market infrastructure.

Looking Ahead: Keep Innovating Amid Changes

From individual exploration in the early days of entrepreneurship to building a global team and expanding into a broader range of financial services, Dr. Han’s speech at the Oxford Union looked back on Gate’s 13-year development journey while presenting his perspectives on industry issues including AI, digital asset infrastructure, market competition, and global regulation.

For business, achieving long-term growth requires sustained investment, continuous learning, independent thinking, and efficient execution. AI is changing how knowledge is acquired and how security is protected, while blockchain has the potential to bring traditional assets and financial services further on-chain. As technology and markets continue to evolve, businesses must not only seize emerging opportunities but also turn technological potential into a driver of long-term growth through team collaboration, risk management, and strategic adjustments.

From “Start Alone” to team collaboration, and from its initial entrepreneurial exploration to a business presence spanning global markets, Gate’s 13-year journey demonstrates the importance of long-term innovation and adapting to change. For the next phase, Gate will continue to follow technological developments and evolving market needs, exploring further possibilities at the intersection of digital assets and financial services as it expands its global presence.

About Gate

Gate, founded in 2013 by Dr. Han, is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency and integrated financial services platforms, spanning financial and everyday use cases including asset management, trading and payments. Serving over 63 million users globally, it supports trading across 5,400+ digital assets and 12,800+ stock assets and ETFs, while providing access to a comprehensive range of TradFi assets, including metals, stocks, indices, forex, and commodities to meet users’ end-to-end needs across asset holding, trading, and spending. As an industry benchmark, Gate was among the first platforms to implement 100% Proof of Reserves. Its ecosystem includes Gate Money, Gate Wallet, Gate Ventures, Gate for AI Agent, and a wide range of products and services.

title: How Deep Do S&P 500 Corrections Usually Go? Where 2026’s Drop Ranks
description:
Charlie Bilello says this S&P 500 pullback is the 34th above 5% since 2009, and an earlier 2026 slide ran deeper.
The post How Deep Do S&P 500 Corrections Usually Go? Where 2026’s Drop Ranks appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
The S&P 500 pullback reached as much as 7.1% from its Oct. 6 high, the third of 2026. A chart from Creative Planning’s Charlie Bilello shows the typical correction since 2009 runs deeper.

Bilello, the firm’s chief market strategist, counts it as the 34th correction above 5% since March 2009. However, S&P 500 holders face a milder loss than the 7.6% median, stretched over 42 days instead of 26.

Is a 7% S&P 500 Pullback Really Unusual?

The first pullback of 2026, from Jan. 28 to March 30, reached 9.8%. A seven-day dip in early June stopped at 5.0%.

None of the three has reached 10%. Fundstrat Global Advisors head of research Tom Lee made a 10% correction call for the index in August.

Meanwhile, Bilello’s table cites the Iran war, inflation and Fed hike fears, and AI spending and debt worries.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem signaled Tuesday that the central bank may need further rate increases.

The index closed Tuesday at its lowest level since July 29 after a fourth straight loss, CNBC reported.

Futures rose that night after Nvidia posted better-than-expected earnings.

Still, the index finished at 7,340.53, or 6.4% below its high. Bilello’s 7.1% measures the 7,288 low instead.

“They all seemed like the end of the world at the time,” Charlie Bilello, chief market strategist at Creative Planning, said on X

What Do 34 Corrections Suggest About the Next One?

Only 10 of the 34 corrections ran past 10%, based on Bilello’s table. The deepest, a 35.4% drop in 2020, lasted 33 days.

Historically, the longest slide, 282 days in 2022, fell 27.5%, with inflation and Fed tightening among its listed causes. The current drop lists inflation and Fed hike fears, too.

In contrast, BeInCrypto counted 27 stock markets worldwide down 20% or more from their highs earlier this month. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were not among them.

The post How Deep Do S&P 500 Corrections Usually Go? Where 2026’s Drop Ranks appeared first on BeInCrypto.

Singapore, Singapore, November 18th, 2026, Chainwire

LBank, a global cryptocurrency exchange, has teamed up with SHIB to launch its Esports Thanksgiving campaign, offering rewards valued at up to 150,000 USDT through December 4, 2026. Tapping into the growing anticipation surrounding GTA VI and the wider gaming community, the campaign brings together gaming culture, high-performance hardware, and crypto trading incentives. Featured rewards include an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 32GB graphics card, an Alienware 18 Area-51 gaming laptop, GTA VI Ultimate Edition, a PlayStation 5 Pro, and futures position vouchers for BTC, ETH, SOL, and other assets. The campaign gives users multiple ways to participate, turning trading milestones into opportunities to unlock rewards that extend beyond the crypto market.

The campaign is open to both new and existing users, with a tiered points system spanning LBank's spot and futures markets. Participants can earn points by completing initial trading activities, reaching cumulative net deposit targets, and meeting daily or cumulative trading volume milestones. This multi-tiered structure allows users to accumulate points through different levels of participation throughout the campaign, rather than relying on a single trading threshold.

New users can access a dedicated welcome offer by registering and depositing at least 100 USDT into their futures accounts. Eligible participants can receive a 5 USDT Futures Bonus, with 200 rewards available daily on a first-come, first-served basis. Users can also earn an additional 50 points by depositing 100 USDT into their futures accounts and completing at least 100 USDT in futures trading volume, providing an initial incentive to explore LBank's futures market.

Beyond the welcome offer, participants can earn additional points through deposit and trading milestones. For cumulative net deposits, users can earn 10 points for maintaining 200 USDT for two days, 20 points for maintaining 500 USDT for two days, and 50 points for maintaining 1,000 USDT for three days, with up to 80 points available across the deposit tiers. Daily spot trading offers up to 10 points for reaching trading volumes of 500 USDT and 1,000 USDT, while daily futures trading provides up to 20 points across four volume milestones: 1,000 USDT, 5,000 USDT, 10,000 USDT, and 50,000 USDT. Cumulative futures trading also provides additional opportunities to earn points, with up to 140 points available as users progress through trading volume milestones of up to 500,000 USDT.

Points accumulated during the campaign can be exchanged for a selection of gaming hardware, entertainment products, and crypto-related rewards. By combining sought-after gaming devices and titles with BTC, ETH, and SOL futures position vouchers, LBank offers participants different ways to use their accumulated points, connecting the appeal of gaming rewards with the trading activities at the center of the campaign.

The campaign also reflects LBank and SHIB's shared engagement with communities that extend beyond traditional crypto trading circles. By tapping into the anticipation surrounding GTA VI and gaming culture, the collaboration brings mainstream gaming interests into a crypto campaign, while extending engagement through social media discussions, interactive Bullet Comment activities, and rewards linked to popular gaming culture. For LBank, the campaign builds on its broader efforts to connect crypto with younger audiences through cultural IPs, gaming, memes, digital collectibles, and community-driven participation. The collaboration with SHIB adds another community-driven dimension to the campaign, creating a bridge between crypto-native communities and mainstream gaming culture.

The Esports Thanksgiving campaign will remain open until December 4, 2026. Users can visit the official LBank campaign page to review the full task requirements, points accumulation rules, reward redemption details, and participation terms.

title: XRP Price Reclaims $1: Can It Break 50% Fail rate For XRP Breakouts in 2026?

The post XRP Price Reclaims $1: Can It Break 50% Fail rate For XRP Breakouts in 2026? appeared first on 99Bitcoins.
fullContent:
In Ripple XRP news on Wednesday, November 18, the token climbed back above $1, touching $1.0078 on Binance shortly after 07:00 UTC. It had first slipped under the mark five days earlier. By 09:00 UTC it was trading right at the line, near $0.999. That is up about 4% over 24 hours and 12% from Saturday’s low of $0.893.

Market Cap

The XRP news that matters now is whether the move sticks. A touch isn’t a reclaim: XRP needs a daily close above $1, and it hasn’t had one since Thursday, November 13.

We checked every time XRP closed back above $1 after a close below it since 2021. There were 12 such reclaims. A week later, XRP was higher in 9 of them. But in 5 of the 12, it fell back under $1 within two days.

XRP $1.00 before GTA 6 100% pic.twitter.com/fDx7kMnsI1

— Cobb (@Cobb_XRPL) November 18, 2026

XRP News Today: Whales Pull Coins Off Binance as Traders Turn Less Bearish

No single headline in the XRP news flow drove the bounce. The signals behind it are mostly about who is buying and who stopped betting against XRP.

  • Whale withdrawals: large holders have pulled more than $127 million of XRP off Binance since November 10, CryptoQuant data shared by analyst Darkfost shows. Between $12 million and $33 million left each day. Coins leaving an exchange are usually not about to be sold, though some of these moves may be Binance shifting its own wallets after the October hack.
  • Funding flips: on OKX, the fee that traders with bullish bets pay those with bearish ones was negative from November 15 to 17. It turned slightly positive on Tuesday afternoon, a sign short sellers are backing off.
  • Less leverage: XRP open interest on OKX, the value of open futures bets, fell from $117 million on November 6 to $95 million on Tuesday, about 19% less. The bounce came with fewer leveraged bets, not more.

ETF demand is still missing. U.S. spot XRP ETFs, which hold the coin itself, lost $19.1 million in the week of November 9 to 13 and saw zero net flows on Monday, SoSoValue data shows.

DISCOVER: 9+ Best High-Risk, High-Reward Crypto to Buy in 2026

The First Close Above $1 Often Fails, the Second Usually Holds

Here is how XRP behaved after each daily close back above $1 since 2021:

  • Quick failures: 5 of the 12 reclaims lasted two days or less. That includes April 2021 and this August, when XRP closed above $1 on August 15, lost it the next day, and only held from August 17.
  • What came after: in 4 of those 5 quick failures, XRP closed above $1 again within five days. In April 2021 and August 2026, that second attempt led to rallies of 66% and 48% within a week. Three of the four second attempts held above $1 for more than a month.
  • When it broke: the three reclaims that were lower a week later all came in 2021: two in May, during China’s mining crackdown, and one in September.

So a first close above $1 has been a coin flip on holding. The pattern favors bulls once a second close follows.

DISCOVER: XRP Price Struggles Below $1: Anthropic IPO and Nvidia Earnings Could Trigger Another 33% Drop

XRP Price Analysis: $1 First, Then $1.05

After a week of mostly bearish XRP news, XRP trades at $0.999 on Binance. On the daily chart, it sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1.210, and its 200-day EMA at $1.323.

  • Resistance: $1.05, which held as a floor four times between June and August: on June 6, July 13, July 28 and August 1. Above that, $1.26, a floor that held five times between February and October before it broke this month.
  • Support: $0.893, Saturday’s low. XRP tested it on Saturday and again on Sunday, so it has only two touches so far, and it is the year’s low. Below it, the next marked level is $0.633, the top of XRP’s 2024 range.
Path What has to happen Next stop
Hold Two daily closes above $1, then a break of $1.05 $1.26, the February-October floor
Stall Closes either side of $1, below $1.05 A range between $0.893 and $1.05
Fail A daily close back below $0.95 A retest of $0.893, Saturday’s low

Tonight’s daily close at 00:00 UTC is the first test. The next XRP news to watch is whether ETF flows turn positive, because without them, a bounce built on short sellers backing off can fade fast.

title: SVRN CEO Says Lower Issuance Eases NEAR Selling Pressure as the 1.6% Cap Passes
description: NEAR holders approved a cut to 1.6% max issuance. SVRN CEO Sal Ternullo says it eases selling pressure. Here is what the chart near $3.81 must show.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • NEAR governance ratified a proposal from SVRN CEO Sal Ternullo that lowers the maximum annual token issuance.
  • Ternullo expects less new supply to mean less selling. Price still trades well below its 50-day average.
  • A daily close above resistance after the upgrade would back his case. A slide under the 200-day average would undo it.

NEAR holders have approved a second cut to the network's token issuance in two months. SVRN chief Sal Ternullo, who wrote the proposal, said lower issuance should ease selling pressure on the token.

The timing matters because NEAR has dropped hard since October, and the earlier cut did not stop the slide. Traders now want to know whether a smaller flow of new tokens will show up on the chart.

NEAR Holders Approve a Second Issuance Cut in Two Months

Ternullo argues that NEAR's token issuance has been too high and creates unnecessary selling pressure.

NEAR governance has now ratified his proposal, HSP-029. It lowers the network's maximum annual issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%. The vote closed on Nov. 2 with 99.96% support and no votes against.

Ratification followed a 14-day review by the House of Stake Security Council, which ended without a veto. NEAR announced the result on Nov. 16.

The change will not hit at once. It takes effect one quarter after ratification and requires a validator protocol upgrade. After that, the ceiling steps down by about 3.75 basis points per month. The split of new tokens stays the same, with 90% going to stakers and 10% to the treasury.

Ternullo named no price target and no date. The fair test is whether selling pressure actually eases.

The Author Behind Both Supply Votes

In October 2025, governance lowered the maximum from 5% to the level that HSP-029 now replaces. The available record does not name Ternullo as the author of that earlier proposal.

NEAR kept falling after the October change. By Nov. 18, the token was down about 33% over a month.

About 32,000 Fewer Tokens a Day Against $579M of Trading

Once fully in place, the cap cuts daily issuance from about 89,517 NEAR to 57,291. That removes roughly 32,000 tokens a day, worth about $107,000 at today's price near $3.32.

The figure is small against trading activity. Daily volume on Nov. 18 was about $579 million, so the saved supply equals less than a fiftieth of 1% of it.

Over two years, the cut prevents about 11.8 million NEAR. That was worth near $39.9 million at the Nov. 18 price. The sum equals about 1% of NEAR's market cap. Over six years, the total reaches 66.1 million tokens.

For the market to confirm the effect, price must first reclaim the 50-day average near $3.91. That level sits about 18% above today's price.

Sellers Still Hold the Chart Below $3.81

NEAR Protocol (NEAR) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

NEAR slipped about 2% over the past day and is down about 7% for the week. The monthly loss shows how hard sellers have pressed since October.

The trend picture is mixed. Price sits under the 50-day line, which acts as a ceiling. It still holds above the 200-day average near $3.02, which marks the floor of the longer trend.

Momentum gives buyers little to work with. RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads about 39. That sits below the neutral zone and points to weak demand. MACD remains below its signal line, so momentum still points down. Trend strength gauges show sellers in charge.

On the daily chart, the first resistance sits near $3.81, with the next near $4.28. Support comes in near $2.73, then around $2.21 if that level breaks.

Talos integrated NEAR Intents for its institutional clients on Nov. 9. That could bring new demand, though the chart shows no sign of it yet.

What Would Prove Him Right, or Wrong

Ternullo's case gets its first real test once the validator upgrade switches the lower cap on. A daily close above the first resistance level after that point would suggest the supply cut is easing selling, as he argued.

A break below the 200-day average while issuance is already falling would undo it. That would show sellers still in charge despite fewer new tokens.

Staking is the side gauge. Estimated yields drop from 5.27% to 3.37%. More than half of supply already sits unstaked, and a rise in that share would add liquid tokens.

title: Former Robinhood Engineer Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud Over Hyperliquid Insider Trades
description:
A former Robinhood software engineer is admitting to wire fraud after misusing confidential information about upcoming crypto listings to trade perpetual futures on Hyperliquid and profiting over $125,000.
The post Former Robinhood Engineer Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud Over Hyperliquid Insider Trades appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
A former software engineer at a popular crypto trading app is pleading guilty to wire fraud after secretly using inside knowledge of upcoming token listings to trade derivatives on a decentralized platform.

The U.S. Department of Justice says Huaisong “Jerry” Xiang, 30, of Jersey City, New Jersey, worked on listing new digital assets and had access to nonpublic plans as a designated “Coin Aware Individual” via a private Slack channel.

Xiang repeatedly bought perpetual futures ahead of Robinhood’s public announcements between around March 2025 and February 2026 on Hyperliquid (HYPE), a decentralized platform for such contracts that do not expire.

“On each occasion, XIANG possessed material nonpublic information that Robinhood would list the cryptocurrency token on Robinhood Crypto, and XIANG traded on that information in breach of the duties that XIANG owed to Robinhood to maintain the confidentiality of this information.”

As part of the plea, he agreed to forfeit the full $125,523 in illicit profits, with sentencing set for February 25th, 2027, and a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.

Says US Attorney Jamie McDonald,

“No matter the trading platform, corporate insiders will be held accountable when they trade based on misappropriated information. As he has now admitted, Huaisong Xiang misused his employer’s confidential business information for his personal benefit. Over the course of a year, Xiang repeatedly traded in the derivatives market in advance of Robinhood’s public announcements.”

The case, handled by the SDNY Securities and Commodities Fraud Task Force with FBI assistance, highlights enforcement against insider trading even on decentralized crypto platforms.

title: Vitalik Buterin Wants Crypto to Have Housing’s Stability, But Can Ethereum Deliver?
description:
Vitalik Buterin wants digital assets to offer housing-like stability, but can Ethereum roadmap help ETH become a long-term investment?
The post Vitalik Buterin Wants Crypto to Have Housing’s Stability, But Can Ethereum Deliver? appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin believes younger generations investing in stocks and digital assets instead of housing could help ease pressure on property prices. However, he says crypto still needs something that makes housing attractive: stability.

Buterin thinks that housing creates incentives for owners to keep property prices high, even when cheaper homes would benefit society. Digital assets could offer an alternative, but today’s platforms often encourage excessive speculation.

“We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets,” Buterin wrote on X

His comments raise a question for Ethereum. Can the network evolve beyond speculative trading and become dependable infrastructure for people building long-term digital wealth?

Ethereum Roadmap Targets the Stability Vitalik Buterin Wants

Ethereum’s development roadmap increasingly focuses on making the network faster, more efficient, and harder to disrupt. Its next major upgrade, Glamsterdam, is currently undergoing devnet testing, with a mainnet launch expected in Q4 2026. The upgrade introduces several changes designed to improve Ethereum’s capacity without sacrificing decentralization.

One major feature is Enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation (ePBS). It moves the relationship between block proposers and builders directly into Ethereum’s protocol, reducing reliance on external relays and additional trust assumptions.

Another important development is Block-Level Access Lists. The feature prepares Ethereum to process unrelated transactions in parallel rather than handling everything sequentially.

These improvements could help Ethereum support more financial applications while keeping its infrastructure accessible to independent node operators. So, if digital assets are expected to become long-term financial instruments rather than vehicles for short-term speculation, this is very much needed.

Ethereum also provides an established foundation for staking, stablecoins, decentralized lending, and tokenized real-world assets. These applications could give investors more ways to hold and use digital wealth without constantly trading volatile tokens.

Yet, security, reliable applications, and responsible financial products must develop alongside network capacity.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

ETH Price Struggles to Reflect Ethereum’s Long-Term Ambitions

Ethereum (ETH)
24h7d30d1yAll time

Ethereum’s market performance presents a contrasting picture. ETH is trading just a notch above $1,800. This leaves the coin 63% below its all-time high of $4,946. The decline highlights the gap between Ethereum’s technological ambitions and its current market valuation.

Ethereum’s network utility and ETH’s investment performance are also not interchangeable. More applications and transactions can strengthen the ecosystem, but they do not create proportional demand for ETH.

The token still plays an important role as Ethereum’s native transaction currency, staking asset, and collateral across decentralized finance. For this reason, continued growth in staking, stablecoins, and tokenized assets could strengthen ETH’s underlying investment narrative.

Buterin’s comments are bigger than a debate about housing affordability. He is effectively challenging the crypto industry to build assets and platforms that encourage long-term ownership rather than constant speculation.

Ethereum has several pieces of that foundation already, including proof-of-stake security, smart contracts, and an expanding financial ecosystem.

Its upcoming upgrades aim to improve the infrastructure supporting those applications. But the network still needs to prove that its technology can deliver dependable financial products at scale.
