title: World Bank Turns To Crypto: Citi And Circle Explore USDC For Global Payments
description: The World Bank Group is taking another significant step toward blockchain-based finance, announcing a new collaboration with banking giant Citi and stablecoin issuer Circle to explore how USDC could transform international development payments. The initiative comes as Ethereum attracts growing Wall Street interest, with major financial institutions increasingly examining blockchain technology for settlement, tokenization, and […]
fullContent:
The World Bank Group is taking another significant step toward blockchain-based finance, announcing a new collaboration with banking giant Citi and stablecoin issuer Circle to explore how USDC could transform international development payments.

The initiative comes as Ethereum attracts growing Wall Street interest, with major financial institutions increasingly examining blockchain technology for settlement, tokenization, and cross-border transactions.

Announced on November 17, the World Bank’s latest initiative will investigate whether regulated, dollar-backed stablecoins can reduce transaction costs, accelerate payments, and improve transparency when development funds are distributed internationally.

Although the project remains exploratory, the involvement of one of the world’s largest development institutions could represent an important milestone for stablecoin adoption.

World Bank Explores USDC Payments With Citi And Circle

According to the official World Bank announcement, the institution will work with Citi and Circle to examine how blockchain-based payment infrastructure could complement its existing international banking arrangements.

Under the proposed model, Citi would provide access to established banking networks, while Circle would contribute the technology required to issue and settle payments using USDC.

The objective is not to eliminate traditional banks, but to explore whether stablecoins can make existing payment systems more efficient.

Currently, international development payments often move through correspondent banking networks involving multiple financial institutions. These arrangements can introduce delays, additional costs, and operational complexity.

Blockchain-based settlement could potentially simplify parts of this process by allowing funds to move across participating networks with greater visibility.

World Bank President Ajay Banga emphasized that improving payment efficiency could have practical consequences for development projects.

Faster transfers could help ensure that essential funding reaches communities when it is needed, rather than being delayed by traditional settlement processes.

Importantly, the announcement does not confirm that the World Bank has begun distributing development funds through USDC. No specific launch date, payment volume, or participating blockchain has been disclosed.

Circle CEO Calls World Bank Initiative A Major Step Forward

Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire welcomed the announcement, highlighting its potential to make global financial infrastructure more accessible.

In a November 17 post on X, Allaire described the collaboration as an important development for the future of international payments.

Allaire’s comments reflect a broader industry argument that blockchain-based dollars could become increasingly useful outside cryptocurrency trading.

For Circle, the World Bank initiative could also strengthen USDC’s position as financial institutions evaluate regulated stablecoins for real-world applications.

Rather than focusing exclusively on trading activity, USDC could potentially support institutional payments, treasury management, and international fund distribution.

The collaboration also builds on the World Bank’s existing blockchain experience.

Its FundsChain platform currently supports the tracking of funds associated with more than 350 development projects across 96 countries.

This infrastructure already allows participating organizations to monitor how project funds are used, demonstrating that blockchain technology has applications beyond cryptocurrency markets.

Could Ethereum Benefit From The World Bank’s Crypto Expansion?

The World Bank’s latest initiative could have implications for the broader blockchain industry, particularly networks that support stablecoin transactions.

Ethereum remains an important part of this ecosystem, supporting USDC transfers, decentralized financial applications, and tokenized assets.

As Bitcoinist previously reported, institutional and business-related transactions account for a substantial portion of Ethereum’s stablecoin transfer volume.

This suggests that blockchain-based dollars are increasingly being used for financial activity beyond individual cryptocurrency transfers.

The World Bank’s exploration could reinforce this trend by encouraging additional institutions to consider blockchain settlement infrastructure.

However, the announcement does not identify Ethereum as the network selected for the proposed payment model.

USDC operates across multiple blockchains, meaning Ethereum, Solana, and other compatible networks could potentially compete for future institutional payment activity.

The implications for ETH would therefore depend on whether Ethereum is eventually selected and whether the initiative generates sustained network usage.

Nevertheless, the development strengthens the broader argument that programmable blockchain infrastructure could play an increasingly important role in global finance.

Traditional Banks Are Moving Closer To Blockchain Payments

The collaboration also reflects a wider transformation taking place across traditional banking.

Financial institutions are increasingly exploring ways to combine established regulatory and payment infrastructure with blockchain settlement capabilities.

As Bitcoinist recently highlighted, PNC Bank has introduced USDC payment capabilities for eligible corporate clients using Ethereum infrastructure.

The development demonstrates how banks are beginning to incorporate stablecoins into services designed for businesses and institutional customers.

Citi’s participation in the World Bank initiative represents another example of this growing interest.

The bank operates across more than 180 jurisdictions, giving it extensive experience managing international payment networks.

Connecting that infrastructure with Circle’s stablecoin technology could provide an opportunity to examine how conventional banking and blockchain settlement might work together.

However, several challenges remain, including regulatory compliance, currency conversion, liquidity management, and the practical costs of moving funds between traditional accounts and blockchain networks.

These considerations will help determine whether stablecoins can deliver meaningful advantages over existing payment systems.

What Happens Next For USDC And Institutional Crypto Adoption?

The World Bank’s announcement represents an encouraging development for the cryptocurrency industry’s long-term integration with traditional finance.

Rather than treating blockchain exclusively as a speculative technology, major financial institutions are increasingly examining its potential to solve operational problems.

The initial exploration will focus on payment models involving intermediary financial institutions and borrower countries where digital asset activity is legally permitted.

Additional banking partners could eventually become involved as the initiative develops.

We believe the most important question is whether this collaboration can demonstrate measurable improvements in settlement speed, costs, and transparency.

If successful, the approach could encourage other international organizations and financial institutions to investigate similar infrastructure.

For now, the World Bank’s decision to explore USDC alongside Citi and Circle offers another indication that stablecoins are moving closer to mainstream financial applications.

The next milestones will be the announcement of participating countries, specific payment arrangements, and any confirmed implementation timeline.

The launch combines Android’s global reach with TRON’s leading role in the stablecoin ecosystem, expanding mobile access to onchain savings opportunities that are not accessible on traditional savings apps. With support for USDT on TRON, eligible users in supported jurisdictions can now deposit USDT on TRON and start earning yield on their savings.

 

Android’s extensive global footprint offers a significant distribution opportunity for digital asset applications, particularly in markets where stablecoins are used for payments, remittances, and savings. TRON provides an established infrastructure for this opportunity, with more than $94 billion in circulating USDT, the largest circulating supply of Tether’s dollar-pegged stablecoin among blockchain networks. TRON also supports a broad range of stablecoin use cases, including payments, cross-border transfers, and digital asset transactions.

 

Aave is building the World’s Savings App, a simple, globally accessible tool designed to help people grow and manage their savings, with a delightful design experience on the surface and powerful onchain finance infrastructure working under the hood. Users of the app can earn yield on their savings, enjoy flexible access to their funds, and benefit from the Balance Protection program. They can also deposit and withdraw via stablecoins or banks in eligible countries and project their potential savings growth over the years with a future simulator. Following its availability on iOS, the Android launch expands the app’s mobile reach, while TRON support connects users to one of the largest USDT ecosystems in onchain finance.

 

“Aave Labs has a proven track record of building leading DeFi products, and the Aave App brings that expertise to everyday users,” said Justin Sun, Founder of TRON. “With TRON support on Android and iOS, more people can use the USDT they already hold on TRON to access simple, accessible onchain savings with the Aave App.”

 

“Millions of people in emerging economies already rely on stablecoins on TRON to save and send money,” said Stani Kulechov, Founder and CEO of Aave Labs. “The Aave App lets them earn on those dollars.”

 

By enabling USDT deposits through the Aave App on Android, the integration connects TRON’s established stablecoin ecosystem with a consumer-focused mobile application. The launch reflects the continued convergence of mobile applications and blockchain infrastructure, as consumer-focused products work to make digital assets and decentralized financial services more accessible worldwide.

 

About TRON DAO

TRON DAO is a community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet via blockchain technology and dApps.

 

Founded in September 2017, the TRON blockchain has experienced significant growth since its MainNet launch in May 2018. Today, TRON hosts the largest circulating supply of USD Tether (USDT) stablecoin, which currently exceeds $94 billion. As of November 2026, the TRON blockchain has recorded over 414 million in total user accounts, more than 16 billion in total transactions, and over $24 billion in total value locked (TVL), based on TRONSCAN. Recognized as the global settlement layer for stablecoin transactions and everyday purchases with proven success, TRON is “Moving Trillions, Empowering Billions.”

 

TRONNetwork | TRONDAO | X | YouTube | Telegram | Discord | Reddit | GitHub | Medium | Forum

Aave Labs is a core contributor in the Aave network and builds products that make saving, lending and borrowing simple and accessible worldwide. Aave is the world’s largest onchain lending network, with more than $30 billion in net deposits. Users, fintechs and financial institutions use it to earn interest on stablecoins and other assets and to borrow against them, 24/7, with every transaction visible onchain. The network is governed by the Aave DAO, where AAVE holders vote on changes to the network and its treasury.

 

Aave Labs’ products include Aave App, a savings app for everyone; Aave Pro, for advanced lending and borrowing; Aave Kit, which lets fintechs and businesses offer savings and loans to their users; and Aave Horizon, an institutional platform for borrowing stablecoins against tokenized real-world assets. fullContent:
Bitcoin price is still under pressure, trading below $65,000. The latest institutional development, however, comes from the stablecoin market. The World Bank Group is exploring Circle’s USDC with Citi to move development funds through blockchain-based payment infrastructure.

The 82-year-old institution wants to determine if regulated stablecoins can make international disbursements faster, cheaper, and more transparent. Its proposed arrangement combines Circle’s USDC settlement infrastructure with Citi’s established banking connections. The initiative builds on FundsChain, the World Bank’s existing blockchain platform covering more than 350 projects across 96 countries.

The announcement arrives as Bitcoin price struggles to recover from a sharp market correction. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded another $239.9 million in net outflows yesterday. Yet institutional adoption of blockchain-based dollar payments continues to expand.

Now, will the growing movement of dollars onto blockchain rails eventually provide another source of liquidity for Bitcoin?

Market Cap

DISCOVER: 15+ Best Crypto IPO to Watch in 2026

World Bank Turns to Circle’s USDC for Global Payments

The World Bank Group announced its exploration last night, bringing together two major financial infrastructure providers. Circle will provide the stablecoin infrastructure to mint and settle funds in USDC. Citi will connect those transactions with established correspondent banking networks.

CONFIRMED: The World Bank Group is exploring CRYPTO dollars to pay out its funds, using Circle's $USDC with Citi.

The 82-year-old lender will test whether USDC can move development money faster and cheaper than today's bank-to-bank transfers.

Its blockchain platform FundsChain… pic.twitter.com/Yz9bGObXQ8

— Coin Bureau (@coinbureau) November 18, 2026

The objective is to improve how development financing reaches governments, businesses, and local projects. Traditional international payments often involve multiple banking intermediaries, processing windows, and settlement delays. Blockchain-based settlement could reduce some of these obstacles through faster transaction processing.

Citi says its network connects clients across more than 180 jurisdictions. The bank wants to deliver 24/7 payment capabilities, allowing critical funds to move in real time. Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire also described development finance as an important application for internet-native money.

“Circle is building the infrastructure for an internet-native financial system, and development finance is one of its most important applications.” – Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire

The initiative builds on FundsChain, which already provides transparency across the World Bank’s development projects. Its digital ledgers allow participating parties to track how project funds are used. The platform currently covers more than 350 projects across 96 countries.

The potential scale is considerable. The World Bank Group delivered $123.5 billion in loans, grants, equity investments, and guarantees during fiscal 2026. Its latest exploration could eventually introduce stablecoin settlement into a substantial institutional financial network.

However, the initial exploration will involve borrower countries where digital assets are permitted. The World Bank also plans an intermediated and interoperable payment model, connecting blockchain infrastructure with conventional banking systems.

DISCOVER: 15+ Upcoming Coinbase Listings to Watch in 2026

Bitcoin Price Could Benefit From Expanding Dollar Liquidity

USDC has become one of the most important dollar-denominated assets circulating across blockchain networks. Circle reported an average USDC circulation of $73.3 billion during Q3 2026. Its on-chain transaction volume reached $13.9 trillion, representing 49% annual growth.

Circle’s latest earnings presentation also showed USDC accounting for 79% of stablecoin transaction volume. That figure compares with its 27% share of stablecoin supply. The difference highlights how frequently USDC moves across blockchain-based financial applications.

This matters because stablecoins provide much of the dollar liquidity used throughout crypto markets. Traders use USDC to enter positions, move capital between exchanges, and settle transactions. Greater institutional adoption could expand the infrastructure supporting these activities.

Bitcoin remains the largest crypto and a major destination for digital asset capital. More accessible stablecoin infrastructure could make it easier for institutions and market participants to move dollars into crypto markets. That creates a potential second-order benefit for Bitcoin price and liquidity.

The timing is interesting given the current market conditions. Bitcoin price is hovering below $65,000, while US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $239.9 million in withdrawals on November 17. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for $209.5 million of those outflows.

The contrast between weakening Bitcoin demand and expanding institutional stablecoin infrastructure raises an interesting question. Could the next phase of cryptocurrency liquidity come from traditional financial institutions moving dollars onto blockchain rails?

title: Ripple (XRP) Price Flashes Incredibly Rare Signals: is a Rebound Coming?
description: XRP’s prolonged downturn has pushed its price into territory that we haven’t seen since 2024. That said, some of the more interesting market indicators suggest that the selling pressure might just be about to reach a turning point. The token recently recorded its lowest weekly close in two years at about $0.97. This extended its […]
fullContent:
XRP’s prolonged downturn has pushed its price into territory that we haven’t seen since 2024. That said, some of the more interesting market indicators suggest that the selling pressure might just be about to reach a turning point.

The token recently recorded its lowest weekly close in two years at about $0.97. This extended its correction, which has wiped out more than 70% of its value since the peak reached in July 2025.

XRP Traders Retreat as Leverage Collapses: What Does it Mean?

As we reported earlier, XRP’s estimated leverage ratio on Binance has fallen to about 0.13, which is the lowest level we’ve seen since November 2024.

Moreover, futures open interest on the exchange has declined to about $325 million, compared to $1.5 billion earlier this year.

What this tells us is that the sharp reduction in speculative positioning could help ease volatility that’s driven mostly by liquidations, although it doesn’t necessarily signal an immediate recovery.

Can XRP’s Price Reclaim $1?

From a technical standpoint, indicators paint a picture that’s rather mixed. XRP’s daily relative strength index (RSI) recently entered deeply oversold territory. Normally, this would suggest that there might be a short-term relief rally around the corner.

However, the $1 level has now turned into an important technical and psychological resistance. This means that in order to improve sentiment, traders need to push the price above it and keep it there convincingly.

On the other hand,  another rejection might expose the PA to the recent low at $0.89 once again.

For now, though, XRP’s next move seems largely dependent on whether or not buyers will return before the broader bearish sentiment resumes.

title: Bitcoin Buyers Add 66,000 BTC During Market Sell-Off — Is A Major Reversal Coming?
description: Bitcoin investors may be witnessing an important shift beneath the surface as new on-chain data reveals that buyers accumulated approximately 66,000 BTC during just two days of intense market selling. While the recent correction pushed Bitcoin toward $62,000 and triggered widespread liquidations, the latest figures suggest that some investors have been taking advantage of lower […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin investors may be witnessing an important shift beneath the surface as new on-chain data reveals that buyers accumulated approximately 66,000 BTC during just two days of intense market selling. While the recent correction pushed Bitcoin toward $62,000 and triggered widespread liquidations, the latest figures suggest that some investors have been taking advantage of lower prices.

As Bitcoinist previously reported, Bitcoin’s latest decline intensified market uncertainty, but new on-chain evidence suggests that the selling pressure may have attracted substantial demand near important technical support levels.

According to a new Glassnode report, Bitcoin’s recent sell-off has produced conditions historically associated with important market turning points. However, the most interesting development may not be the losses themselves, but the substantial buying activity taking place at critical support levels.

Bitcoin Accumulation Accelerates As Investors Absorb Selling Pressure

Glassnode’s November 17 research, titled Capitulation Meets Support, highlights a significant concentration of Bitcoin purchases between $62,000 and $66,000.

This region represents approximately 20% of the Bitcoin supply held by short-term investors. More importantly, the amount of BTC associated with this cost-basis range increased by roughly 66,000 coins during the two heaviest days of selling.

The figures suggest that buyers were willing to absorb substantial selling pressure even as market sentiment deteriorated.

Glassnode also reported that realized losses had reached levels previously observed near important Bitcoin market lows in 2018, 2020, 2022, and early 2023.

The analytics firm highlighted these developments in a November 17 post on X, pointing to the unusual combination of capitulation, leverage liquidations, and emerging support.

The latest findings raise an important question: could this accumulation represent the early stages of a more sustainable Bitcoin recovery?

Historically, sharp corrections accompanied by extreme realized losses have sometimes created opportunities for stronger buyers to accumulate coins from investors exiting their positions.

However, accumulation within a price range does not necessarily prove that long-term holders or whales were responsible for the purchases.

Why The $62,000–$66,000 Bitcoin Support Zone Matters

Bitcoin’s latest correction has placed the market near an important technical region.

Glassnode’s research suggests that the $62,000–$66,000 region could now play a decisive role in determining Bitcoin’s next direction.

A sustained move above $66,000 would provide an encouraging indication that buyers are regaining control of the immediate support region.

However, the more important recovery target sits near $74,100, which Glassnode identifies as the average acquisition price of Bitcoin’s short-term holders.

Reclaiming this level could improve sentiment by allowing a larger portion of recent buyers to return to breakeven.

Conversely, a daily close below $62,000 could expose Bitcoin to additional selling pressure, with $58,500 and $53,700 emerging as potential downside reference levels.

Institutional Demand Could Determine Bitcoin’s Next Move

Although the latest accumulation data provides an encouraging signal, broader institutional demand remains an important consideration.

Glassnode reported that US spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced approximately $2.6 billion in net outflows during the ten trading sessions ending November 13.

As Bitcoinist recently highlighted, BlackRock’s IBIT subsequently attracted $76.5 million on November 16, ending an extended withdrawal streak.

This creates an interesting contrast between investors accumulating Bitcoin near technical support and the broader institutional market, where capital flows have remained inconsistent.

The latest activity also follows a period of substantial withdrawals from cryptocurrency investment products. Previous Bitcoin ETF outflows demonstrated how institutional selling can influence market sentiment and short-term price movements.

Another development worth monitoring is the reduction in leveraged positions. Glassnode found that November 13 and 14 produced some of the largest long-liquidation events relative to open interest since 2023.

While these liquidations contributed to Bitcoin’s decline, they also removed some of the excessive leverage that can amplify market volatility.

Could Bitcoin Be Preparing For A Recovery?

Bitcoin’s latest on-chain signals present a potentially constructive development despite the challenging market environment.

The addition of approximately 66,000 BTC to a heavily defended support region suggests that meaningful demand emerged during one of the market’s most difficult periods.

Meanwhile, historical capitulation indicators and the removal of excessive leverage offer reasons to monitor the possibility of a market stabilization phase.

Nevertheless, a sustainable recovery will likely require more than accumulation alone.

We believe Bitcoin’s ability to defend $62,000, recover above $66,000, and eventually challenge $74,100 will provide important clues about whether buyers can establish a stronger foundation.

For now, the latest Glassnode findings suggest that Bitcoin’s recent correction has not eliminated investor demand. Instead, the sell-off has created a closely watched contest between sellers exiting their positions and buyers willing to accumulate at lower prices.

title: 4 Things NVIDIA’s Latest Earnings Reveal About the Future of AI
description: Here are some of the most important takeaways from NVIDIA's latest earnings call.
fullContent:
NVIDIA’s latest earnings offer an interesting snapshot of the current state of the artificial intelligence industry and its rapid expansion. At the same time, though, it raises certain questions about how sustainable the current pace of investment will be in the short- to mid-term future.

Following the company’s fiscal third-quarter results published on November 17, here are five key takeaways to consider.

AI Spending Continues to Accelerate

First things first, the firm reported Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, representing a whopping 103% increase compared to the same period last year and a 20% increase from Q2 2026.

The figure suggests that major tech companies continue allocating considerable resources to AI development, even as questions persist about the profitability of these investments.

That said, strong demand for computing hardware doesn’t necessarily mean that businesses that deploy AI will generate the returns needed to justify their spending. This is an important distinction that remains quite central to concerns about a potential AI investment bubble.

Data Centers Remain the Primary Growth Engine

The company’s data center division generated $107.6 billion in quarterly revenue, which accounts for about 93% of its total sales.

This reflects the continued investment in computing infrastructure required to train and operate increasingly sophisticated AI models.

Nonetheless, the concentration creates serious exposure to shifts in spending among major cloud providers and other large customers.

In other words, if companies start slowing their infrastructure expansion or reassess AI budgets, the growth of NVIDIA could face pressure. For now, however, the latest figures indicate that such a slowdown has yet to materialize in its reported sales.

Growth Expectations Remain Elevated

Here is where things get a bit more exciting. The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of about $130 billion, which exceeds the expectations of analysts and suggests that management anticipates more demand for its products.

One thing that’s becoming increasingly important is Nvidia’s Vera Rubin – a next-gen computing platform that’s a very important part of the product strategy as customers seek greater processing capacity and more efficiency.

Of course, higher revenue forecasts also mean more challenges: maintaining growth against increasingly demanding comparisons.

Leadership Uncertainty Matters More Than Some May Have Expected

And unless you’ve been completely isolated from the world of technology and finance, for that matter, you must be aware of the fact that the firm’s founder and CEO (since inception), Jensen Huang, resigned on November 12, introducing massive leadership challenges and a transition during a period of otherwise rapid business expansion.

The firm is now overseen and led by interim CEO Colette Kress (former CFO) and faces growing operational complexity.

The stock price tumbled on the news of Huang’s resignation and the broader controversy that unraveled around him, suggesting that financial performance alone isn’t enough to resolve questions surrounding longer-term leadership challenges.

What this means is that investors are likely going to focus on the firm’s succession plans, execution of its product roadmap, as well as its ability to maintain its relationships with major partners and customers.

fullContent:
Billionaire Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway has sold most of its Capital One (COF) stake in just two quarters.

The conglomerate held 1,150,000 Capital One (COF) shares on September 30th, down from 7,150,000 on March 31st, reports Yahoo Finance.

Berkshire cut the stake to 3,000,000 COF shares in the second quarter, then to 1,150,000 in the third.

Over six months, 6,000,000 COF shares were sold, or 83.9% of the position.

The firm unloaded 1,850,000 COF shares in the third quarter, which were worth about $357 million at the September 30th price of $193.07.

The remaining shares were worth about $222 million, or 0.07% of the firm’s $304.20 billion portfolio, according to Berkshire’s latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Berkshire also trimmed Bank of America (BAC) by 5.7% in the third quarter to 455,860,908 BAC shares, a sale worth about $1.5 billion.

Meanwhile, the conglomerate’s American Express (AXP) stake did not change.

The 13F filing shows holdings as of September 30th and says nothing about trades since then.

Berkshire filed it on Monday, November 16th.

Greg Abel has run Berkshire as chief executive since the start of 2026, after Warren Buffett stepped down at the end of 2025.

The filing does not say who made each trade.

Capital One is a major US credit card issuer and bank.

  • Four Democratic senators challenged the SEC’s tokenized-stock trading exemption in a new letter.
  • Their concerns include wallet-to-wallet transfers, AML checks, pricing and issuer protections.
  • The letter seeks clarification and oversight; it does not itself revoke the exemption.

Four Democratic US senators have pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission for answers about how its new approach to tokenized stock trading will protect investors and prevent illicit transfers. Their November 16 letter, reported by The Block, takes aim at gaps they see in the SEC’s five-year innovation exemption for certain trading venues. The development is an oversight challenge, not a court ruling or a notice that the exemption has been cancelled. It goes to a central difficulty for tokenized securities: a regulated purchase can become a blockchain transfer to another address.

What the exemption is intended to enable

The SEC introduced its approach in September, allowing qualifying tokenized-securities venues to operate under a defined exemption from some ordinary exchange-registration requirements. The aim is to permit experimentation with trading stocks in token form while the agency assesses a new market structure. A token representing a security still raises questions about ownership, trading rules and investor rights. The exemptions and their precise conditions matter more than a general statement that securities have moved on-chain. Not every blockchain token, broker or venue automatically qualifies for the same regulatory treatment.

The lawmakers’ main concern

Senators Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto reportedly told SEC Chair Paul Atkins that the framework lacks sufficiently specific safeguards around know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering procedures. A buyer verified by a regulated venue might later transfer a token to a wallet whose controller has not undergone the same checks. This problem is not solved merely by verifying the identity of the first purchaser. The letter asks how secondary transfers and the reach of compliance obligations would be managed once tokens circulate beyond the initial venue.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's developing licensing rules.

Investor pricing and issuer rights also feature

The senators raised concerns about retail-investor protections and pricing, and reportedly asked whether companies could opt out of having their shares tokenized. Those questions are distinct from financial-crime screening. A token that references equity needs a clear relationship to the rights and obligations of the underlying security, as well as fair information about execution and ownership. If an issuer’s wishes, the investor’s expectations and the platform’s legal structure do not line up, technical transferability alone cannot resolve the conflict. Policymakers must address those issues in enforceable terms.

What happens next

The lawmakers asked the SEC to explain its approach and urged a transparent rulemaking process for changes in the regulatory treatment of tokenized securities. Such a letter can affect oversight and public debate, especially as control of congressional committees changes, but it is not itself binding legislation. Venues exploring tokenized equities should continue to follow the actual exemption terms and any subsequent SEC guidance. The next concrete milestones are the agency’s response, proposed revisions if any, and how early trading models implement identity, custody and transfer restrictions.

A workable compromise, if one emerges, may turn on which transfers are allowed after a regulated initial sale. Some token designs can restrict transfers to approved addresses, while others rely on venue-level checks or additional intermediaries. Each model gives up something different in portability, privacy or market openness. The senators' concerns therefore reach beyond rhetorical support for or opposition to blockchains: they ask what compliance guarantees exist when a security is represented by a programmable token that can move outside its original trading environment.

For related context, see our earlier report on new institutional crypto-custody arrangements.

Tokenization can change how securities move, but it does not automatically settle which rules should accompany them. The dispute now concerns the design of that regulatory perimeter, with no basis to describe the senators’ letter as an immediate prohibition on tokenized stocks.

title: OKX-ICE Tokenized Stocks Lean on 6 Crypto Firms: Will Wall Street Ever Follow?
description:
OKX-ICE's tokenized stocks open Nov. 23 with only crypto firms from its original list. Will Wall Street ever follow?
The post OKX-ICE Tokenized Stocks Lean on 6 Crypto Firms: Will Wall Street Ever Follow? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
OKX-ICE, an OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) venture, opens tokenized stocks trading Nov. 23 after 56 of 62 targets objected. The six that did not are all crypto-linked, so no non-crypto name among the 62 has joined.

Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle, Strategy, Securitize, and BitGo are those six. Better.com and 59 Direxion exchange-traded funds also list, so single-stock access skews toward crypto-linked names. ICE owns the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

Is Wall Street’s Silence on Tokenized Stocks Turning Into Consent?

Not so far. Neither Apple nor Nvidia had objected in late October, per BeInCrypto’s earlier objection tally. However, both appear among objectors in Fortune‘s Nov. 5 count.

Objections on the original list rose from 30 in late October to 54 by Nov. 5, then 56 per Bloomberg.

Applied Optoelectronics, a networking equipment maker, filed an objection. It told Fortune that uncertainty over its stock’s pricing, liquidity, and volatility remained. It also feared investors would think it sponsored the offering.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg’s hosts flagged that 24/7 trading removes the breathing room companies relied on during the 2008 financial crisis.

Therefore, issuers may want evidence on pricing and liquidity before backing any venue.

Can Objectors Be Won Over, or Bypassed?

Objections apply venue by venue, so a company that blocks OKX-ICE must object again elsewhere.

In contrast, the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) clears and settles US equity trades. Its tokenization service needs no issuer approval and has 20 participants and 34 securities.

Nadine Chakar, DTCC’s managing director and global head of digital assets, tied the refusals to design. Under opt-out rules, silence enrolls a company. She said earlier issuer conversations might have changed the outcome.

Volume caps may also matter. Each token faces a ceiling of 0.25% of the underlying stock’s prior-month volume, per BeInCrypto’s OKX first-mover analysis. That could ease volatility concerns while limiting the venue’s reach.

The test after Nov. 23 is whether any large non-crypto issuer agrees to list. Until one does, tokenization may reach Wall Street through DTCC’s infrastructure before stock tokens do.

title: Ethereum’s Next Upgrade Could Let Callers Skip Payments
description:
Key Takeaways Caller gas limits can skip a 2.5% payment OP Stack withdrawals failed at the estimated gas EF estimate: […]
The post Ethereum’s Next Upgrade Could Let Callers Skip Payments appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • Caller gas limits can skip a 2.5% payment
  • OP Stack withdrawals failed at the estimated gas
  • EF estimate: 10,000–15,000 of 90 million contracts
  • Core developers weigh EIP-8037/8038 on November 19

The findings come from tests of EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, two gas-repricing proposals that led AllCoreDevs to pause the Hoodi testnet fork, according to the Ethereum Foundation’s November 6 update.

A Withdrawal That Pays Everyone but One

The clearest case comes from a proof-of-concept repository published under the GitHub account mejango and cited in the developer discussion. Its vault sends 2.5% of each withdrawal to a separate component contract inside a try block. If that payment reverts, the vault keeps the share and the user is paid anyway, a common way to stop one broken component from freezing every withdrawal.

The author ran the same call at gas limits from 30,000 to 900,000 using eth_simulateV1 on public RPC endpoints, once against Ethereum mainnet and once against Sepolia, which the repository says already applies Glamsterdam gas rules. Nothing was deployed. On mainnet, every limit either reverted the whole withdrawal or paid the component. Under Glamsterdam rules, a band roughly 112,000 gas wide completed the withdrawal and skipped the payment.

These are the author’s simulations. Coindoo has not reproduced them, and they do not describe an exploit of a live contract.

The Caller Chooses Which Outcome Happens

The outer gas limit is set by whoever calls the withdrawal. According to the repository, that turns the band into a lever: a caller can pick a limit inside it on purpose, making the component payment fail while the withdrawal itself goes through.

The vault has no way to respond. Its contracts are immutable, so logic written to tolerate a broken component now also tolerates a deliberately underfunded one. Under current mainnet rules the same attempt fails, because a limit too low to fund the component also leaves too little gas to finish, and the whole transaction reverts.

Why the Payment Fails but the Fallback Survives

Two proposals produce that result together. EIP-8038 raises the gas cost of reading and writing state, so a budget that used to cover the component’s work can now run out sooner. EIP-8037 separates the cost of creating new state from ordinary execution gas and raises it. Coindoo has covered what that means for onboarding costs.

The second change is what keeps the fallback alive. ChainSecurity’s October 13 analysis explains that state-creation charges are drawn from a separate pool that is restored when a call fails, and that a failed call’s state charges paid from regular gas go back to its caller. A contract can therefore have more gas left after a failure than it would today.

ChainSecurity’s worked example uses a write to a fresh storage slot. Under current rules it costs 22,100 gas, so a failure handler with about 15,000 gas left runs out and the transaction reverts. Under the reviewed Glamsterdam specification, the same write costs 12,100 execution gas, while a 97,920-gas state charge comes from the separate pool, leaving room for the write and a short continuation. The write is not cheaper overall; a different pool pays for the expensive part.

The vault scenario needs both effects: the component’s call fails earlier because work costs more, and the vault’s fallback completes because it no longer runs out of gas. A contract that counted on running out of gas to force a rollback can end in a different state. ChainSecurity limits that conclusion to specific call patterns, and most findings reported so far stem from the cost increases rather than the separate pool, according to the summary of the November 16 testing call.

READ MORE:

Grayscale Reveals ‘Compelling Entry Points’ but Data Says No

When the Default Gas Estimate Lands in the Gap

A higher fee per unit of gas changes nothing here, because price does not add units to an internal call. A higher gas limit does help in the vault example, since larger limits pay the component, but only when the software setting the limit chooses a large enough number. The repository’s second test shows what happens when it uses the standard estimate.

That test models an OP Stack withdrawal being finalized on Ethereum, using the real OptimismPortal2 and L1CrossDomainMessenger contracts. The message being delivered requests a fixed 375,000 gas. On mainnet, finalizing at the eth_estimateGas result of 931,416 delivered the message. Under Glamsterdam rules on Sepolia, finalizing at the estimate of 1,517,344 succeeded, but the messenger recorded the delivery as failed and the funds were not credited. Doubling the limit delivered it.

The repository presents that estimate as the one a wallet or relayer would send, so the user would have done nothing unusual. Recovery remains possible because the messenger lets anyone replay a failed message, but it takes a third, manual transaction and another gas payment. The two runs also used different messenger versions, 2.11.1 on mainnet and 2.13.0 on Sepolia, a difference the comparison does not isolate.

The two gas sweeps side by side

Vault withdrawal – current mainnet rules

  • 30,000–106,000: whole withdrawal reverts
  • 108,000–898,000: component paid

Vault withdrawal – Glamsterdam rules

  • 30,000–180,000: whole withdrawal reverts
  • 182,000–294,000: withdrawal succeeds, payment skipped
  • 296,000: reverts
  • 298,000–898,000: component paid

OP Stack finalization – mainnet

  • 400,000–900,000: reverts, retry later
  • 925,000–10,000,000: message delivered

OP Stack finalization – Glamsterdam rules

  • 400,000–1,000,000: reverts
  • 1,025,000–1,600,000: finalized, delivery recorded as failed
  • 1,625,000–10,000,000: message delivered

Glamsterdam results were simulated on Sepolia. OP Stack runs were pinned to a single L1 block.

What a Success Receipt Does Not Show

In both tests, the transaction receipt reports success. A receipt’s status covers only the outer call. It says nothing about whether a call caught inside a try block, or a message handed to a bridge messenger, did what it was meant to do.

Confirming that means checking the specific evidence: a balance change or event from the component in the vault case and, for OP Stack withdrawals, whether the messenger emitted RelayedMessage or FailedRelayedMessage. A bridge interface that marks a withdrawal “finalized” from the receipt alone can show a user a completed withdrawal before any funds arrive.

10,000-15,000 Contracts, and Who Can Fix Them

At the November 16 testing call, the Ethereum Foundation’s Marius estimated that around 10,000–15,000 out of roughly 90 million contracts would be affected, according to the meeting’s auto-generated summary. The summary does not explain how that figure, or a separate value-at-risk estimate of “a few hundred thousand dollars,” was produced. A contract count is not an application count, and an affected contract does not necessarily put funds at risk.

Auditors brought their own tallies to the same call. ChainSecurity reported 152 findings, rising to 200 when combined with the Foundation’s internal search. The summary describes most findings as easy to mitigate, with some requiring contract upgrades or redeployment.

Who can apply a fix depends on where the outdated gas assumption sits:

  • Wallets and RPC providers can change how they estimate gas, the layer behind the OP Stack result.
  • Applications with adjustable gas settings can raise those values and retest them.
  • Upgradeable contracts can ship a new implementation, usually after a governance vote.
  • Immutable contracts cannot be patched. Their options are a supported retry, an external workaround, moving users to a replacement contract, or a change to the protocol rules themselves.

That last group is why the issue sits with core developers rather than app teams alone, a compatibility question Coindoo examined in its earlier look at how the upgrade could change old contracts. The testing-call summary also assigns follow-up work with affected app teams, L2s and OP Stack chains, including testnet replays to find contracts not yet identified.

What the November 19 Call Can Settle

Core developers take up the findings at the November 19 execution-layer call. The Foundation says no decision is pre-committed for that meeting, while the testing-call summary lists deciding whether to proceed with EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 as the action item.

Options raised on November 16 included proceeding as planned, dropping the proposal, waiting for contract-size limit increases, and delaying. Those favouring the current plan pointed to the post-quantum roadmap, and one developer warned that dropping the proposal would prevent large contracts from being deployed. The Foundation’s update adds that several specification revisions are being prototyped, each documented for the problems it fixes and the other invariants it could break.

Hoodi stays unforked until that is resolved. The gas bands above describe the proposal as tested, and any revision to the specifications would change the rules those simulations ran against.

The post Ethereum’s Next Upgrade Could Let Callers Skip Payments appeared first on Coindoo.

fullContent:
Anthropic is heading toward one of Wall Street’s biggest IPOs, and Bitcoin’s price could face another battle for institutional capital. The Claude developer is preparing to list on Nasdaq under ticker ANT tomorrow, after setting an indicative price range of $70–$78 per share.

Demand is already running hot, with reports indicating the offering is six times oversubscribed, raising the prospect of an IPO price above the initial range. Yet Anthropic’s potential $64.35 billion share sale could become another major test of investor appetite for AI stocks.

The timing is difficult for Bitcoin. Nvidia has just delivered another blockbuster earnings report, reinforcing the scale of the AI investment boom.

Anthropic Price to Break Above $78 as IPO Demand Surges

Anthropic IPO prospectus puts 825 million shares on offer, with an indicative price range of $70–$78. At the upper end, the public offering could raise up to $64.35 billion.

The company is also arranging a separate $26 billion private placement involving major technology partners. Nvidia and Google have each committed $10 billion, with AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC participating. Combined, the IPO and private placement could bring Anthropic between $84.6 billion and $93.7 billion.

That makes the Anthropic price particularly important as investors prepare for Wednesday’s pricing decision. Six-times oversubscription suggests demand substantially exceeds the shares available.

A price above $78 would then again strengthen the signal that institutional buyers are willing to pay more for exposure to the AI industry. The anticipated November 19 debut could also produce another explosive first-day trading session.

Anthropic’s growth story helps explain the appetite. Its annualized revenue run rate reportedly reached $81 billion by October 31, while New Street Research projects revenue could exceed $500 billion by 2030.

Bitcoin Faces Another SpaceX IPO Liquidity Shock

Bitcoin has already suffered a substantial decline ahead of Anthropic’s debut. BTC fell 23% during the 50 days preceding Anthropic’s expected listing. That closely resembles the 19% decline during the 50 days before SpaceX began trading in June.

Yet, the SpaceX comparison becomes more interesting when examining what happened after its debut. SpaceX launched its record-breaking IPO at $135 per share on June 12. Shares closed their first trading session at $160.95, gaining 19.2%.

The stock subsequently climbed nearly 40% during its first week, briefly pushing its valuation above $2 trillion. Bitcoin did not collapse during the listing. It was trading around $63,500, remaining almost flat over 24 hours. Crypto markets eventually recovered alongside the wider risk-on move.

It was somewhat expected; a $64 billion public offering creates a substantial new destination for investors. So, even a small shift in portfolio allocations could matter when crypto liquidity is already under pressure.

Nvidia Earnings Beat Adds Another Liquidity Battle for Bitcoin

Nvidia has given the AI investment narrative another powerful boost. The chipmaker reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion, beating analyst expectations of $109.11 billion. Revenue increased 103% year over year, while its fourth-quarter revenue forecast reached $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. Nvidia shares gained 4% in extended trading following the results.

The earnings beat reinforces the investment case behind Anthropic’s IPO. AI infrastructure spending continues expanding, and investors have another opportunity to buy into that growth through public equity markets.

There is an interesting twist: Nvidia itself is committing $10 billion to Anthropic’s private placement. The same company delivering the latest earnings catalyst is helping finance one of the largest anticipated stock market debuts.

Anthropic’s debut is more than another technology listing. It could become a defining test of Bitcoin’s ability to compete for investor attention during the AI boom.

title: Binance Hack-Linked Wallet Moves 34,279 ETH, but Investigators See No Confirmed Sale
description: A wallet linked by blockchain investigators to the October 29 Binance breach has transferred 34,279.66 ETH to three newly created addresses, ending a period of.
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Investigators tracked 34,279.66 ETH from a Binance hack-linked address to three new wallets.
  • The movement was worth roughly $63 million at the reported market price.
  • No verified exchange deposit or executed sale had been established in the initial reports.

A wallet linked by blockchain investigators to the October 29 Binance breach has transferred 34,279.66 ETH to three newly created addresses, ending a period of inactivity. The ether was worth roughly $63 million at prices used in Tuesday’s reporting. That is a significant movement of suspected stolen funds, but a wallet transfer is not automatically a sale, a successful laundering step or proof that the recipient controls are independent of the sender. Investigators had not identified the new addresses as exchanges at the time of their initial reports.

The new transactions are visible on-chain

Monitoring groups MistTrack and Solid Intel reported the transfers on November 17. MistTrack described three movements of approximately 12,000 ETH, 12,000 ETH and 10,279.66 ETH. The receiving wallets were newly created, and the monitored funds had not moved again when the analysts published their findings. Public transaction records make it possible to trace the amounts and destinations, but they do not disclose the human operator behind each address. The link to the earlier breach rests on investigators’ attribution of the sending wallet, not a label embedded in the blockchain itself.

The wider breach remains unresolved

The October attack involved vastly larger losses than Tuesday’s movement. US investigators attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking group, and authorities have announced substantial asset restraints and seizures. Blockchain intelligence firms have also tracked funds moved through different assets and protocols. These parallel developments should not be added together casually, because frozen, seized, recovered and still-controlled amounts describe different legal and operational states. The fresh ETH transfers are one piece of a complex post-incident trail rather than an update to the full net-loss number.

For related context, see our earlier report on Coinbase's custody and security precautions.

Movement does not establish selling pressure

Crypto trading commentary sometimes treats any transfer from an exploit-linked wallet as preparation to dump tokens. That can happen, but the evidence here does not yet establish a market sale. Transfers may consolidate funds, redistribute control or precede another operation. Until an address is linked to a trading venue, bridge, mixer or other service, the immediate observable fact is the destination change. Even a later exchange deposit would need careful interpretation: deposits are not identical to executed sell orders. Reporting should preserve those steps rather than collapsing them into one dramatic conclusion.

Why transparency helps, and where it stops

Ethereum’s public ledger lets investigators monitor known addresses and alert service providers if assets reappear at identifiable points. Token issuers, exchanges and law enforcement may each have different powers depending on the assets and jurisdictions involved. Native ETH cannot simply be frozen by an issuer in the way some centrally administered tokens can. That difference complicates recovery when funds leave services that can intervene. The next useful evidence will be further movements, identification of services receiving the funds and official updates to the case.

Investigators can improve attribution confidence by comparing the sequence, amounts and transaction timing with addresses already associated with the incident. Yet public labels can be incomplete, and a newly created wallet may simply be another address controlled by the same actor. Readers should resist claims that funds have reached a criminal group, a particular country or a cash-out desk unless that identification is supported by additional evidence. Future investigative notices should specify their degree of confidence and distinguish observed transfers from hypotheses about their purpose.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet compromise.

The latest transfer warrants close monitoring, but it should not be reported as the disposal of $63 million in stolen ether without further proof. The distinction between observable transactions and inferred intent is especially important in a security incident of this scale.

Reporting sources: CoinDesk report of MistTrack and Solid Intel monitoring · MistTrack transfer report

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Crypto Had a $2 Billion Leverage Flush. Why Is US Stock Margin Debt Still Near Record?
description:
US margin debt fell 2.1% in October while crypto liquidations hit $2 billion in a day. Which market holds more unwind risk?
The post Crypto Had a $2 Billion Leverage Flush. Why Is US Stock Margin Debt Still Near Record? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
US margin debt fell just 2.1% in October to $1.45 trillion. Crypto exchanges, however, liquidated about $2 billion in leveraged positions within 24 hours last weekend.

Data from the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) show stock borrowing still sits 3.6% below June’s record of $1.50 trillion. In contrast, crypto traders have faced recurring liquidation waves, raising the question of whether stock borrowers face the same.

Why Has Stock Leverage Barely Budged While Crypto Cracked?

FINRA puts October margin debt, or money borrowed against holdings, at $1.45 trillion, down from $1.48 trillion in September. However, borrowing remains up $223 billion, or 18%, since December.

Brokers also hold about $423 billion in free credit balances, meaning uninvested customer cash. That works out to roughly $3.40 borrowed for every $1 of that cash.

Meanwhile, Coinglass data, cited by Bloomberg, recorded about $2 billion in crypto liquidations in the 24 hours through Sunday.

Long positions made up most of that total, with Bitcoin (BTC) at $774 million and Ethereum (ETH) at $488 million.

US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) also saw almost $3 billion in net outflows from Oct. 30 to Nov. 13.

Leverage had already become a key crash driver before the weekend flush, alongside rate-hike expectations.

Will November’s Margin Data Show Stocks Joining the Flush?

October’s reading predates last weekend’s liquidations, because FINRA measures balances on the last business day of each month. The November data, generally released in the third week of December, will therefore cover that selloff.

In July, margin debt fell $85 billion, the largest one-month drop on record, according to CMG. Borrowers then rebuilt $63 billion across August and September.

If that pattern repeats, stock leverage could stay near record while crypto positions keep shrinking. However, a crypto rebound or a sharp drop in November balances would weaken that read.

Otherwise, margin books could become a bigger forced-selling source than crypto exchanges, especially with December hike expectations in play.

title: Peter Schiff Has a New Candidate for the Next Financial Crisis. It’s Not Bitcoin
description:
Peter Schiff says AI is the subprime of the next financial crisis, arguing Fed tightening will deflate every bubble.
The post Peter Schiff Has a New Candidate for the Next Financial Crisis. It’s Not Bitcoin appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
“AI is the subprime of the next financial crisis,” economist Peter Schiff wrote on X. He expects it to dwarf the last crisis as the Federal Reserve withdraws easy money that inflated nearly every asset.

Subprime mortgages, the high-risk home loans at the center of the 2008 meltdown, are his template for AI stocks. Yet Nvidia (NVDA) just delivered record revenue, complicating the bubble case for Nasdaq holders facing another Fed hike.

Why Would Fed Tightening Hit Every Bubble at Once?

Schiff, chief economist at Euro Pacific Asset Management, says cheap Fed money pushed nearly every asset into a bubble. The unwind, in his view, follows the Fed’s retreat.

The Fed raised its benchmark rate to 3.75% to 4% in September, its first hike since 2023. Then it held steady in October by a 10-2 vote, with both dissenters favoring a hike.

Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, hotter than the 0.3% economists forecast. After the report, markets priced a December hike as a near certainty, with a half-point move at about 15% odds.

Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 is down about 9% over the past month.

Separately, Schiff has targeted crypto, urging Bitcoin (BTC) holders to sell in an earlier Bitcoin bubble warning.

Can Record AI Earnings Outrun a Rate Hike?

Nvidia’s fiscal third-quarter revenue hit $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. The fourth-quarter outlook, which includes an extra week, is $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

The results were also the first since CEO Jensen Huang resigned on November 12. That exit has sharpened questions about the AI boom’s future.

Gil Luria heads technology research at D.A. Davidson. He said in October that Nvidia’s ecosystem and chip demand could support growth through 2030. However, he warned that debt-heavy data-center builders may face serious pressure.

Still, Nvidia now carries $390 billion in purchase commitments and $118 billion in guarantees.

The Fed meets on December 8 and 9, a day before November inflation data arrives. That decision will test how much of the AI rally depends on cheap money.

The post Peter Schiff Has a New Candidate for the Next Financial Crisis. It’s Not Bitcoin appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Grayscale Says November Crypto Slump Reflects Stablecoin Exits and Tech-Sector Stress
description: Grayscale’s latest market note offers a two-part explanation for the sharp decline in crypto prices: money moving out of stablecoins and pressure spilling over from.
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Grayscale links crypto weakness to stablecoin off-ramping and pressure in AI-related equities.
  • Its analysis also highlights moving-average signals and leverage as possible amplifiers.
  • Its claim that prices offer attractive entry points is a manager’s opinion, not an established market outcome.

Grayscale’s latest market note offers a two-part explanation for the sharp decline in crypto prices: money moving out of stablecoins and pressure spilling over from technology equities. Head of research Zach Pandl argues that fundamental adoption trends remain intact, even while Bitcoin and other large assets struggle. That is the assessment of an asset manager with a commercial interest in digital assets, not a settled finding that the sell-off is over. Its value lies in examining the mechanisms rather than repeating the optimistic conclusion as fact.

Stablecoin supply is one signal

The November 16 research note points to accelerating withdrawals from stablecoins after the late-October Binance security incident. When investors redeem dollar-backed tokens for bank deposits, the supply of on-chain dollars can contract. That may reduce the liquidity available for trading and collateral, although it does not mean each redeemed dollar was about to buy Bitcoin. Other drivers can change supply, including arbitrage and issuer operations. Grayscale views off-ramping as one contributing factor to the November weakness. Confirming its influence requires tracking issuance, redemptions and market activity across venues.

AI-related equities may transmit risk

The firm also identifies pressure in Nvidia and other AI-linked stocks as a possible source of portfolio de-risking. Investors holding growth technology and crypto exposure may sell both when financing conditions worsen or their risk limits tighten. There is a further link through physical infrastructure: some Bitcoin mining firms are developing high-performance computing services for AI operators. Those connections do not make Bitcoin a direct claim on AI company earnings. They suggest overlapping investors and capital requirements through which stress can travel across otherwise different sectors.

For related context, see our earlier report on stablecoin supply contraction.

Technical selling can amplify the move

Grayscale notes that Bitcoin fell below its 200-day moving average on November 12, a level followed by some trend-oriented trading strategies. Leveraged positions and thinner weekend order books can make subsequent price moves more abrupt. Those mechanisms may amplify a decline without identifying a single fundamental cause. Importantly, technical signals are not universal commands: different funds use different models and time horizons, and a moving-average breach does not determine the market’s next direction. The research describes a chain of plausible forces, not a proven one-factor explanation.

What the bullish argument leaves open

Grayscale believes medium- and long-term investors may find current valuations attractive because institutional stablecoin and tokenization activity continues to develop. The note also acknowledges inflation, interest-rate uncertainty and geopolitical risk. Those headwinds could persist longer than optimistic scenarios assume. Readers should distinguish the factual observation of a significant drawdown from the manager’s valuation judgment. ETF flows, stablecoin supplies and changes in rates can help test the thesis, but none offers a reliable standalone timing signal.

Another test of the explanation is whether on-chain capital actually returns when equity-market stress eases. A rebound in technology shares accompanied by ongoing stablecoin redemptions would suggest the factors are not moving in lockstep. In contrast, renewed stablecoin issuance without a broader Bitcoin recovery would show that liquidity availability alone is insufficient. Such cross-checks are more informative than assigning every daily price move to the same narrative. They also allow readers to separate Grayscale's interpretation from the specific market data used to support it.

For related context, see our earlier report on recent bitcoin ETF outflows.

The report provides a framework for thinking about November’s crypto decline, not proof that prices have bottomed. Its strongest contribution is highlighting how stablecoin redemptions, shared growth-stock positioning and leveraged market structure can interact during a difficult month.

Reporting sources: Grayscale November 16 research note

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence on Nvidia Scandal, Says He Is Ready to Return as CEO
description: The Nvidia founder acknowledged his mistakes and expressed willingness to return, should the board decide it's the right move.
fullContent:
Jensen Huang has finally broken his silence following the controversy that led to his resignation as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12. He admitted to personal misconduct while also signaling that he would welcome an opportunity to lead the tech giant again.

In a statement that was published on X on Tuesday, Huang expressed his gratitude for the support that he had received and acknowledged his responsibility for the unfolding scandal.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” He said.

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I’ve never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

— Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang) November 17, 2026

Recall that the controversy started following revelations about extramarital relationships, including one reportedly involving a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. These allegations also raised concerns about potential violations of US chip export restrictions.

As CryptoPotato reported yesterday, the firm’s share price dropped by around 4% amid reports that the board was unwilling to reinstate Huang.

Odds of him returning currently circle around 10% on popular prediction market Kalshi, while these of Rene Haas becoming the next CEO of the company have increased to about 22%.

title: Cypherpunk Reports 8,967 ZEC Mined as Zcash Treasury Nears 342,000 Tokens
description: Publicly traded Cypherpunk Technologies has reported the first results from its Zcash mining operation, producing 8,967.29 ZEC in just 44 days. The company says those.
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Cypherpunk reported mining 8,967.29 ZEC during its first 44 operating days.
  • Its treasury reached about 341,859 ZEC after mining and purchases.
  • Operating earnings should be distinguished from large unrealized token-valuation gains.

Publicly traded Cypherpunk Technologies has reported the first results from its Zcash mining operation, producing 8,967.29 ZEC in just 44 days. The company says those tokens represented approximately $9.9 million of mining revenue in the third quarter, while its treasury later grew to about 341,859 ZEC through purchases and continued production. The figures are impressive in isolation. But investors need to separate operating earnings from accounting gains on an appreciated token reserve, especially after ZEC’s volatile price action.

Mining began only in August

Cypherpunk’s November 16 filing says the mining fleet began operation on August 18 and delivered about 95% uptime through September 30. The company reported revenue corresponding to 8,967.29 ZEC, with a stated average cost of mining revenue of approximately $104 per token before depreciation. Once depreciation of equipment is included, the company reported a higher per-token cost near $237. The distinction is crucial when comparing mining economics across companies because machines lose value over time even if their near-term power and hosting costs look low.

The treasury is larger than the quarter’s production

Cypherpunk says holdings reached around 341,858.75 ZEC after adding October mining output and recent market purchases, equivalent to roughly 2% of the circulating supply at its reporting date. Its strategy therefore combines an operating mining business with a substantial asset inventory. Both components are sensitive to the cryptocurrency’s price. Tokens generated through mining may be held rather than sold to cover expenses, which can expand exposure and affect cash needs. A higher coin count is not the same as higher spendable cash in the company’s bank accounts.

For related context, see our earlier report on the recent Zcash NU7 protocol upgrade.

The earnings split matters

The Block reported approximately $2.6 million of quarterly operating profit and substantially greater net income driven by unrealized increases in the value of the ZEC treasury. Valuation gains can be economically relevant, but they can also reverse without an operational change. Investors should read the quarterly income statement and cash-flow statement together. A business with rising book profits may still need external financing to buy new equipment or meet operating expenses if it is retaining mined tokens. The source of earnings determines how repeatable they are.

Network share and equipment expansion

The company says its fleet represented a material part of Zcash network hashrate at launch, while broader network competition has already changed that percentage. Management has discussed additional equipment purchases for 2027, subject to commitments and delivery. More hardware can produce more hashes, but miner returns depend on network difficulty, rewards, uptime, electricity and ZEC’s price. The most useful follow-up will compare actual production and operating cash with capital spent, rather than treating a treasury-size target as proof of long-term mining profitability.

Mining economics can shift even when a company executes its own operating plan well. As competitors add machines, a given fleet's fraction of network hashrate may fall, reducing expected token output at the same energy cost. Rewards also depend on protocol rules and equipment performance, while treasury purchasing introduces separate exposure to spot prices. Reporting those risks alongside current revenue helps readers understand why one profitable early period does not establish a permanent advantage. A full-year record will offer a stronger measure of the fleet's competitiveness.

For related context, see our earlier report on Bitcoin mining-difficulty changes.

Cypherpunk now has measurable mining output as well as a sizable ZEC balance. The challenge for investors is to value those as two connected but distinct businesses, avoiding the temptation to treat unrealized token appreciation as recurring operational income.

Reporting sources: Cypherpunk Q3 financial results, SEC exhibit · The Block coverage
