title: Beware: Over 178 Popular Websites Hit by Crypto-Stealing Malware
description: The malware targeted Apple devices too, loading Coruna and Darksword exploit chains based on the iOS version detected on each visit there.
fullContent:
Earlier today, Optimizely, an AI-powered marketing platform with thousands of large organizations as customers, announced that an attacker had used a vulnerability in the service to insert malicious code into scripts that some of those organizations use on their websites.

According to security reports, the code collected the card information of people who visited the affected websites and could also redirect their crypto payments to the attacker’s address.

Optimizely Project Code Became a Malware Delivery Route

In an update published on November 16, Report URI, which monitors scripts run by websites, said that after checking more than 1,600 Optimizely snippets, it found malicious code in 188 that were linked to 178 organizations, although the real figure could be higher.

These organizations included HSBC’s US and Hong Kong operations, Zoom, Salesforce, IKEA, and toy maker Mattel. Websites of news agencies such as CNN, Fox News, NPR, and the BBC were also affected, as were airlines, including Air France-KLM. You can find the full list of affected companies in the Report URI briefing.

Per the report, the attacker inserted a loader into an optional Project JavaScript field in customer dashboards, which Optimizely’s CDN then served using its own domain and certificate. After that, most visitors to the impacted websites received a script hosted at 1688360.cc that scanned pages for crypto addresses and replaced legit wallet destinations, including for BTC, ETH, Solana, and TRON, with ones the attacker controlled.

It also changed clipboard content, links, and outgoing requests, with a card skimmer collecting card numbers, expiry dates, and CVVs that people had entered into payment detail forms on a site.

If a user visited those websites on an Apple device, the malware loaded exploit chains through separate domains for Coruna and Darksword. According to Report URI, Coruna targeted iOS 13 to 17, while Darksword went for iOS 18.x, although iOS 18.7.3 and iOS 26.3 had been patched against those chains.

As CryptoPotato recently reported, Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao had warned iPhone users to update their devices so as to protect themselves from Darksword.

“The vulnerable path is blocked, the injected code was removed, and customers have been contacted directly,” Optimizely said after identifying the incident.

However, by 19:25 UTC yesterday, the attacker had stolen about $7,000 in crypto, most of it being small amounts of Bitcoin and Litecoin as well as USDT, TRX, and ETH.

Few Sites Were Protected

The incident exposed a gap in the security of many websites; Report URI found that, of 256 hosts belonging to the affected organizations, 68 didn’t have a Content Security Policy. This is a browser rule listing which sources a page may load scripts from or send data to.

Another 50 had policies that allowed the payload and data theft, while 14 blocked data theft but still allowed address swapping. Only 24 blocked the payload.

The script monitoring firm has urged anyone who might have visited the websites on its list to check their crypto transfers and monitor their card statements. Those using Apple devices have also been asked to update them.

The post Beware: Over 178 Popular Websites Hit by Crypto-Stealing Malware appeared first on CryptoPotato.

title: DeFi Development Adds 9,482 SOL as Treasury Grows for Tenth Straight Week
description: DeFi Development Corp. has reported another increase in its Solana treasury, adding 9,482 SOL and SOL equivalents to reach approximately 2.62 million. The November 16.
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • DeFi Development disclosed 9,482 additional SOL and equivalents, taking holdings to about 2.62 million.
  • Management says its treasury has grown for ten consecutive weeks.
  • CHAD’s reported annualized preferred rate and dividend streak are separate from SOL price performance.

DeFi Development Corp. has reported another increase in its Solana treasury, adding 9,482 SOL and SOL equivalents to reach approximately 2.62 million. The November 16 SEC-filed statement describes ten consecutive weeks of holdings growth and a separate streak of 31 business days of dividends on its CHAD preferred stock. The pairing illustrates how companies built around crypto treasuries increasingly operate two different propositions: directional token exposure for common shareholders and an income-oriented capital instrument with its own terms.

The new treasury count

The filing lists approximately 2,619,311 SOL and equivalents, up from 2,609,829 in its previous update. Management says the accumulation streak began in September following a return to active buying in late August. Its activities include acquisitions, staking, validator operations and other on-chain opportunities. That mix matters because not all increases in token inventory necessarily correspond to purchasing the same number of SOL on a spot exchange. A complete shareholder analysis should separate bought tokens from rewards, then compare the increase with changes in the company’s shares and outstanding claims.

What SOL per share aims to show

The company says increasing SOL per share is a strategic objective. A coin count divided by a share count can illustrate one dimension of exposure, but it does not replace net asset value, cash-flow analysis or a review of dilution. Capital raised to buy SOL may increase total tokens while changing ownership percentages. Some holdings may also be subject to staking arrangements or operational constraints. Investors should examine the definitions attached to any company-specific per-share indicator before concluding that a higher treasury automatically improves common-equity returns.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana corporate treasury results.

CHAD dividends are a different instrument

The firm’s variable-rate Series C perpetual preferred stock, CHAD, carries a reported 14% annual dividend rate as of the update. The company says it has made payments for 31 consecutive business days. Those distributions are subject to the preferred security’s terms and declarations by the board; a stated annualized rate is not an ironclad future payment guarantee. Common stockholders and preferred investors face different risks and rights. Presenting the preferred yield as though it were a return paid by holding SOL would be inaccurate.

The limits of the treasury comparison

Solana’s price can move substantially faster than a weekly treasury increase, so a company could report more tokens while its dollar portfolio value falls. Staking rewards are also variable and bring their own operational requirements. For DeFi Development, the most informative future disclosures will combine updated token counts with cash reserves, financing costs, issuance, validator income and the amount available to common equity. The accumulation streak is a measurable development, but its investment significance depends on what the company gave up to extend it.

Treasury-company comparisons also require attention to liabilities and timing. Two firms holding similar numbers of SOL can have very different shareholder economics if one borrowed to finance purchases, has preferred dividends to meet or issued substantially more common stock. Reported SOL-per-share figures can be useful, but the numerator and denominator should be consistently defined. Investors should also distinguish income from staking from changes in SOL's market value. Neither measure on its own guarantees liquidity to support future payments or operating expenses.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana infrastructure updates.

This update is evidence of continued SOL accumulation and preferred-dividend activity. It is not an assurance that either share class will preserve its value, and the reported yield should not be confused with a guaranteed return on the underlying cryptocurrency.

Reporting sources: DeFi Development Corp. SEC exhibit

title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska’s Senate race, NBC News projects
description: NBC News projects Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan in Alaska’s Senate race. NBC News’ Steve Patterson reports on the midterm election outcome.
fullContent: NBC News projects Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan in Alaska’s Senate race. NBC News’ Steve Patterson reports on the midterm election outcome.

title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race, beating Republican Dan Sullivan
description:
Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan to flip yet another Senate seat for Democrats.
Updated vote counts released Tuesday night gave Peltola just over 50% of the first-choice ballots, according to the Associated Press, allowing her to secure victory without having to rely on any second-choice ballots under the state's ranked-choice voting system. 
Peltola's victory comes after weeks of controversy, accusations and legal wrangling stemming from the presence of Daniel J. Sullivan — an unaffiliated candidate who happens to share a name with the incumbent Republican senator — on the ballot.
Alaska's race was the last undecided Senate contest of the midterm cycle, which saw Democrats flip both chambers of Congress with substantial majorities. Peltola is the ninth Democrat to flip a GOP-held Senate seat this year. 
She is the first Democrat elected to the Senate in Alaska since 2008.

Double Dan drama
Alaska's Senate race came to dominate headlines in the weeks before Election Day when the Department of Justice filed a lawsuit in federal court to block certification of the election results if Sen. Dan S. Sullivan lost by a narrow margin, alleging that retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan launched his candidacy with the sole purpose of siphoning away votes from the incumbent Republican.
A few days later, the New York Times published an extensive investigation that appeared to substantiate that allegation, calling it "Democrats' secret effort to stack Alaska's ballot."
Trump, who said he ordered the DOJ to file the suit, later argued on Truth Social that both Peltola and the "fake" Dan Sullivan should be removed from the ballot. 
Sen. Dan Sullivan
Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

While having two candidates with the same name on the same ballot is unusual, tactical "ballot stacking" is a relatively common — and largely legal — practice among both parties. A federal judge ultimately dismissed the DOJ's lawsuit, writing that any attempt to determine whether Peltola's win could be directly attributed to voter confusion over the two Dan Sullivans would be "infeasible."
Still, investigations by the DOJ and state law enforcement to determine whether any laws may have been broken in the process of getting the second Dan Sullivan's name on the ballot appear to be ongoing.  
Some Republicans have suggested that they may attempt to block Peltola from being seated in the Senate,but Peltola's victory on first-choice ballots makes it more difficult to argue that she won because of voter confusion. There's also the reality that Democrats will be taking over the Senate in early January, which puts a limited shelf life on any campaign to keep her from formally taking her seat. 
Who is Mary Peltola?
Peltola, 53, was born in Anchorage in 1973, the child of a German-American transplant from Nebraska and a Native Alaskan woman of the Yup'ik people — one of several Indigenous groups in western and southwestern Alaska.
She grew up fishing with her father in Yup'ik and became the captain of her own fishing boat by the age of 14. As an adult, she worked for the Alaska Department of Fish and Game and later served as executive director of the Kuskokwim River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission. Her lifetime of efforts to protect Alaska's wild fisheries and protect its coastal waters have become a key element of her political identity.
Peltola turned to politics in the late 1990s, when she was elected to a seat in Alaska's House of Representatives, where she served for 10 years. Peltola's pragmatic approach to politics was highlighted in 2010, when she led a write-in campaign that helped Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski win reelection after she lost the GOP primary to a Tea Party conservative.
In 2022, Peltola joined the race for Alaska's lone seat in the U.S. House of Representatives, which had been left vacant after the death of longtime incumbent Rep. Don Young. title: Anthropic Token Sale on Binance: The Catch Behind the Price
description:
Key Takeaways A 5% xStocks fee lifts the break-even price Delivery comes at least two hours after open Oversubscription can […]
The post Anthropic Token Sale on Binance: The Catch Behind the Price appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • A 5% xStocks fee lifts the break-even price
  • Delivery comes at least two hours after open
  • Oversubscription can leave partial or zero allocations
  • ANTx tracks Anthropic without granting shareholder rights

The campaign announcement sets the application window for November 18, 2026, from 06:00 to 14:00 UTC, with a 100 USDC minimum and a 500 million USDC cap on total subscriptions.

The 70–78 USDC per token that Binance displays excludes fees and, by Binance’s own calculation, values Anthropic at roughly $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion. It is also only indicative. According to Binance Wallet’s campaign FAQ, the issuer and underwriters set the final offering price after the window closes, based on demand, valuation and issuance arrangements, and that price can land above or below the range.

Applicants are therefore committing an amount of money, not buying a set number of tokens. Every cost figure below starts from the final offering price, whatever it turns out to be.

A 10% Rise Is Not a 10% Return

xStocks charges a 5% partner service fee to cover operational and distribution costs, and Binance Wallet says it adds no fee of its own. Neither the announcement nor the FAQ states whether the 5% is added on top of the committed USDC or taken out of it, or whether any charge applies to funds that go unallocated.

For break-even purposes, the first question makes no difference. If the fee is added on top, a 1,000 USDC allocation costs 1,050 USDC. If it is deducted, 1,050 USDC buys 1,000 USDC worth of tokens. Either way, each token costs 5% more than the final offering price: 73.50 USDC at the bottom of the indicative range and 81.90 USDC at the top. The mechanics change how many tokens a commitment buys, not the price ANTx must reach before an applicant is level.

That fixed hurdle shrinks every gain and deepens every loss, as the scenarios below show.

If ANTx trades this far from the final offering price…

Token move
−5%
Applicant’s return
−9.5%
Token move
+3%
Applicant’s return
−1.9%
Token move
+10%
Applicant’s return
+4.8%
Token move
+20%
Applicant’s return
+14.3%

Coindoo calculation of return on cost after the 5% partner fee. Excludes network costs, trading spreads and any charge on unallocated funds.

Delivery Comes After the Opening Trade

The announcement schedules distribution for at least two hours after Nasdaq opens, with the exact time still to be confirmed and the timeline subject to change. Neither page gives a listing date. The FAQ says only that pricing is expected on November 18.

“At least two hours” sets a floor, not a delivery promise. Whatever Anthropic’s shares do in their first hours of trading, applicants have no tokens to sell into that move. Their first available exit is the price ANTx commands once it reaches their wallets, and that is the price the fee hurdle has to clear. How tokenized shares are priced relative to the underlying stock is a separate question, covered in Coindoo’s analysis of tokenized-stock pricing.

A Partial Fill Leaves Capital Waiting

Binance describes an oversubscription model: if demand exceeds what is on offer, allocations are made in proportion to each applicant’s deposit. The issuer and underwriters set the results, and Binance Wallet applies them without discretion. Full, partial and zero allocations are all possible.

How much a single wallet can commit depends on its Alpha Points. The limit is 20,000 USDC for holders with any points, 100,000 USDC above 40 points, 200,000 USDC above 100 and 500,000 USDC above 200. Trenchers Badge holders get an extra 50,000 USDC.

Until allocations are settled, committed USDC stays locked in a non-custodial smart contract. Unused funds return to the wallet automatically afterwards, but neither page says how many days that takes.

Proportional allocation creates a trap for applicants who commit more than they want to own, expecting to be scaled back. If deposits reach twice the amount on offer, a 10,000 USDC commitment fills at roughly 5,000 USDC. If demand comes in below supply, the same commitment fills in full, and the applicant holds twice the intended position. Only an amount the applicant is prepared to hold at a full fill is safe from that outcome.

READ MORE:

Grayscale Reveals ‘Compelling Entry Points’ but Data Says No

What ANTx Actually Gives You

ANTx tracks Anthropic’s share price, but holding it does not make anyone a shareholder. The FAQ states that the tokens carry no direct ownership, voting or dividend rights and no claim against Anthropic. Any dividends may instead be reinvested or paid out at redemption, net of withholding tax.

Responsibility for the token sits with Backed, the company that issues xStocks tokenized shares, or its affiliates. Binance Wallet describes itself as the interface, not the issuer, and the FAQ notes that the issuer can blacklist wallet addresses it considers in breach of laws, regulations or sanctions.

On backing, the two companies speak with different degrees of confidence. xStocks’ product description says its tokens are backed 1:1 by underlying assets held in regulated custody. Binance’s FAQ says the backing may be cash or other eligible assets rather than the shares themselves, and that the wallet neither verifies those assets nor represents that ANTx is backed 1:1. Neither statement shows that any collateral is missing. Applicants are relying on the issuer’s word, not on a check by the platform distributing the token.

Redemption is not a simple way out either. It follows the issuer’s terms and eligibility rules, can be suspended temporarily and, where available, may carry extra fees and minimum sizes. For most holders, the realistic exit is a sale on the secondary market, which needs a buyer at an acceptable price. That is also what separates ANTx from the Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual futures: the subscription delivers a token, with no margin or funding payments attached.

The Number to Check on Distribution Day

Once tokens arrive, the wallet’s transaction history holds everything needed to measure what the campaign actually cost.

Effective entry cost per token

Total USDC deducted, fees included ÷ ANTx received

Compare it with a price you can actually sell at, not Anthropic’s Nasdaq quote.

If that figure comes out above the final offering price plus 5%, the difference is a charge the campaign documents do not describe. If the price available on the secondary market sits below it, the IPO gain shown on the chart has not reached the applicant’s wallet.

Sixty-seven companies have opted out so far of having their shares traded on OKX ICE's tokenized stock venue, and a full-page Wall Street Journal ad warned CEOs that crypto would soon tokenize their stock on unregulated venues.

title: Former Robinhood Engineer Pleads Guilty to Trading Crypto Listings Through Hyperliquid
description: A former Robinhood software engineer has pleaded guilty to using confidential information about forthcoming crypto listings to trade perpetual futures on Hyperliquid..
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Huaisong Xiang pleaded guilty to wire fraud linked to confidential Robinhood listing plans.
  • The Justice Department says he will forfeit $125,523 and faces sentencing in February 2027.
  • The case concerns misuse of employer information, not an allegation that Hyperliquid itself committed the fraud.

A former Robinhood software engineer has pleaded guilty to using confidential information about forthcoming crypto listings to trade perpetual futures on Hyperliquid. The US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York says Huaisong Xiang agreed to forfeit $125,523 in proceeds from the scheme. The case is a useful reminder that moving a trade to a decentralized venue does not erase legal duties tied to information obtained through an employer. It is also important to describe this as a guilty plea by one defendant, not a judgment against the entire platform or everyone named in earlier proceedings.

How the scheme worked, according to prosecutors

Federal prosecutors say Xiang had access to internal plans detailing which digital assets Robinhood would add and when public announcements were expected. Between 2025 and 2026, he used that information to take positions in perpetual futures linked to those assets before listings became public. Such instruments allow a trader to speculate on price changes without buying the underlying tokens, and they can be held without a fixed expiry if funding requirements are met. The information advantage came from alleged misuse of confidential business plans, not from a flaw in the exchange’s public data feed.

A plea is not the same as an accusation

The Justice Department’s November 16 release says Xiang pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud before US District Judge Colleen McMahon. He agreed to forfeit the stated proceeds, and sentencing is scheduled for February 25, 2027. The offense carries a statutory maximum of 20 years, but that is not a forecast of what sentence the judge will impose. This reporting describes the admitted conduct as set out by prosecutors and the plea. Any allegations against another individual should remain separate unless they are themselves resolved by court action.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hyperliquid trading and open-interest trends.

Why on-chain execution is not a legal loophole

Hyperliquid is a decentralized venue for perpetual derivatives, but the duties at the center of the case arose when confidential employer information was misappropriated. An employee’s ability to execute a trade without a conventional broker does not make the information public or remove obligations to protect it. On-chain settlement can also leave a detailed transaction trail, although linking wallets to specific people requires evidence. The case illustrates why compliance policies must cover external crypto platforms and derivatives, rather than only the trading accounts an employer officially monitors.

Implications for listing teams and traders

Companies planning token listings need clear access controls, internal approval records and policies that explain what staff may trade and when. Prosecutors’ earlier account described employees with access to nonpublic listing communications. Decentralized markets give informed actors new instruments, but do not change the underlying conflict between privileged information and fair market access. For traders, the case is not an argument that every price move before a listing is illicit; proof of confidential access, duties and misuse is the key distinction.

For compliance departments, the case illustrates why handling confidential listing plans resembles handling other market-sensitive corporate information, even when the resulting trade takes place on a decentralized venue. Firms may need clearer access controls, monitoring of employees' external accounts and written policies on information obtained through employment. Trading venues can publish transactions, but linking a wallet to the person who controls it often requires additional evidence. Regulators and prosecutors will continue to evaluate conduct under the applicable statutes rather than using blockchain transparency as an exemption.

For related context, see our earlier report on an earlier crypto-asset security case.

The plea adds a concrete enforcement example to a debate often framed in abstract terms. It shows how traditional fraud theories can reach misconduct involving on-chain perpetuals while leaving the status of ordinary public-information trading to be assessed on its own facts.

Reporting sources: US Justice Department November 16 statement

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: 8-year-old Haitian boy returns to school after being detained by ICE
description:
An 8-year-old Haitian boy who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement earlier this month in San Diego has been released, according to an advocacy group and the boy's school. 
"School leadership, and counselors had a meeting with the student when he returned to school this morning to ensure he had all the supports he and his family needed, and then he went off to class," the San Diego Unified School District said in a statement. 
Haitian Bridge Alliance, which had advocated for the boy's release, said it welcomed the development.
"An eight-year-old child belongs in a classroom, on a playground, and surrounded by love—not in immigration detention," said Guerline Jozef, executive director of Haitian Bridge Alliance, in a statement. "We welcome his release, but his freedom should never have required a public outcry."
The Department of Homeland Security previously confirmed that ICE agents placed the child in federal care on Nov. 5 after he attended a check-in appointment with a man the agency said claimed to be the boy's uncle.
Haitian Bridge Alliance said the boy, a third grader, has been living with relatives since his father was deported in 2025. In August of this year, following a legal victory for the Trump administration, some 350,000 Haitians living in the U.S. lost Temporary Protected Status, stripping them of deportation protections and work permits.
Advocates recorded and documented the moment when the 8-year-old was escorted by at least one ICE agent inside the Edward J. Schwartz building in San Diego, with Haitian Bridge Alliance saying the detention left the boy's cousins "in tears."
DHS said at the time that the agents designated the child an unaccompanied minor because "the alleged uncle could not establish legal guardianship of the minor."
"Out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child's safety, ICE determined it was best to remove the child from the household and place him in the care of the Office of Refugee Resettlement," DHS added.
The Office of Refugee Resettlement is an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services that is responsible for housing minors who lack a valid immigration status and who are taken into custody without their parents or legal guardians.
Haitian Bridge Alliance said in a previous statement that "when parents are taken into custody by ICE, they are not provided an opportunity to return home to see their children or to be able to transfer guardianship."
"ICE just incarcerated then deported without taking into account the wellbeing of the children left behind," it said.
This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/8-year-old-detained-ice-released-custody/

title: Lighter Reopens Withdrawals After Nonce-Reuse Error Exposes Trader API Keys
description: Decentralized derivatives venue Lighter says deposits and withdrawals have resumed following a November 16 security incident that initially froze access. The latest.
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Lighter says deposits and withdrawals have resumed after its November 16 incident.
  • Bitquery observed a roughly $10.4 million USDC withdrawal; the venue reports about $5 million returned to traders.
  • The reported root cause involved nonce reuse in unofficial signing code, not a confirmed smart-contract exploit.

Decentralized derivatives venue Lighter says deposits and withdrawals have resumed following a November 16 security incident that initially froze access. The latest explanation points to unsafe signing code used by affected trader accounts, not an announced compromise of the protocol’s smart contracts. That distinction is central to the incident: a cryptographic error in an external trading integration can expose account authority even when a venue’s core software behaves as designed.

The on-chain withdrawal was substantial

Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery traced a withdrawal of 10,393,057 USDC from a Lighter-related Ethereum contract on November 16. The funds were converted into ether, and investigators followed part of the subsequent movement through multiple wallets. Those observations establish a visible transfer trail, but they are not the same thing as a complete, audited final-loss figure. Earlier reports also cited higher possible amounts covering more than one account, which Lighter had not confirmed at the time. The safe description is an observed approximately $10.4 million USDC outflow and an incident whose recovery accounting may evolve.

Why nonce reuse can reveal a key

According to Lighter’s reported postmortem, some affected accounts used unofficial or custom signing code that reused one-time cryptographic values, known as nonces. Reusing these values with the wrong signature scheme can allow an attacker to derive secret signing material from information that was supposed to be public. Once an API signing key is compromised, apparently authorized instructions can be sent through normal account capabilities. This is not a conventional stolen-password story, and it underscores why teams should use well-tested official signing libraries rather than copy cryptographic routines into trading bots.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet incident.

The pause and partial recovery

Lighter activated its Guardian safeguard during the incident, temporarily restricting withdrawals and related activity while its Security Council acted. The exchange says roughly $5 million USDC was returned to affected traders and that Guardian mode was subsequently deactivated. Its official announcements channel states that deposits and withdrawals are back to normal, with pending requests being processed. That $5 million figure should not be described as full recovery of the separately observed $10.4 million transfer. The remaining exposure and final accounting need a detailed reconciled report.

Security changes traders should understand

The venue says it has changed how API signatures are exposed and now requires wallet signatures for transfers into public pools. Further planned controls include IP allowlists, scoped permissions, per-key limits and monitoring for repeated nonces. For a trader using custom automation, the immediate lesson is to audit signing code, rotate uncertain keys and understand what each API credential can authorize. Smart-contract audits remain important, but they cannot substitute for secure key handling in external client software.

Nonce-reuse vulnerabilities are particularly serious because digital signatures rely on the uniqueness and secrecy of certain temporary values. If an attacker can infer a private key from flawed signatures, simply restarting a user interface or changing a password may not fix the exposed credential. The scope depends on which keys were affected and whether they could authorise actions beyond trading. Users should follow the protocol team's specific revocation and key-rotation instructions rather than assuming that reopening withdrawals means every associated security risk has ended.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Kava Lend exploit.

This is now a restoration-and-root-cause story, not simply a withdrawal-halt headline. The strongest follow-up will be a fully reconciled account of losses, recovered funds and the effectiveness of the new controls under live trading conditions.

Reporting sources: Lighter official announcements feed · Bitquery transaction investigation · CoinDesk initial incident coverage

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitmine Adds 7,653 ETH as Ethereum Treasury Climbs Above 6.08 Million Tokens
description: Ethereum treasury company Bitmine says it added 7,653 ETH over the past week, taking its reported holdings to approximately 6.08 million tokens. That is an increase in.
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Bitmine reported ETH holdings of about 6.08 million after adding 7,653 tokens.
  • The treasury’s dollar valuation fell as the broader Ethereum market weakened.
  • Staking and accumulation strategies do not remove price, operational or financing risks.

Ethereum treasury company Bitmine says it added 7,653 ETH over the past week, taking its reported holdings to approximately 6.08 million tokens. That is an increase in the unit count, but not a guarantee that the dollar value of the position grew at the same time. Ether has been under heavy selling pressure, and the company’s reported combined crypto, cash and marketable securities holdings were worth about $11.8 billion in its November 16 update. The contrast highlights the risks of evaluating a digital-asset treasury through a single metric.

The acquisition amid a sell-off

Bitmine’s investor-relations page lists a November 16 release reporting an ETH holding above 6.08 million. The Block says the latest weekly addition was 7,653 ETH, while ether prices had declined sharply. Buying more tokens increases the number held, but changes in the price can overwhelm the value of incremental purchases over a short period. Treasury investors should therefore track both coins and fair-market value. It is possible for a company to accumulate strategically while shareholders experience a substantial decline in the marked value of the underlying asset.

The five-percent goal has consequences

Bitmine has framed its strategy around acquiring a material share of Ethereum’s circulating supply and building associated staking infrastructure. The larger the treasury becomes, the more its exposure concentrates in a single volatile asset. The company’s long-term thesis may connect ETH ownership with network activity and institutional tokenization, but that remains an investment view rather than a guaranteed economic result. Significant purchases also raise questions about how they are financed and how much incremental exposure existing shareholders receive after dilution or other capital-structure changes.

For related context, see our earlier report on institutional Ethereum yield-fund developments.

Staking adds activity, not a price floor

Bitmine has also discussed staking and validator operations as ways to earn rewards using Ethereum holdings. Staking can produce token-denominated revenue and contribute to network security. However, rewards vary with network conditions and do not remove the risk that ETH falls in dollar terms. Running validators involves technical, operational and potentially slashing or counterparty risks depending on the arrangement. A headline yield can obscure the difference between earning additional tokens and protecting shareholder purchasing power. Investors need transparent reporting on costs, locked assets and realized rewards.

How to judge the quarterly picture

The relevant questions include how much ETH is owned, what it cost, whether assets are encumbered, how staking contributes to cash or token income, and which claims sit ahead of common equity. Short-term market capitalization or portfolio value can fluctuate far more quickly than business operations change. The reported weekly purchase shows continued accumulation, while price declines mean the company’s valuation remains highly sensitive to ether markets. Watching both acquisition activity and funding terms will be more informative than treating chairman Tom Lee’s commentary as a price signal.

title: White House pulls Trump's pick to lead FDA as Republican support falters
description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The White House said Tuesday it has pulled the nomination of Dr. Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration amid growing indications she didn’t have the votes needed to win Senate confirmation.
Overton, a physician and White House domestic policy adviser, has spent most of her professional career working directly for Trump or conservative groups aligned with his agenda. Her nomination in August was seen as a move to bring a stabilizing Trump loyalist to the FDA, following a tumultous year under Trump’s first FDA commissioner, Dr. Marty Makary.
But Overton faced bipartisan questions in the Senate about her willingness to break from Trump, particularly on his administration's approach to vaccines.
Republican Sen. Bill Cassidy, a Louisiana doctor who chairs the Senate health committee, said earlier he remained undecided about Overton ahead of a critical vote on her nomination scheduled for Wednesday morning.
Cassidy had previously called Overton’s support for Trump’s plan to break up combination vaccines — including the measles, mumps and rubella shot— “almost disqualifying.” And he pressed her during a September hearing about her scientific independence and willingness to disagree with Trump and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a longtime vaccine critic.
But late Tuesday night, Cassidy suggested he had been prepared to back Overton and suggested her nomination was derailed by disagreements over abortion, not vaccines.
“I believe she would have had the votes to pass out of committee and pass the full Senate,” Cassidy stated in a posting on X. 
He went on to say that anti-abortion Republicans had sought commitments on “life issues” from the White House, but “the Administration withdrew Dr. Overton rather than make such commitments.”
Currently, the FDA is conducting a safety review of the abortion pill mifepristone — at the request of Trump — that could reinstate restrictions on the drug’s use, including a requirement for in-person prescribing. FDA has promised a report on its safety findings by March.
To win confirmation, Overton would have needed the votes of all 12 Republicans on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee. Democrats hold 11 seats. Without support of the committee, Overton faced little chance of winning a full Senate vote on chamber floor. 
Republicans have been racing to try to confirm Trump’s nominees before handing over power to Senate Democrats in January.
It was not immediately clear when, or if, the White House might put forward another nominee.
Cassidy has previously threatened to oppose health nominees
Cassidy has repeatedly tried to win commitments on upholding vaccine standards, including from Kennedy, by threatening to withhold his vote. Ultimately, though, he voted in favor of each nominee that came before his committee. 
Other Republicans, including Maine Sen. Susan Collins, raised concerns about other health issues, including Overton's approach to flavored e-cigarettes. The FDA recently authorized the first fruit-flavored e-cigarettes for adult smokers looking to quit. Under previous administrations, including the first Trump administration, the agency had opposed vaping flavors that could attract teens and children.
Opposition to Overton’s nomination also came from influential figures in the Make America Healthy Again movement, who blamed her and other White House officials for sidelining some of Kennedy’s top health goals, including crackdowns on food additives and pesticides.
Earlier this month, Calley Means told Joe Rogan that White House aides, including Overton, worked within the administration to advance a Supreme Court decision blocking thousands of lawsuits over the weedkiller glyphosate. Means, a former Kennedy aide who recently left the government, said that and other key decisions were carried out at the behest of industry lobbyists.
“There is a very concentrated group in the Trump administration that are antagonistic to what people voted for,” Means said.
Trump has pulled back several other health nominations 
Trump’s first nominee for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr. David Weldon, was replaced because it was unclear he had enough Republican support to be confirmed. Two of Trump’s surgeon general nominees, including Dr. Casey Means — Calley Means’ sister — were also pulled after facing pushback from Senate Republicans and most Democrats.
The FDA is currently being led on acting basis by Kyle Diamantas, an attorney and friend of Donald Trump Jr. He was elevated to the post in May after previously serving as the agency’s top food official. Under federal rules, acting officials are limited to about seven months leading a federal agency.
The FDA under Makary was marked by a string of scientific disputes, leadership changes and media stories detailing low morale and internal dysfunction among staffers. The FDA has lost about 20% of its employees to layoffs, buyouts, retirements or resignations since Trump took office.

title: From Delray Beach to the Exumas: William DeBilzan Has Started the Official $ONELOVE Painting
description: The Florida artist has begun a commissioned original for Captain Robbie Olson’s One Love Sailing Coin, with an unveiling planned aboard the 82-foot catamaran One Love². On a short trip to Delray Beach, Florida, Captain Robbie Olson walked into the gallery of his longtime friend, artist William DeBilzan, and left with something he says he […]
fullContent:
The Florida artist has begun a commissioned original for Captain Robbie Olson’s One Love Sailing Coin, with an unveiling planned aboard the 82-foot catamaran One Love².

On a short trip to Delray Beach, Florida, Captain Robbie Olson walked into the gallery of his longtime friend, artist William DeBilzan, and left with something he says he did not see coming: a new original painting, already underway, made for $ONELOVE and for the boat that gave the coin its name.

Olson, a 500-ton master mariner and the founder of One Love Sailing Charters, shared the news on November 13, 2026, after sitting down with DeBilzan at the artist’s gallery on East Atlantic Avenue. In a video from the visit, he said the idea came up while they were talking about new ways for people to use the token in real life. “It ended up being my favorite part of the whole visit,” Olson said. That same day he wrote that “Billy is beginning a commissioned original painting inspired by $ONELOVE,” and that the crew would document the work “from the first brushstroke to the finished work.”

A painter who already knows these waters

DeBilzan is a Delray Beach painter, sculptor, and designer whose work is hard to miss: elongated figures, layered texture, and a color palette drawn from years on the water. His galleries have described the Caribbean as his greatest source of inspiration. He has been exploring the region for close to thirty years, often at the helm of his own yacht, and has channeled that love into his Tropical Series. Collectors of his work have included Adam Sandler, Shaquille O’Neal, Tony Hawk, and Kevin James. His paintings and installations have appeared at Marriott Central Park in New York and in Dubai’s Burj Khalifa, and he also designs clothing, swimwear, and a long-running line of handbags with Colombian luxury craftsman Mario Hernandez.

This is an established Florida studio opening its doors to a coin that already lives in the world DeBilzan paints: boats, islands, and the pull of the Caribbean.

A coin that started on a working yacht

$ONELOVE, or One Love Sailing Coin, launched on Solana through Moonshot on August 15, 2026. The name did not have to be invented for a token. It was already the name of Olson’s business and of S/Y One Love², an 82-foot Nautitech sailing catamaran operating in the Exumas, Bahamas. Olson has spent about thirty years sailing the Bahamas, fifteen years running charters, and a decade focused on the Exumas.

The token is already accepted for sailing charters aboard One Love² and for merchandise, and the team has said a first charter client has paid a booking deposit in $ONELOVE. On November 2, Olson announced that DeBilzan would accept $ONELOVE for original artwork, fashion, designer handbags, and luxury accessories. In the Delray Beach video, DeBilzan went further, saying the gallery would take the coin for “paintings and prints,” and that “we’re adding the whole inventory here in the gallery to his currency.”

That real-world use is the point Olson keeps returning to. In a September interview with writer Bob Lorns, published as “Charting a Different Course: Can a Caribbean Crypto Project Grow Without the Hype?,” he said: “The thought was to create something people here could recognize as ours. Not just another coin somebody launched somewhere on the internet, but something with a Caribbean identity that might get people curious enough to learn how all of this actually works.”

Built for the long haul

The art news lands during a stretch Olson has framed as a test of conviction. On November 17, he posted a joint message with the Ethereum community token $NEKO under the banner “Bulls in a Bear Market.” “Bear markets shake out the tourists. They do not shake the believers,” he wrote. “We did not just show up when the charts turned green. We have been here all along, building, believing, and holding strong while the rest of the market struggles.” The post noted that both tokens finished the past week in the green, with $ONELOVE up 17.5%, and called the pairing “the Captain and the King.”

Behind the slogan are commitments holders can check for themselves. As of Olson’s latest announcement, 80 million $ONELOVE tokens are locked, and the token’s mint and freeze authorities have been revoked, so no new supply can be created and no wallet can be frozen. A commissioned painting from an established artist fits the same pattern: something built to last, not a quick headline.

The canvas is already on the easel

In the gallery video, DeBilzan said Olson asked him “to do a kind of a logo painting for both the coin and his boat,” which already carries a DeBilzan painting. Towels, t-shirts, and swimsuits are already sold from that earlier work. This new canvas is meant for both the token and the yacht.

Then came the line the community has been waiting for. “I have started the painting,” DeBilzan said, “and I think we’re planning to do an unveiling on his boat this next week. We will keep you up to date with the progress of the painting and do the unveiling.” He also said he planned to join Olson in Miami before the captain heads back to the Bahamas to get the boat ready for upcoming charters. “I think it’s going to be exciting,” DeBilzan said. “I’m looking forward to it and we’ll keep you informed.”

DeBilzan has already started the new $ONELOVE painting, and an unveiling is planned aboard One Love² soon. The date will be announced on Olson’s X account, @TheCaptRobbie, and in the Telegram crew at @ONELOVECoinCrew. The gallery already accepts $ONELOVE for paintings and prints, and anyone interested in the new $ONELOVE painting or in DeBilzan’s other work can follow along, and reach out, through those channels or through the gallery.

Until then, the story is already vivid enough. A working captain and a Caribbean-minded artist, friends before they were collaborators, are putting a new canvas at the center of a coin that can already book a charter, buy merch, and walk into a Delray Beach gallery and leave with a painting, a print, or a handmade bag. The official $ONELOVE site likes to say that the strongest ships are built from timber like the mighty oak, “because the strongest trees take the longest to grow.” A painting takes time, too. DeBilzan has picked up the brush. The next time that work meets the public, the plan is for it to happen on deck, with salt in the air and the Exumas somewhere ahead.

CA: F1r5AqRj8bJyzM4nUZpVBH1JQT8ToR4Rvjj2YwxHmoon

Follow the progress through Captain Robbie Olson on X at @TheCaptRobbie, the community on Telegram at @ONELOVECoinCrew, and at onelovesailingcoin.com. DeBilzan’s work can be explored at debilzan.com and shopdebilzan.com.

title: Man with axe accused of destroying $60 million U.S. military plane in Ireland
description:
The $60m (£45m) US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules was rendered inoperable and will not fly again, US prosecutors said.Photograph: US Department of Justice/PA


An axe-wielding man breached a security perimeter and destroyed an American military plane while it was parked at an Irish airport, US prosecutors said.
Daithi O’Corrain, 48, is accused of cutting hydraulic lines, smashing cockpit gauges and pouring ball bearings into fuel tanks.
O’Corrain is charged with destruction of US government property in connection with the incident in April at Shannon airport in the west of Ireland, according to an indictment unsealed on Tuesday in Manhattan.
He is not in US custody and his arraignment on the charge has not been scheduled, the AP news agency reported. If convicted, he faces up to 10 years in prison.
The $60m (£45m) US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules, which had been en route to a military assignment in another country, was rendered inoperable and will not fly again, US prosecutors said.
O’Corrain, described by supporters as an independent peace activist, was arrested immediately after the attack by Ireland’s police force, An Garda Síochána. He was charged with causing criminal damage and trespassing.
Manhattan US attorney Jamie McDonald said the indictment sends “a clear and powerful message that attacks on US military assets – and thus our national security – will not be tolerated.”
An online fundraiser organised by people describing themselves as O’Corrain’s friends said he disarmed the C-130 in protest against the US’s war with Iran and support for Israel’s war in Gaza.
O’Corrain plotted the attack on 11 April for months, US prosecutors said.
He searched online for information about the construction of the C-130, a quad-engine turboprop mainly used for transporting equipment and personnel, and looked up coordinates for sneaking on to the airport’s grounds, prosecutors allege.
O’Corrain subscribed to a phone app that provided live flight tracking and ordered capsules of gallium, a chemical that can corrode steel and break down aluminium, prosecutors added.
He is also accused of trying to contact someone who had been involved in a prior breach at Shannon airport, prosecutors said.
O’Corrain breached the airport’s perimeter at about 4.40 am and broke into the C-130 as it was parked on a taxiway by destroying a locking mechanism on the rear crew door, his indictment said.
The document added he used the crew’s hammocks to cover the plane’s windows but left the cockpit windshield exposed.
He then barricaded himself inside the aircraft, securing the doors with straps, brackets and screws, and put ball bearings mixed with epoxy in door tracks to prevent doors from being opened or closed, the indictment said.
James Barnacle, the head of the FBI’s New York office, said: “This was not an act of spontaneous vandalism.”
This article originally appeared on The Guardian at https://uk.news.yahoo.com/man-accused-destroying-us-military-000615511.html

title: Strategy Adds 485 Bitcoin as It Repurchases $228 Million of STRC Preferred Shares
description: Strategy has added 485 Bitcoin to its already enormous treasury, but its November 16 disclosure carries another figure that deserves equal attention: the company also.
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Strategy disclosed a 485-BTC purchase for approximately $33.4 million.
  • Total holdings reached 850,849 BTC at the reporting date.
  • The same announcement disclosed around $228 million of STRC repurchases, an important financing detail.

Strategy has added 485 Bitcoin to its already enormous treasury, but its November 16 disclosure carries another figure that deserves equal attention: the company also repurchased about $228 million of STRC preferred shares. The update is a reminder that digital-asset treasury companies make capital-allocation decisions across both their crypto holdings and the securities used to finance them. Counting BTC alone cannot tell investors whether each step improves their economic position.

The latest acquisition

Strategy says it bought 485 BTC between November 9 and November 15 for approximately $33.4 million, at an average acquisition price of about $68,887 per coin. The purchase raised aggregate holdings to 850,849 BTC. The company reported an aggregate acquisition cost of around $64.2 billion, equivalent to roughly $75,452 for each Bitcoin held across its history. Those cost figures are not the current market value of the treasury, and the average changes when additional purchases are made. The purchase window also matters because it spans a period of falling Bitcoin prices rather than a single quoted trade.

Why the STRC buyback belongs in the headline

STRC is part of Strategy’s preferred-capital structure. The company has used such instruments alongside equity and other financing tools to build and manage its balance sheet. Buying back preferred shares below their stated amount can affect obligations, market confidence and the securities still outstanding. It also uses capital that could otherwise serve different purposes. Investors therefore need to compare the BTC acquisition with the repurchase, cash reserves and dividend commitments. Describing the update as an unqualified large Bitcoin bet overlooks the simultaneous management of financing instruments.

For related context, see our earlier report on Twenty One Capital's bitcoin treasury results.

Dilution and claims matter to shareholders

Strategy’s treasury size is a headline measure of exposure, but a common shareholder owns an interest in a company with other securities and obligations ahead of ordinary equity. Increases in BTC can coexist with changes in share count, leverage, dividend requirements and the value of preferred securities. Simple “Bitcoin per company” comparisons do not measure everything shareholders receive. The company provides additional proprietary metrics intended to describe its strategy, but it warns that these are not identical to profitability or conventional balance-sheet valuations.

The market will test the financing strategy

Bitcoin’s November decline puts the resilience of capital structures under greater scrutiny. A company can keep buying assets while still facing pressure if its shares, preferred securities or access to funding weaken. The key disclosures to monitor are future BTC purchases, security repurchases, cash and liquid reserves, and any changes in capital-raising conditions. The latest acquisition is independently meaningful, but its significance for investors depends on the full balance sheet and the prices at which capital is issued and retired.

Capital structure deserves particular attention because Strategy finances parts of its Bitcoin accumulation through instruments with distinct investor claims. Preferred shares, common equity and debt can behave differently during sharp BTC drawdowns, especially when market prices diverge from accounting values. The relevant questions are not just how many coins were bought but what resources funded the transaction, which obligations were reduced and what exposure remained per common share. Investors should consult the full financing disclosures rather than treating a gross BTC increase as automatic shareholder accretion.

For related context, see our earlier report on JPMorgan's Strategy shareholdings disclosure.

The company has clearly continued acquiring Bitcoin through weakness. The more complete story is that its treasury strategy also includes active management of preferred claims, making both sides of the November 16 announcement essential to understanding the business.

title: Waymo pauses all U.S. freeway operations of its self-driving cars after California ban
description:
Clipped From Video
Waymo is temporarily pausing driverless rides on freeways in all its markets after California’s Department of Motor Vehicles said Tuesday that its self-driving vehicles can’t use state freeways for now, citing safety concerns following a series of incidents.
Waymo has allowed its cars to operate on freeways in five of its 13 operating areas across the US: San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles County, Phoenix, Miami and Austin, according to the company.
California’s DMV said the autonomous cars pose “imminent hazard to public safety” following at least two recent incidents involving the vehicles. In one occasion, three Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone along US Route 101, while another incident involved California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280, the department said.
In the latter, a Waymo vehicle attempted to pass patrol cars conducting a traffic break earlier this month, CNN affiliate KGO reported.
According to the agency, Waymo vehicles have made “recurrent incursions” into active construction zones, putting workers, other vehicles and equipment at risk.
“We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations,” a Waymo spokesperson said.
The company noted the US Route 101 incident did not result in any injuries or collisions.
This is the second time this year Waymo has faced highway restrictions in the state, according to CNN affiliate KGO. The company paused freeway operations in May in San Francisco and Los Angeles to improve its vehicles’ response to construction zones. The previous restriction followed similar incidents that month, according to the California DMV.
A CNN analysis in June found hundreds of incidents in which robotaxis allegedly made dangerous maneuvers and struggled with obstacles that humans instinctively handle. They ran red lights, drove into oncoming traffic and active crime scenes, failed to abide by emergency road closures and came within inches of pedestrians lawfully crossing the street.
On Tuesday, a Waymo spokesperson pointed to the company’s June statement in response to CNN reporting. Waymo said it took public feedback seriously and is actively working on improvements for some of the issues raised, but that these were largely isolated incidents. The overwhelming majority of rides are smooth and uneventful, the company said.
Waymo data said its vehicles are involved in 95% fewer crashes resulting in serious injuries, or worse, than human drivers.
The restriction went into effect on November 11 and will remain in effect until Waymo addresses the safety lapses, the California DMV said.
This story has been updated with additional information.
For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com
This article originally appeared on CNN at https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/17/us/california-waymo-ban-freeways

title: How to Find, Mitigate, and Patch the Critical Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Now
description: Executive Summary Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a critical memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder. The researchers who found it rate it 9.2 under CVSS v4.0, and Oracle rates it 8.1 under CVSS v3.1. An attacker with no credentials can corrupt Java heap memory, read secrets from it, and reach remote code execution. Researchers demonstrated pre-authentication RCE […]
fullContent:
Executive Summary

Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a critical memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder. The researchers who found it rate it 9.2 under CVSS v4.0, and Oracle rates it 8.1 under CVSS v3.1. An attacker with no credentials can corrupt Java heap memory, read secrets from it, and reach remote code execution. Researchers demonstrated pre-authentication RCE on default installations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate. Unpatched OpenJDK builds from 17.0.6 onward, from any vendor, are affected when they run on x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI, which includes Intel Xeon from Ice Lake through Granite Rapids and AMD EPYC from Zen 4 onward. Oracle released fixes on November 17, 2026, and a single JVM flag closes the exposure where patching has to wait. CISA has issued an alert urging organizations to patch immediately. Start with internet-facing identity, CI/CD, and collaboration systems, and assign an owner and a deadline to every system still unpatched.

What’s at Risk

A Critical Java Flaw Could Hand Attackers Your Identity and Build Servers.

Java4Shell is in the Java runtime itself, so no application or library has to be at fault for a service to be exposed. The flaw sits in handwritten assembly that speeds up Base64 decoding with AVX-512 instructions. A short malformed input makes that code write 62 bytes past the end of a buffer before Java rejects the input.

Base64 carries login headers, tokens, and file uploads, so the vulnerable code often runs before a user has authenticated. Calif, the firm that discovered the flaw, demonstrated remote code execution against the following products in their default configurations:

The researchers say these lists are not exhaustive. They also reached RCE in sample applications built on Apache Struts and Spring Boot.

The pre-authentication list is where the business risk concentrates. Identity providers issue the tokens every other system trusts, and build and artifact servers sign and ship your software. A compromise of either can expose downstream systems that trust its identities, tokens, or software artifacts.

Code execution is not the only outcome. A successful exploit chain can read Java heap memory before it runs any attacker code. That memory can hold private keys, tokens, and personal data. CISA also warns that crafted input can crash the JVM, so availability is at risk too. Java clients are exposed as well. The researchers report a client-side exploit in which a Java program is compromised simply by connecting over TLS to a malicious server.

Are You Affected?

A system is in scope only when both conditions are true. For an attack to work, attacker-controlled data must also reach the vulnerable Base64 decoding path in the application.

The runtime condition covers every OpenJDK-based distribution: Oracle Java SE, Oracle OpenJDK, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Eclipse Temurin, Amazon Corretto, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, BellSoft Liberica, SAP SapMachine, and Red Hat OpenJDK. There is one exception on Java 8. Oracle lists the 8u511b33-perf build of Java SE 8 as vulnerable.

On Linux, run this command to check the processor. The host meets the hardware condition only if all four flags appear.

grep -m1 ‘^flags’ /proc/cpuinfo | tr ‘ ‘ ‘\n’ | grep -E ‘^(avx512f|avx512bw|avx512vbmi|bmi2)$’

Two cautions when scoping:

  • Check the runtime each application actually runs. Many products and container images bundle their own JDK, which operating system updates do not touch. CISA notes that bundled runtimes, including those in appliances, may not appear as separate entries in a software inventory.
  • Use the processor condition to order the work, not to close findings. A workload on an unaffected CPU today can land on an affected one after an instance resize or a move to newer hardware.

Exploitation Status

As of November 17, 2026, we have not seen public confirmation of exploitation in the wild. Do not plan around that. The trigger is a short malformed Base64 string; the root cause and exploitation technique are public, and the researchers have said details of the bug leaked before the patch.

The researchers are holding back their product-specific exploits until organizations have had time to upgrade, and plan to publish them later. They report finding the bug with AI assistance in about an hour and having a first working exploit two hours after that, for under $200 in AI token costs. Expect others to repeat that work.

There is one limit worth knowing. No universal exploit exists: each product needs its own chain, and the technique is sensitive to network conditions. That slows mass exploitation. It does not protect a specific target such as your identity provider.

What to Do Now

Updating the Java runtime is the only complete fix. Oracle released fixed builds on November 17, 2026.

Other OpenJDK vendors publish on their own schedules. As of November 17, 2026, Amazon had released Corretto 17.0.21.1.2 with the fix. Use your vendor’s advisory to identify the fixed build and confirm it addresses CVE-2026-114938.

If you cannot patch today, there is a temporary workaround. It is a startup setting for Java, applied by the team that runs the application, and it takes effect after a restart. You need only one of the two options below.

  • Preferred: -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics. This turns off the fast Base64 decoder where the bug lives. Java falls back to its standard decoder, and everything else runs as before. Applications that decode large amounts of Base64 may run slower, so test first.
  • Alternative: -XX:UseAVX=2. This turns off a wider set of processor optimizations, including the vulnerable one, so the performance cost is broader. Use it only on Intel and AMD servers. Java on ARM does not accept this setting and will not start.

Neither option replaces the patch.

Either way, restart every Java process. A patch or a flag takes effect only when the JVM restarts, so verify the running process and not only the installed package. Do not rely on a reverse proxy as a control. Request buffering breaks some exploit chains but is not a general mitigation.

Reduce exposure while you wait for a patch. Take identity, build, and collaboration consoles off the open internet, or put them behind a VPN, until they are patched. CISA also suggests validating Base64 input and enforcing input-size limits at the application boundary. Size limits alone will not stop this bug, because the malformed input is very short. The JVM flag above is the more direct stopgap because it removes the vulnerable code.

Work in this order:

  1. Internet-facing identity providers such as Keycloak and PingFederate.
  2. Internet-facing Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and Artifactory.
  3. Other internet-facing Java services that handle logins, tokens, or file uploads.
  4. Internal Java systems, starting with Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker.

Assign an owner and a remediation deadline to every system that is waiting on a vendor build.

What to Watch For

CISA advises monitoring for rogue runtimes, unexpected JVM crashes, and suspicious Java processes. Qualys TRU suggests starting with these checks:

  • Unexpected JVM crashes or restarts on internet-facing Java services.
  • Java processes that start a shell or open outbound connections they have not made before.
  • Java runtimes on a host that your inventory does not account for.

How Qualys Can Help

Qualys helps you respond to Java4Shell: discover and assess exposure using Qualys CyberSecurity Asset Management (CSAM). It inventories Java installations across your assets and helps put internet-facing ones first.

Use the following CSAM query to identify potentially affected OpenJDK installations across Java 17, 21, 25, and 27 for further assessment.

software:(name:"OpenJDK" AND (
(version>=17.0.6 AND version<17.0.21.1) OR
(version>=21 AND version<21.0.13.1) OR
(version>=25 AND version<25.0.5.1) OR
(version>=27 AND version<27.0.1.1)
))

As distributions publish their own advisories, InstaScan turns them into findings without waiting for the next scheduled scan.

Detection QIDs

Qualys is releasing the following detection QIDs. We will add distribution-specific detection QIDs to this blog as they are released.

References

  • Calif: Java4Shell: Write once, RCE everywhere
  • Oracle: Critical Security Patch Update, November 2026
  • CISA: Critical Java Vulnerability Requires Immediate Patching: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/11/17/critical-java-vulnerability-requires-immediate-patching

The post Hacker Exploits Trader on Ethereum DEX Lighter, Looting $10,000,000 Worth of Crypto appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
A hacker looted $10 million worth of crypto from a trader operating on the Ethereum (ETH) decentralized exchange Lighter.

The blockchain security firm PeckShield published an alert about the hack early Monday morning, noting the hacker had already bridged 640 ETH, worth $1.12 million, to Hyperliquid to buy 2,240 Monero (XMR), a privacy coin.

Lighter temporarily suspended withdrawals to investigate the exploit, then resumed them several hours later. The project noted the incident was caused by a leaked API key for a specific trader’s account and didn’t impact its trading protocol, smart contracts or infrastructure.

“Every transaction on Lighter is authorized by a signature from an API key. Each signature uses a one-off random value called a nonce, which must be unique and unpredictable every time.

Signatures are public. If the same nonce is used with the same key to sign two different transactions, anyone can calculate the private key from those two signatures. After that, the key is exposed, and needs to be rotated.

This issue isn’t specific to Lighter – the above applies to Bitcoin and Ethereum signatures as well.”

Lighter’s native token, LIT, is trading at $2.74 at time of writing. The 86th-ranked crypto asset by market cap is down more than 3% in the past day and more than 17% in the past week, per data from CoinGecko.

title: Senate Democrats Push Back Against CFTC Prediction Market Rules
description: Senate Democrats are urging the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to reverse its latest directive on prediction markets, arguing that the regulator is pushing platforms to ignore existing court orders and state-level gambling restrictions. The dispute centers on the agency’s November 5 interpretation requiring designated contract markets to end geographic restrictions within 30 days. The […]
fullContent:
Senate Democrats are urging the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to reverse its latest directive on prediction markets, arguing that the regulator is pushing platforms to ignore existing court orders and state-level gambling restrictions.

The dispute centers on the agency’s November 5 interpretation requiring designated contract markets to end geographic restrictions within 30 days. The move could force platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket to offer certain event contracts nationwide, even in jurisdictions where courts have ordered them to block access.

In a letter sent on November 16, the lawmakers warned that the CFTC’s position conflicts with state and tribal laws and could encourage companies to violate active judicial decisions.

Senate Democrats Demand CFTC Withdraw Its Geofencing Directive

The letter was led by Senator Adam Schiff of California and signed by eight other Democrats, including Amy Klobuchar, Elissa Slotkin, Gary Peters, Maria Cantwell, Patty Murray, Catherine Cortez Masto, Jacky Rosen and Alex Padilla. The senators argued that the CFTC’s interpretation of federal derivatives rules effectively requires prediction market operators to disregard restrictions imposed by courts in several jurisdictions.

They pointed to decisions involving Michigan, Nevada and Washington, as well as tribal lands in California. Courts in these cases have ordered platforms to stop offering certain prediction contracts and maintain geographic restrictions around affected areas.

The lawmakers described the agency’s directive as incompatible with those rulings, warning that exchanges could be encouraged to offer contracts that judges have already determined violate applicable gambling laws.

They called on the CFTC to withdraw its interpretation or suspend its implementation until the ongoing legal disputes are resolved.

CFTC Chairman Mike Selig Defends Nationwide Market Access

The conflict stems from the CFTC’s position that federally regulated prediction markets should operate under a consistent national framework.

Chairman Mike Selig has argued that platforms registered as designated contract markets fall under federal derivatives law, which he believes takes precedence over state efforts to regulate their event contracts as gambling.

Under the agency’s November 5 interpretation, exchanges were told that restricting access based on a user’s location conflicts with federal impartial-access requirements. They were given 30 days to remove those restrictions or explain why they could not comply.

However, the senators disputed that interpretation, arguing that federal registration does not automatically override state and tribal gaming laws. They also cited decisions from the Sixth and Ninth Circuit Courts of Appeals supporting the ability of states to apply their gambling regulations to prediction market activity.

Louisiana and Arkansas Add to Prediction Market Legal Pressure

The regulatory dispute is expanding as more states challenge the industry’s business model.

Louisiana recently moved against prediction market operators, with a judge allowing state officials to pursue restrictions on certain event contracts. The state’s Gaming Control Board has previously argued that sports-related contracts and other event markets offered by these platforms constitute illegal gambling.

A temporary restraining order targeted several companies, including Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood, Coinbase, Gemini and Crypto.com. The CFTC responded by filing its own legal action to challenge the state’s restrictions, while some companies have sought to join the federal regulator’s case.

The agency is now involved in legal disputes with approximately a dozen states, reflecting how widely the disagreement over prediction market regulation has spread.

Supreme Court Could Ultimately Decide the Regulatory Dispute

The senators’ intervention comes at a significant moment for the CFTC and its oversight of prediction markets.

The commission currently has only one serving commissioner, Chairman Selig, despite being legally structured to have five members. The White House has nominated two additional candidates: Nathan Anonick, a Republican Senate Agriculture Committee staffer, and Matthew Rowland, a former senior adviser to a Democratic commissioner.

Meanwhile, conflicting court decisions could push the broader jurisdictional question toward the US Supreme Court. Until a clearer legal framework emerges, prediction market operators may continue facing uncertainty over whether federal derivatives rules or state gambling restrictions determine where their contracts can be offered.

The dispute is particularly important for platforms seeking to expand into mainstream financial markets, as access to users across different states remains central to their business models.

Do you think the CFTC should have exclusive authority over prediction markets, or should individual states retain the power to restrict these platforms? Could the growing legal conflict slow the expansion of Kalshi, Polymarket and other event-contract exchanges?

title: Senate Democrats Push Back Against CFTC Prediction Market Rules
description: Senate Democrats are urging the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to reverse its latest directive on prediction markets, arguing that the regulator is pushing platforms to ignore existing court orders and state-level gambling restrictions. The dispute centers on the agency’s November 5 interpretation requiring designated contract markets to end geographic restrictions within 30 days. The […]
fullContent:
Senate Democrats are urging the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to reverse its latest directive on prediction markets, arguing that the regulator is pushing platforms to ignore existing court orders and state-level gambling restrictions.

The dispute centers on the agency’s November 5 interpretation requiring designated contract markets to end geographic restrictions within 30 days. The move could force platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket to offer certain event contracts nationwide, even in jurisdictions where courts have ordered them to block access.

In a letter sent on November 16, the lawmakers warned that the CFTC’s position conflicts with state and tribal laws and could encourage companies to violate active judicial decisions.

Senate Democrats Demand CFTC Withdraw Its Geofencing Directive

The letter was led by Senator Adam Schiff of California and signed by eight other Democrats, including Amy Klobuchar, Elissa Slotkin, Gary Peters, Maria Cantwell, Patty Murray, Catherine Cortez Masto, Jacky Rosen and Alex Padilla. The senators argued that the CFTC’s interpretation of federal derivatives rules effectively requires prediction market operators to disregard restrictions imposed by courts in several jurisdictions.

They pointed to decisions involving Michigan, Nevada and Washington, as well as tribal lands in California. Courts in these cases have ordered platforms to stop offering certain prediction contracts and maintain geographic restrictions around affected areas.

The lawmakers described the agency’s directive as incompatible with those rulings, warning that exchanges could be encouraged to offer contracts that judges have already determined violate applicable gambling laws.

They called on the CFTC to withdraw its interpretation or suspend its implementation until the ongoing legal disputes are resolved.

CFTC Chairman Mike Selig Defends Nationwide Market Access

The conflict stems from the CFTC’s position that federally regulated prediction markets should operate under a consistent national framework.

Chairman Mike Selig has argued that platforms registered as designated contract markets fall under federal derivatives law, which he believes takes precedence over state efforts to regulate their event contracts as gambling.

Under the agency’s November 5 interpretation, exchanges were told that restricting access based on a user’s location conflicts with federal impartial-access requirements. They were given 30 days to remove those restrictions or explain why they could not comply.

However, the senators disputed that interpretation, arguing that federal registration does not automatically override state and tribal gaming laws.
