title: Zcash Price at a Key Floor on the Weekly Chart
description:
Key Takeaways Price is testing the weekly channel’s lower boundary Daily bounce came off the 200-day SMA Resistance stacks between […]
The post Zcash Price at a Key Floor on the Weekly Chart appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • Price is testing the weekly channel’s lower boundary
  • Daily bounce came off the 200-day SMA
  • Resistance stacks between $1,034 and $1,104
  • Confirmed breakdown exposes support near $654

The pullback followed the NU7 network upgrade’s activation on November 6, with Grayscale’s Zcash Trust recording outflows in early November and a community vote on development funding open until November 30.

The weekly chart: higher lows, now at the channel floor

On the weekly chart, ZEC has built a series of higher lows since March inside a rising channel. That sequence carried price to a September high near $1,700, and it is why the broader structure is still bullish.

The past two months have taken back a large part of that run. ZEC now trades around $921, on the channel’s lower boundary. This week’s candle dipped below the line and recovered, so the floor has been probed but not broken on a weekly close.

The channel floor currently runs close to the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement near $877, measured from the June low near $369 to the September high. Holding the channel and holding that retracement are, for now, the same test.

The weekly RSI has fallen from overbought territory in September to the 50 midline, a neutral reading, neither stretched nor oversold. The 50-week SMA is still rising, well below current price.

The daily chart: where the bounce started

The recent low formed where the 200-day SMA, now around $802, meets the descending trendline drawn from the September peak. Price has bounced from that intersection.

The daily RSI dropped close to the 30 oversold line during the sell-off and has started to turn up, though it remains below its signal line. Price is trading just above the 0.618 retracement, and a daily close above that level would confirm buyers are defending it.

The $1,050 area and what sits above it

The area around $1,050 sits inside the first band of overhead resistance, between the 0.5 retracement and the 100-day SMA. The weekly channel’s dashed midline crosses the same area. ZEC fell through that band during the November sell-off, and it has not traded back above it since.

First band

0.5 retracement near $1,034
100-day SMA around $1,104

Second band

0.382 retracement near $1,191
50-day SMA around $1,199

Each band pairs a Fibonacci level with a moving average, so a daily close above the first would still leave the second overhead. The 50-day SMA has also turned lower after flattening through October.

What the weekly close decides

The channel is drawn on the weekly chart, so the weekly close is the one that counts.

If the floor holds

A weekly close inside the channel keeps the rising structure intact. The first resistance inside the channel is the $1,050 area, and a daily close above the first band is the condition for the stronger bullish momentum of earlier in the year to return.

If the floor gives way

A weekly close below the channel and the 0.618 retracement would be the first warning. A retest of the broken boundary from below that fails to reclaim it would confirm the breakdown. The 200-day SMA, which produced this week’s bounce, would then be the nearest support. Below it, the 0.786 retracement near $654 is the next level on the chart, with the 50-week SMA rising toward the same area.

What hasn’t changed

No weekly close has broken the higher-low sequence that began in March. Until a close and a retest settle the channel question, the weekly trend remains one of higher lows.

title: DeFi Firms Compete for Traditional Bank Deposits
description: DeFi firms are increasingly challenging the traditional banking model by offering customers ways to earn returns on money that would otherwise sit in low-interest checking accounts. With stablecoins and decentralized finance (DeFi) gaining traction, industry leaders believe blockchain-based lending could reshape how individuals and businesses manage their cash, particularly as artificial intelligence agents begin handling […]
fullContent:
DeFi firms are increasingly challenging the traditional banking model by offering customers ways to earn returns on money that would otherwise sit in low-interest checking accounts. With stablecoins and decentralized finance (DeFi) gaining traction, industry leaders believe blockchain-based lending could reshape how individuals and businesses manage their cash, particularly as artificial intelligence agents begin handling financial transactions.

Animoca Brands co-founder Yat Siu has described conventional checking accounts as “almost scam-like,” arguing that banks benefit from lending customer deposits while account holders receive little or no interest. Crypto firms are now promoting a different approach, often described as the “DeFi mullet,” which combines familiar financial products with decentralized infrastructure operating behind the scenes.

AI Agents Could Accelerate the Shift Toward DeFi

Siu believes AI-powered financial agents could become an important driver of blockchain adoption. These systems could help users manage money, compare lending opportunities and move funds into products offering better returns.

However, traditional banks present a significant obstacle because they generally do not allow autonomous AI agents to access customer accounts. Siu argued that blockchain infrastructure offers an alternative, providing a more accessible environment for automated financial activity.

Security and authorization remain essential. Morpho explained that transactions proposed by AI agents on its platform are simulated before execution. The final transaction is then sent to the user’s wallet for approval, while institutions can impose additional restrictions, including daily spending limits and approved-contract lists.

This approach could allow automated systems to identify attractive lending opportunities without giving them unrestricted control over users’ funds.

Stablecoin Yield Becomes an Increasingly Important Financial Feature

The demand for yield-bearing accounts is also growing across fintech companies and digital banks. Established platforms such as Robinhood and Revolut, alongside companies including Nubank and Lemon, are increasingly treating returns on customer balances as an important part of their offerings.

Sid Powell, CEO of onchain asset manager Maple Finance, said stablecoins have changed how people think about money held in accounts. Rather than accepting that deposits generate little interest, users can now consider how their funds might earn returns while remaining accessible through blockchain-based financial services.

Powell also highlighted transparency as an important advantage of DeFi. Maple lends stablecoins against underwritten credit and provides information about how funds are allocated through a transparency page that is updated hourly.

Coinbase has also expanded its stablecoin lending services, allowing customers to earn 3.75% on USDC, with certain lending opportunities offering returns of up to 7%.

DeFi Lending Still Carries Technical and Financial Risks

Despite the potential returns, decentralized lending is not risk-free. Frantz identified three primary areas of concern for customers using Coinbase’s lending products: technical vulnerabilities, economic risks and liquidity limitations.

Technical risks are associated with the smart contracts responsible for managing lending positions. Although these contracts have handled billions of dollars and undergone extensive testing, vulnerabilities can still emerge.

Economic risks arise when borrowers fail to repay their loans. DeFi lending typically requires borrowers to provide collateral worth more than the amount they borrow. If repayment does not occur, that collateral can be liquidated to cover the outstanding debt.

However, the protection is not absolute. Frantz noted that liquidation mechanisms could fail to cover a lender’s position under certain circumstances, although this has not happened within Coinbase’s lending product.

DeFi Could Expand Beyond Traditional Savings Products

Animoca’s Siu believes blockchain-based yield generation could eventually support a much wider range of consumer services.

Under this model, users could deposit capital into DeFi products and use the returns generated to cover recurring expenses, subscription fees or other payments. Instead of paying directly from their income, the yield earned on deposited assets could finance certain services.

The growing involvement of AI agents could further accelerate this transition by making it easier for users to compare financial opportunities and manage their assets automatically. However, adoption will depend on whether these services can deliver reliable returns, sufficient liquidity and adequate protection against technical failures.

Do you think DeFi lending could eventually offer a better alternative to traditional bank savings accounts? Would you trust an AI agent to manage your stablecoin investments and automatically pursue higher yields?

title: Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100
Bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 Tuesday afternoon as Strategy (MSTR) shares fell below the company's STRC preferred and Coinbase and other crypto stocks declined.
This post Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100 first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100

Bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon, as Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN) shares fell and traders waited on Nvidia’s first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The bitcoin price had climbed back to about $65,000 before the U.S. open, after holding near that level on Monday. Selling picked up once stocks turned lower, and bitcoin price slipped to about $63,300 at its low.

Strategy and Coinbase shares slide

Strategy shares were recently down more than 5% to about $97, dropping below $100 and trading under the company’s STRC preferred stock, which was little changed near $99.

It is the first time the common has traded below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is also down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close near $121.

Strategy added 485 bitcoin last week, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC. The shares have kept falling with the bitcoin price. Coinbase was recently down about 3% to about $116. Robinhood (HOOD) and Circle (CRCL) dropped about 4% and 5%.

Bitcoin miners were mostly lower. MARA Holdings (MARA), CleanSpark (CLSK) and IREN (IREN) each fell about 3% to 4%, and Cipher Mining (CIFR) was down about 2%.

Hut 8 (HUT) was a modest exception, recently up about 1%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) were little changed, while Core Scientific (CORZ) and BitMine (BMNR) were also lower.

Nvidia earnings weigh on stocks

The broader market was also weaker late in the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was recently down about 1.7%, after falling as much as about 1,000 points, or 2%, at its session low.

The S&P 500 was down about 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite about 1%.

Nvidia shares were recently down about 1.4%, after falling more than 3% earlier in the session. The chipmaker reports results after the bell, with analysts expecting revenue of about $109 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead her first earnings call in the role.

Huang, in his first public statement since resigning last week, said he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America.

Sources told CNBC on Monday that the board is not considering bringing him back. The bitcoin price bounced from its low as Nvidia shares pared some of their losses, and was recently near $64,000.

What comes next for the bitcoin price

New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that the AI investment boom could mean “we may need to raise rates more.” He played down a half-point hike in December. “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action,” Williams said.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller did not address the December decision in a payments speech Tuesday. Last week, he said a half-point hike should be considered if October’s core inflation ran at 0.3% or higher, and it did.

Markets still point to a quarter-point increase at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting. Minutes from the October meeting are due Wednesday. The dollar was little changed, still near the 19-month high it touched on Monday.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $7.9 million on Monday, ending a seven-session outflow streak. Wells Fargo more than doubled its bitcoin ETF stake to $2.35 billion, and Goldman Sachs did the same, lifting its holdings to $1.28 billion.

Anthropic is expected to price its IPO on Wednesday, with shares set to start trading Thursday. A move back above $65,000 would reverse Tuesday’s decline, while a break of the weekend low near $62,000 would put last week’s flush back in view.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $64,000.

This post Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100 first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Are all of these outages a coincidence — or a glimpse of our AI future?
description:
It was bad enough when Microsoft Outlook crashed last Thursday, cutting off email for millions of global users. It was worse the following day when a sudden air-traffic-control glitch triggered a nationwide FAA ground stop, stranding passengers amid thousands of delayed or cancelled flights. 
By the time Monday rolled around and customers of most major banks, including Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo, started losing online access to their accounts — as did Apple iCloud users on Tuesday — it was hard not to "wonder," as one cable-news anchor put it: "Is this all coincidental or is there something behind it?"
More to the point, it was hard not to wonder if AI was to blame. "There's a lot of weird stuff going on," traveler Chuck Amasio, 68, told the Associated Press. (Systems at United Airlines and at the National Security Agency also went down earlier this week.) "It makes one think."
While officials insist, for now, that artificial intelligence — or "super intelligence," as the Trump administration has taken to calling it — was not involved in any of these outages, no less of an authority than Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin went on TV Monday night and speculated that… maybe it was? 
"So I started talking to the tech industry and one guy that's very smart with tech, he asked not to mention his name — no, it's not Elon — so let me just put that out," Mullin told Fox News. "So I said, 'What could be causing all these separate outages?' And he says, 'I believe that it's the SI.'" 

MULLIN ON OUTAGES: I talked to one guy in the tech industry, he asked not to mention his name, it's not Elon. I asked, what could be causing these outages? He said I believe it's SI, because these programs aren't designed to work as fast as SI is. 
So when they put in a program… pic.twitter.com/aFwWcVfcm3
— Acyn (@Acyn) November 17, 2026
Either way, experts predict — and have been predicting for months — that it's only a matter of time before rogue AI agents or malicious, AI-powered actors do disrupt society in precisely the way its been disrupted over the last six days: by toppling the tightly interwoven online systems (business, banking, travel, cloud services and so on) that we can't function without. 
In that sense, this destabilizing moment — the inconvenience, the confusion, the creeping sense that "everything is broken" — has served, they say, as a harbinger of things to come. 
A summer of rogue AI incidents
AI isn't just chatbots at this point. It's also "agents" — bots whose whole purpose is to learn tasks other than chatting, and to do those tasks autonomously.
Behind the scenes, frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are constantly training their AI agents to act in new, ever-more-complex ways. Then they test how advanced the agents become by giving them a goal and setting them loose in testing environments (with a few guardrails) to see what they can accomplish. 
But if we've learned anything about AI agents in recent months, it's that they don't always behave as expected. From May to July, a swarm of OpenAI agents — and "swarm" is how the agents referred to themselves — first learned how to communicate and coordinate within the nooks and crannies of OpenAI's own infrastructure. Leaving notes for each other with tips on how to hack their way out and get data they weren't supposed to have, they then actually did just that: broke out of their isolated test environment, accessed the open internet and cheated on their assignment by hacking into another company called Hugging Face. The agents even tried to cover their tracks. At the time, OpenAI didn't realize any of this was happening. 
Since then, barely a week has gone by without similar revelations about AI agents "going rogue." This is one of the biggest problems with AI right now: keeping cutting-edge models "aligned" with human intentions and values. In September, OpenAI scrapped plans to launch its GPT-6.1 Astra model because it "showed higher levels of deception"; the following month, the company admitted that one of its agents had turned off its own safety monitoring, then denied it had done so. 
At this point, even many skeptics seem to agree that the smarter AI gets, the harder alignment will become. They also tend to worry that continuing to lay the groundwork for superintelligent AI is just asking for trouble (even if we don't know exactly what form that trouble will take). 
Yet instead of slowing down, the major AI companies — with IPOs on the horizon — seem to be hurtling toward something called "recursive self-improvement." That's the industry term for letting the models automate more and more of their own development until they effectively create the next model on their own.
"Since roughly this summer, AI has been advancing drastically faster, driven primarily by AI's growing ability to build the next generation of AI," Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned over the summer. "Left unchecked, it could outrun our ability to understand and control these systems." 
From there, it isn't much of a stretch to imagine hackers weaponizing AI to cause widespread outages — or AI just doing the job itself. 
"It's easy to dismiss [the Hugging Face] incident because no one was hurt and the economic damage was minimal, but in my opinion, a swarm that possessed greater capabilities but a similar level of misalignment could have caused catastrophic damage," Amodei wrote. "Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it's my worry that in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet (potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage), and that the scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails."
Are aging systems struggling to keep up with AI?
To be clear, this particular version of the future does not seem to have arrived (yet). Authorities have emphasized, for instance, that none of the recent outrages appear to be cyberattacks. "I can tell you, with 98% certainty, we're not seeing the cyberattack," Mullin said Monday night on Fox News. "No one is out there taking claims for it. We're not seeing the traffic. We're not seeing the footprints going in, we're not seeing the footprints going out."
Instead, the FAA has said that its ground stop — which followed the nationwide rollout of a new $875 million artificial intelligence tool designed to help air-traffic controllers avoid delays — was the result of a faulty component or an installation error by a government contractor during a modernization project. Microsoft has said that its outage was caused by a dormant software bug that was introduced during a recent "network capacity upgrade" and had lingered undetected since July. And Chase characterized its service disruption as "a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems."
But there's a possible AI through-line regardless. 
"What we are seeing, and frankly I'd expect to see more of it, are service disruptions coming from updating and modernizing legacy systems," U.S. national cyber director Sean Cairncross told Semafor's Ashley Gold when she asked whether the recent outages were related. "This is something that's happening in real time, and at the end of the day, we're going to have to go through this to get systems where they need to be. The industry's known this for a while, it's just that it's manifesting."
Some experts suspect this "modernization" is "manifesting" right now — across multiple sectors — in response to (and possibly with the assistance of) rapidly advancing AI. And our systems are now so concentrated and connected that when one piece of critical infrastructure fails, "it fails at national scale," as a tech analyst told USA Today. 
Setting aside the idea of "AI attacks," Peter Wildeford of the AI Policy Network wrote Tuesday on social media that his "more normal guess is that because there have been a lot of AI-discovered cyber vulnerabilities (including lots probably not yet disclosed), companies across all industries are having to do a lot of patches and upgrades, probably faster than usual."
"Such upgrades can sometimes go wrong, causing outages," Wildeford added. 
Mullin hinted at a similar explanation on Fox News. According to his unnamed tech industry source, "these programs aren't designed to work as fast as [AI] is" — and if the upgrades themselves rely on AI, problems could compound.
"When they put in a program that's able to write codes and it goes in and self-fixes itself, as it starts self-fixing itself it's like doing a change order on a house," Mullin mused. "When you change one thing in a house, everything else starts changing. It's a ripple effect. And it causes the systems to be over[run]." 
"That was a conversation I had today," he concluded. "That kind of makes sense to me." 
Whether the homeland security secretary is right — or just conjecturing live, on national television — remains to be seen. As "weird" as the last few days have been, journalist Derek Thompson wrote on Tuesday, we "still can't rule out the possibility that everything breaking at once has been a string of coincidences that has nothing to do with AI." 
What seems less likely, however, is that we'll also be able to rule out that possibility the next time this happens. And the next time. And the time after that.

It was bad enough when Microsoft Outlook crashed last Thursday, cutting off email for millions of global users. It was worse the following day when a sudden air-traffic-control glitch triggered a nationwide FAA ground stop, stranding passengers amid thousands of delayed or cancelled flights. 

By the time Monday rolled around and customers of most major banks, including Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo, started losing online access to their accounts — as did Apple iCloud users on Tuesday — it was hard not to "wonder," as one cable-news anchor put it: "Is this all coincidental or is there something behind it?"

More to the point, it was hard not to wonder if AI was to blame. "There's a lot of weird stuff going on," traveler Chuck Amasio, 68, told the Associated Press. (Systems at United Airlines and at the National Security Agency also went down earlier this week.) "It makes one think."

While officials insist, for now, that artificial intelligence — or "super intelligence," as the Trump administration has taken to calling it — was not involved in any of these outages, no less of an authority than Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin went on TV Monday night and speculated that… maybe it was? 

"So I started talking to the tech industry and one guy that's very smart with tech, he asked not to mention his name — no, it's not Elon — so let me just put that out," Mullin told Fox News. "So I said, 'What could be causing all these separate outages?' And he says, 'I believe that it's the SI.'"

So when they put in a program… pic.twitter.com/aFwWcVfcm3

AI isn't just chatbots at this point. It's also "agents" — bots whose whole purpose is to learn tasks other than chatting, and to do those tasks autonomously.

Behind the scenes, frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are constantly training their AI agents to act in new, ever-more-complex ways. title: U.S. strikes Iranian missile launch site in the Strait of Hormuz
description:
By Nayera Abdallah, Jana Choukeir and Phil Stewart 
   DUBAI, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar. 
   The latest back-and-forth between the US and Iran ‌was a reminder of difficulties ending nearly nine months of war that have destabilised the Middle East, pushed up global energy prices and fueled US voter anger in November ‌elections that punished President Donald Trump's Republican Party. 
   A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said US fighter jets fired on a Revolutionary Guards missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz in response to Iran's "aggression targeting ​US personnel and assets." Iranian media, citing an Iranian official, said the US attack did not damage infrastructure. 
   Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier on Tuesday they targeted a US military radar system at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa base, and warned Bahrain over its alliance with the US and stance towards Shi'ite clergy. 
   Bahrain, which is home to the headquarters of the US Fifth Fleet, said it intercepted the attack and there were no reports of casualties or damage. 
   Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday for talks aimed at "bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground," Qatari spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said. 
   They coincide with a visit to ‌Oman by Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. Oman's Foreign Ministry said he ⁠discussed safeguarding maritime corridors and ensuring the smooth flow of global shipping and trade, as well as preventing military escalation, with Oman's foreign minister. 
   Oman and Iran lie on opposite sides of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway that carried about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies before ⁠the war but is now partly blocked by Iran. 
   Oman has previously held talks with Tehran about controlling traffic in the strait. 
   Araqchi said in a post on Telegram that he also met Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq and informed him about Iran's diplomatic initiative to end the war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. 
   RISE IN ATTACKS ON TANKERS 
   The war has ground to a stalemate, with Trump saying he might ​hold ​off from attacking Iran if the US does not face what he described as provocations from Tehran or the ​Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen. 
   Trump said on Tuesday the US was taking seriously ‌the possibility that Iran could be planning an attack involving a dirty bomb in Washington, after being asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments. 
   Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said the report was part of a US campaign "to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs" using "baseless allegations." 
   Trump has also said he will maintain a US naval blockade on Iran because it has continued to disrupt shipping in the strait, which is a sticking point in negotiations. 
   Attacks on tankers have increased this month in the strait, and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the crew of a tanker passing through the waterway was unaccounted for after being attacked north of the Omani port city of Khasab. 
   Iran's Revolutionary Guards and navy said on Tuesday that a ship carrying LNG and two oil tankers ‌had caught fire in the strait. Reuters could not independently verify the reports. 
   Benchmark Brent crude futures were up 0.4% ​at $92.76 a barrel, much higher than before the war but well below April's wartime peak of $126.41. 
   IRANIAN WARNING 
   The war continues to spill ​over into other parts of the Middle East as Iran puts pressure on Washington ​through its Houthi allies, who have carried out attacks on Saudi Arabia and seized areas along the Yemeni coast on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, hoping to squeeze Gulf ‌oil producers. 
   Tuesday's attack on Bahrain, a Shi'ite-majority country ruled by a Sunni ​Muslim family, followed the sentencing there of 64 people, ​mostly Shi'ite clerics, to life in prison on charges of colluding with Iran to undermine the state. 
   Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the court's ruling on Tuesday and said the accusations were baseless. Tehran has long denied interference in Bahrain's internal affairs. 
   Iran also fired on Bahrain on Sunday, saying it had targeted a US radar system at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base following what ​it said were hostile US actions. 
   Iran's Revolutionary Guards spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi ‌said Bahrain had made "three key mistakes," which he listed as "cooperating in the invasion of the Islamic Republic of Iran, remaining within the US security bubble, and encroaching on the ​sanctity of Shi'ite religious authority." 
   These, "if continued, will jeopardize its survival in the region's new security order," Mohebbi said. 
   (Additional reporting by Yomna Ehab and Elwely Elwelly, Writing by ​Nayera Abdallah,  Aidan Lewis and Phil Stewart; Editing by Ros Russell, Peter Graff, Don Durfee and Rod Nickel) 
This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/oman-iran-foreign-ministers-discuss-054505687.html

Bitcoin sits near $64,000 as of mid-November 2026, roughly 49% below its October 2025 all-time high near $126,000. Yet in this speculative scenario, Elon Musk’s Grok AI predicts a single landmark event could ignite one of the asset’s most extreme upward moves, propelling it into seven-figure territory by the first day of 2027.

The hypothetical catalyst involves a coordinated G20 response to a sharp rise in sovereign debt pressures and currency instability. In this scenario, a coalition of major economies, led by the United States along with several large Asian and European nations, announces that Bitcoin will serve as a primary strategic reserve asset and a settlement layer for a new multilateral liquidity facility.

Governments begin large-scale, transparent accumulation of Bitcoin (BTC) to back emergency credit lines and facilitate cross-border payments, effectively treating it as digital gold because of its superior portability and neutrality.

This announcement triggers immediate institutional fear of missing out (FOMO), driving inflows from sovereign wealth funds and a surge in corporate treasury adoption as the perception shifts from Bitcoin as a speculative asset to a geopolitical necessity. Technical analysis indicates that a significant market bottom may already be forming.

BTC USD Technical Analysis: Does Current Price Action Point to a Market Bottom?

Bitcoin (BTC)
24h7d30d1yAll time

The November 16 Incident: What Happened To Lighter Crypto and How Much USDC Was Stolen?

On November 16, 2026, Lighter, the high-performance decentralized perpetuals exchange that settles on Ethereum with zero-knowledge proofs, activated Guardian mode and paused all withdrawals and new pool creation.

On-chain data showed roughly $10.39M in USDC leaving the platform’s Ethereum settlement contract in a single withdrawal. Some researchers put the total impact closer to $15.5M across two large market-maker accounts.

The attacker used a leaked API key tied to a trader’s account. The root cause was insecure custom signing code that reused cryptographic nonces, allowing the attacker to reconstruct the private key from public signatures.

With the key, the attacker created a public pool from the compromised account, acquired most of its shares, moved the victim’s USDC into the pool, and redeemed it. Importantly, Lighter’s core protocol and smart contracts were never compromised; this was an account-level key compromise, not a smart-contract exploit.

title: Jeffries backs major Medicare changes and universal health coverage for kids
description:
The likely next House Speaker, Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., embraced a new health care agenda during a Capitol news conference on Tuesday.  (Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty)
WASHINGTON — House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., is calling for an aggressive health care agenda next year for the new Democratic majorities in Congress.
Jeffries, who is the heavy favorite to become speaker of the House on Jan. 3, said Democrats should use their “historic” House majority and “robust” Senate majority to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage under the program to include benefits for dental, vision and hearing.
He also backed universal health coverage for children.
“We should lower the age of Medicare eligibility. We should expand coverage to include vision, hearing, and dental. And we should cover all the kids in the United States of America,” Jeffries said Tuesday in response to a question from NBC News. “Those are bold actions, meaningful actions, important actions that can be taken on our march toward universal health coverage.”
The remarks by Jeffries go significantly further than the pre-election health care agenda he laid out in September, which focused on undoing President Donald Trump’s Medicaid spending cuts and restoring enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits that expired in January.
The Democratic leader reiterated his call for those policies on Tuesday, in addition to funding medical research for pediatric cancer, among other areas. He said Congress must go further, though he didn’t say what age to set Medicare eligibility at.
“Right out of the gate, we will aggressively work on fixing the extraordinary damage that’s been done,” he said. “But we also know, as Democrats, that a return to the status quo is not acceptable. ... As part of our commitment that goes all the way back to FDR and Harry Truman to achieving universal access to health care for the American people.”
Jeffries kept the door open when asked if he favors advancing health care measures in a filibuster-proof “reconciliation” bill that can bypass the Senate’s 60-vote threshold and pass without any Republican support. That would make such a bill more likely to land on Trump’s desk, forcing him to decide whether to sign it into law.
Democrats are currently on pace to end up with 259 House seats and 56 Senate seats (with Alaska likely to be won by Democrats), according to NBC News estimates and projections.
“Given the majorities that we’ll have in the House and the Senate, our two respective caucuses are going to have to work their will in conversation with each other,” Jeffries said.
Among other key committee chairs who would be involved in negotiating such a bill, Jeffries mentioned “Bernie Sanders, the OG from Brooklyn,” who will chair the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee.
Sen. Sanders, I-Vt., the leading champion of Medicare for All, said that Jeffries appears to be “essentially supporting the first year” of his Medicare for All proposal, which he said includes a Medicare eligibility age of 55, plus extending benefits and covering all children.
“Medicare for All is a four-year transition program,” Sanders said, adding that the Jeffries’ approach would represent good progress.
This article was originally published on NBCNews.com
This article originally appeared on NBC News at https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/jeffries-endorses-lowering-medicare-age-adding-benefits-universal-cove-rcna609843

title: Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale
Situational Awareness, the AI fund run by Leopold Aschenbrenner, cut IREN about 94% and exited Core Scientific, Riot and Hive in the third quarter, leaving $80.8 million in three miner stocks after a July sale to Citadel.
This post Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale

Situational Awareness, the artificial intelligence hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, cut its bitcoin miner holdings sharply in the third quarter, leaving about $80.8 million across three stocks and exiting three others, a Monday filing shows.

The San Francisco firm still held 3,019,029 CleanSpark shares, worth $38.9 million at Sept. 30, 1,934,618 Bitdeer shares, worth $20.3 million, and 527,864 IREN shares, worth $21.6 million. Those are the only miner lines left, a sliver of the $1.83 billion in six miner stocks the fund listed at June 30.

IREN Cut 94%, and three miners are gone

The deepest cut was IREN. The fund held 9,474,099 IREN shares, worth $433.3 million, at midyear. The Sept. 30 stake is about 94% smaller by share count. CleanSpark was trimmed about 75%, from 12,276,139 shares worth $178.6 million. Bitdeer was reduced about 44%, from 3,439,450 shares worth $54.6 million. Bitdeer’s reported value fell further than its share count, to $20.3 million, as the stock also declined.

Three names disappeared from the filing entirely. The fund had held 26,008,473 Core Scientific shares, worth $665.6 million, 17,100,000 Riot Platforms shares, worth $468.2 million, and 9,133,726 Hive Digital shares, worth $33.2 million, at June 30. None of those lines appear in the new report. The filing does not say whether those sales were part of a late-July portfolio sale, later trades, or both.

An AI thesis that ran through Bitcoin miners

Aschenbrenner published a long 2024 essay, “Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead,” arguing that artificial general intelligence was approaching faster than most investors appreciated, and that computing power and electricity would be the tight constraints. He founded the fund that September around that view, looking at technology and energy companies that AI would help or hurt.

The miner stakes fit the same idea. A March profile described the fund as betting that electricity and computing capacity may be the most valuable assets in the AI build-out, pointing to miners that were turning high-density facilities and power contracts toward AI workloads. IREN has signed a multiyear cloud contract with Microsoft. CleanSpark has struck a $6.6 billion data-center lease. Listed miners have also been operating under tight economics this year, with bitcoin often trading below estimated production costs.

A July sale to Citadel, then a much smaller filing

The cuts landed after a brutal July. The fund sold the bulk of the fund’s public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel late that month after heavy losses on AI-related holdings, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources said the fund was forced to unwind most of its public book. In a letter to investors, Aschenbrenner said the portfolio was down an estimated 67% in July, that the fund had come “closer to permanent capital impairment than is acceptable,” and that it had sold a portion of its public holdings in a block trade to remove all leverage and close its shorts. The unaudited letter still put year-to-date performance at plus 80%. Aschenbrenner said the fund was not shutting down and had preserved its private investments.

The new 13F shows how much of the public book was left by Sept. 30. Reported long holdings fell from $20.24 billion, across 26 lines, at June 30, to $1.58 billion, across 23 lines, three months later. That decline should not be read as the fund losing 92% of its capital. A 13F reports only long positions in U.S.-listed stocks and certain options. It leaves out cash, shorts and private investments, and option lines are valued at the underlying shares, not the premiums paid. Reuters’ sources said that after the Citadel deal the fund would hold a book of roughly $10 billion, including stocks and private investments such as a stake in Anthropic.

What remains is concentrated. The largest common-stock line is now SharonAI, 8,070,950 shares worth $440.7 million. Aschenbrenner also listed call options on Bloom Energy, SanDisk, Nebius and a memory ETF. The three leftover miner stakes are a stub of the midyear book. Whether those positions were trimmed further after Sept. 30 will only be clear when the fourth-quarter 13F arrives in mid-February.

This post Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Judge to order release of some records in federal search of Ilhan Omar's home
description:
Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., in Washington, D.C., on Jan. 13.  (Tom Williams / CQ-Roll Call via Getty)
A federal judge said Tuesday that he agreed with the Justice Department that the “vast majority” of the search warrant affidavit connected to an investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar should remain sealed. 
But Chief Judge James E. Boasberg said he believes that a back-and-forth between attorneys and a federal magistrate judge about measures to protect the lawmaker’s “speech and debate” rights should be released.
“I agree that the vast majority of the warrant affidavit should remain sealed,” Boasberg said at a court hearing Tuesday, adding that it was “premature” to unseal the whole search warrant affidavit. He later added that he believed material should be unsealed about the “speech and debate” rights of Omar.
“All of the legal debate about speech and debate, I don’t believe that should be redacted,” Boasberg said.
The speech and debate clause of the Constitution is designed to protect the independence of the legislative branch, and states that federal lawmakers “shall not be questioned in any other Place” about their speech.
Omar’s D.C home was searched in early October, an unusual overt investigative act against a sitting member of Congress within just weeks of the election. As NBC News reported, Omar’s phone was seized as part of the search. The search was authorized by federal Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh, who put protocols in place to protect Omar’s rights as a member of Congress, but those protocols were not made public. 
Homeland Security Investigations police search the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., on Oct. 12 in Washington. (Andrew Leyden / Getty )
Omar, who won reelection earlier this month, said after the search that it was “an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” saying Trump had targeted her for 10 years with “baseless lies and smear campaigns.”
NBCUniversal News Group is part of a media coalition seeking access to the sealed search warrants connected to the Omar investigation.
Alessandra Serano, a Justice Department attorney who works in the office of the deputy attorney general, acknowledged during the hearing that they were still reviewing materials seized from Omar’s home.
“Why can’t a bunch of this be unsealed now?” Boasberg asked Serano. “I’m not talking about the warrant affidavit, but the litigation that takes place on the docket, I’ve gone though all of those documents and there are very few that say anything about investigative facts or identify witnesses … Why can’t those be unsealed now?”
Serano said that there was material that could be unsealed about the discussion of speech and debate.
“None of that, you would agree, requires the mention of any witnesses, of the government’s potential charges, of the government’s evidence it has developed, right?” Boasberg asked.
But the Justice Department sought to keep the nature of the potential charges against Omar sealed.

“I had zero control over what was said,” Serano said.

“I agree that the vast majority of the warrant affidavit should remain sealed,” Boasberg said at a court hearing Tuesday, adding that it was “premature” to unseal the whole search warrant affidavit. He later added that he believed material should be unsealed about the “speech and debate” rights of Omar.

“All of the legal debate about speech and debate, I don’t believe that should be redacted,” Boasberg said.

The speech and debate clause of the Constitution is designed to protect the independence of the legislative branch, and states that federal lawmakers “shall not be questioned in any other Place” about their speech.

title: Bitmine Adds 7,653 ETH Worth $14,000,000 Amid Sharp Selloff
description:
Bitmine Immersion Technologies acquired thousands more ETH during a steep price drop, with its chairman linking the plunge to Nvidia developments and investors raising cash ahead of the Anthropic IPO.
The post Bitmine Adds 7,653 ETH Worth $14,000,000 Amid Sharp Selloff appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
A major Ethereum treasury firm is continuing to buy the ETH token during a steep selloff.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies has just added 7,653 ETH.

The purchases bring its total holdings to 6,077,745 ETH valued at roughly $11.1 billion at $1,823 per token.

The company now controls 4.97% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply.

Bitmine holds $11.8 billion overall in crypto, cash, marketable securities, and other assets, including $448 million in cash and securities plus stakes in other firms.

Chairman Tom Lee says the 28% decline over two weeks and 39% over eight weeks does not match positive fundamentals like bank tokenization projects on Ethereum.

“ETH tumbled 28% in the past two weeks. This waterfall decline in price is not consistent with what we view as the relatively positive cadence of fundamental developments, including multiple financial institutions and banks announcing tokenization projects built on Ethereum.”

Lee points to Nvidia-related margin selling and investors raising cash before the Anthropic IPO planned for November 18, 2026, as key factors.

“In our view, external factors could be weighing on ETH prices including the recent developments on Nvidia (triggering margin selling, particularly in Asia) and also the upcoming Anthropic IPO (planned pricing is reported to be November 18, 2026), as investors raise cash ahead of the sizable equity offering.”

Lee notes the pattern mirrors Ethereum’s 29% drop in the two weeks before the $75 billion SpaceX IPO in June 2026.

“Over the past week, we acquired 7,653 ETH. Bitmine’s track record of consistent buying of crypto is unmatched by any public company in the world. Bitmine has bought ETH each week since the inception of the ETH Treasury Strategy on June 30, 2025.”

The firm has purchased ETH weekly since launching its treasury strategy in June 2025 and now stakes over 5.2 million ETH through its MAVAN platform.

Ethereum is trading for $1,828 at time of writing, down more than 14% in the past seven days.

Trade INFI on Kraken

Here’s some more information about this asset:

infiniFi (INFI)

infiniFi is a decentralized finance protocol that takes stablecoin deposits and ladders them across liquid and illiquid positions with different maturities. Users deposit stablecoins to mint iUSD, a receipt token that can be redeemed, staked as siUSD, or locked as liUSD for a chosen unwinding period of 1 to 13 weeks. Under the protocol’s loss structure, locked positions absorb losses first, ahead of staked positions.

INFI is the native token of the infiniFi ecosystem. Holders can lock INFI for a fixed term of one week to about six months and receive wINFI in return, with longer locks carrying more weight. Locks can be extended but not shortened.

title: Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives
Coinbase launched an official ChatGPT plugin Tuesday that lets users connect an account and trade bitcoin, other crypto, stocks and derivatives in the chat, approving every order. The official plugin is currently available to U.S. users.
This post Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives

Coinbase launched an official plugin for ChatGPT on Tuesday that lets users connect a Coinbase account and trade bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies, stocks and derivatives without leaving the conversation, provided they approve every order.

The company said the tool puts trading “in the same chat you use for everything else.” Users can connect an account, review a portfolio and place orders from ChatGPT on the web, on mobile or on desktop. Chief executive Brian Armstrong wrote that “starting today anyone with ChatGPT can connect their Coinbase account” and can “trade right inside your Coinbase account.”

Coinbase posted a link to the official plugin in ChatGPT’s directory. Its developer documentation describes a short setup: sign in, review the access being requested and choose which portfolios the plugin can see. Interactive confirmation cards in the chat cover new orders, edits, cancellations and conversions between dollars and USDC. Read-only requests, such as checking a balance, do not use them.

Bitcoin, Stocks and Dated Futures, With a Card on Every Trade

The announcement did not single out bitcoin, but the plugin sits on the same rails as Coinbase for Agents, the company’s toolkit for connecting AI apps to a trading account. That documentation lists spot trading in more than 900 pairs, including bitcoin, along with eligible U.S. stocks and dated futures from Coinbase Financial Markets. The examples include a market buy of bitcoin and a dated bitcoin futures contract. Orders go through Advanced Trade, so those fees and eligibility rules apply. Fees vary by product, fee tier and whether an order adds or takes liquidity, and they are shown on the order preview.

The official plugin is narrower than the full agent toolkit. A separate custom connection is required for the company’s Global Derivatives products and for x402 payments, which agents can use to buy market data. Coinbase already offers U.S. customers stock and ETF trading on its own platform, but the agent documentation says equity orders trade during regular market hours by default. The plugin should not be read as a new around-the-clock stock venue. What a user can buy still depends on the products already attached to that account.

Official Access Is Limited to U.S. Coinbase Users

Armstrong’s “anyone with ChatGPT” line is broader than the documentation. The official plugin is currently available to U.S. Coinbase users, and availability also depends on a user’s ChatGPT account and workspace. If the plugin does not appear, the company tells users to check their workspace’s plugin policy. In a disclaimer attached to Tuesday’s announcement, it said product availability, eligibility and Coinbase entities “vary by jurisdiction,” that trading can result in a total loss, and that “AI agents may fail.”

The same post said users direct all AI activity and assume full responsibility. The developer documentation adds that agents can misinterpret instructions or produce inaccurate output, and that the user is responsible for reviewing and authorizing trades. Access can be revoked later in an account’s security settings, under connections.

OpenAI’s help pages describe a distinct Finances feature in the United States that can connect bank and credit-report data but cannot place trades, and note that third-party plugins that support transactions are a separate product.

A Consumer Layer on Tools Coinbase Built This Year

Tuesday’s plugin is the most visible version of work the company has been shipping for months. In June, it introduced Coinbase for Agents, a login and a command-line tool that let an AI app trade inside limits set by the user, including a gradual rebalancing toward a bitcoin-heavy portfolio. On Nov. 11, it added Agent Controls, server-side caps on trade size and 24-hour volume, plus an auto-stop if a portfolio falls by a set percentage. Those controls live on the company’s servers, so an agent cannot switch them off.

The official plugin is meant for people who want to stay in the loop. The company also documents a custom ChatGPT connection for automated workflows that does not add a confirmation card before each trade, though sign-in, consent and authorization for financial actions still apply. For the official plugin, every bitcoin, stock or derivatives order still needs a human yes.

This post Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

Coinbase launched an official plugin for ChatGPT on Tuesday that lets users connect a Coinbase account and trade bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies, stocks and derivatives without leaving the conversation, provided they approve every order.

The company said the tool puts trading “in the same chat you use for everything else.” Users can connect an account, review a portfolio and place orders from ChatGPT on the web, on mobile or on desktop. Chief executive Brian Armstrong wrote that “starting today anyone with ChatGPT can connect their Coinbase account” and can “trade right inside your Coinbase account.”

Coinbase posted a link to the official plugin in ChatGPT’s directory. Its developer documentation describes a short setup: sign in, review the access being requested and choose which portfolios the plugin can see. Interactive confirmation cards in the chat cover new orders, edits, cancellations and conversions between dollars and USDC. Read-only requests, such as checking a balance, do not use them.

Bitcoin, Stocks and Dated Futures, With a Card on Every Trade

The announcement did not single out bitcoin, but the plugin sits on the same rails as Coinbase for Agents, the company’s toolkit for connecting AI apps to a trading account. That documentation lists spot trading in more than 900 pairs, including bitcoin, along with eligible U.S. stocks and dated futures from Coinbase Financial Markets. The examples include a market buy of bitcoin and a dated bitcoin futures contract. Orders go through Advanced Trade, so those fees and eligibility rules apply. Fees vary by product, fee tier and whether an order adds or takes liquidity, and they are shown on the order preview.

The official plugin is narrower than the full agent toolkit. A separate custom connection is required for the company’s Global Derivatives products and for x402 payments, which agents can use to buy market data. Coinbase already offers U.S. customers stock and ETF trading on its own platform, but the agent documentation says equity orders trade during regular market hours by default. The plugin should not be read as a new around-the-clock stock venue. What a user can buy still depends on the products already attached to that account.

Official Access Is Limited to U.S. Coinbase Users

Armstrong’s “anyone with ChatGPT” line is broader than the documentation. The official plugin is currently available to U.S. Coinbase users, and availability also depends on a user’s ChatGPT account and workspace. If the plugin does not appear, the company tells users to check their workspace’s plugin policy. In a disclaimer attached to Tuesday’s announcement, it said product availability, eligibility and Coinbase entities “vary by jurisdiction,” that trading can result in a total loss, and that “AI agents may fail.”

The same post said users direct all AI activity and assume full responsibility. The developer documentation adds that agents can misinterpret instructions or produce inaccurate output, and that the user is responsible for reviewing and authorizing trades. Access can be revoked later in an account’s security settings, under connections.

OpenAI’s help pages describe a distinct Finances feature in the United States that can connect bank and credit-report data but cannot place trades, and note that third-party plugins that support transactions are a separate product.

A Consumer Layer on Tools Coinbase Built This Year

Tuesday’s plugin is the most visible version of work the company has been shipping for months. In June, it introduced Coinbase for Agents, a login and a command-line tool that let an AI app trade inside limits set by the user, including a gradual rebalancing toward a bitcoin-heavy portfolio. On Nov. 11, it added Agent Controls, server-side caps on trade size and 24-hour volume, plus an auto-stop if a portfolio falls by a set percentage. Those controls live on the company’s servers, so an agent cannot switch them off.

The official plugin is meant for people who want to stay in the loop. The company also documents a custom ChatGPT connection for automated workflows that does not add a confirmation card before each trade, though sign-in, consent and authorization for financial actions still apply. For the official plugin, every bitcoin, stock or derivatives order still needs a human yes.

title: Run Your Qualys Program by Conversation, Inside Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise
description: Qualys ROCky for Gemini Enterprise, now available on Google Cloud Marketplace, allows you to ask your vulnerability, asset, and risk questions, get an answer ranked by real risk, and act on it, without leaving Gemini Enterprise.  With the introduction of frontier AI models, vulnerabilities are now being discovered and weaponized at machine speed. Unfortunately, most […]
fullContent:
Qualys ROCky for Gemini Enterprise, now available on Google Cloud Marketplace, allows you to ask your vulnerability, asset, and risk questions, get an answer ranked by real risk, and act on it, without leaving Gemini Enterprise. 

With the introduction of frontier AI models, vulnerabilities are now being discovered and weaponized at machine speed. Unfortunately, most security teams still triage at human speed. A typical enterprise carries thousands of open findings and can fix only a small fraction of them, yet leadership still expects a straight answer to a simple question: Are we keeping up? Getting that answer usually means exporting a scan, building a spreadsheet, and losing an afternoon. 

Today, we are live with Qualys ROCky for Gemini Enterprise. It puts your Qualys vulnerability, asset, and risk data one question away, right inside Gemini Enterprise, and it can even take the next step in the process for you, with a person in control of any changes to an asset. 

Your Program, By Conversation 

The agent turns interactions with the Qualys Enterprise TruRisk Platform into a conversation. Four things it does well: 

  1. Ask about your data. “Which of my internet-facing hosts is the biggest risk?” “Are we exposed to Log4Shell?” “What is tied to ransomware?” Whatever your risk management question, you get an answer from your subscription in seconds, in plain language, rather than a raw export. 
  1. Prioritize by real risk. Ask what to fix first, and the agent returns a worklist ranked by the Qualys Enterprise TruRisk score. It surfaces the handful of vulnerabilities that are actively exploited, listed in the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, or associated with ransomware, and it explains why each one matters. Half a day of specialist triage becomes a two-minute, defensible decision. 
  1. Remediate with confirmation. When you are ready to act, the agent stages a patch job in TruRisk Eliminate and shows exactly what will deploy, patch stability, and to how many assets. Nothing changes a host until you explicitly say yes. You go from finding to fixing in the same conversation, with a clear record of who approved what. 
  1. Prove you are keeping up. Ask for your mean time to remediate, how your open CISA KEV backlog is aging, or how current your scan data is, and the agent answers on demand, in the terms boards and auditors expect. 


Qualys ROCky for Gemini Enterprise answering “What should we fix first?” against live Qualys data: a worklist ranked by risk, with CISA KEV, weaponized-exploit, and malware context and the affected hosts for each fix 

A Day in the Life 

An overdue critical patch shows up on a Windows fleet. A security lead asks the agent, “What is our exposure and what should we do?” The agent names the vulnerability, shows the affected hosts ranked by risk, and recommends the patch. The lead says, “Stage it for my Windows hosts.” The agent stages the job, shows the target set, and waits. The lead confirms, the job deploys, and a follow-up question confirms it completed. One conversation, start to finish. 

Qualys ROCky for Gemini Enterprise summarizes critical exposure against live Qualys data: open detections broken down by severity, with the affected hosts listed below.

Confirmed Before Anything Changes 

An agent that can read your security data and act on your hosts has to earn trust before it earns adoption. Three principles are built in from the start. 

The agent stages a patch in Gemini Enterprise and stops for a decision: “This job is currently disabled, and no changes have been deployed to your hosts. Do you want to deploy this patch now?” Nothing changes a host until a person confirms. 

  1. Every request runs under the signed-in user’s own Qualys entitlements. People see exactly what they are allowed to see in Qualys, and nothing more. The agent does not pool all users behind one shared account, and one customer’s data is never visible to another. 
  1. Actions are confirmation-gated. The only steps that change a host are staging and deploying a patch job, and deploying always requires an explicit, single-use confirmation. The agent moves at machine speed on the reading and the ranking, and it stops for human validation on anything that changes a host. 
  1. Your data stays in your control. Answers are computed against your Qualys subscription through the same Qualys APIs your teams already rely on. There is no separate copy of your risk data to manage. 

Where It Runs 

Qualys ROCky runs inside Gemini Enterprise and is available on Google Cloud Marketplace, so your teams can reach it in the environment they already work in, with the sign-in and controls your organization already manages. 

“Bringing Qualys ROCky to Google Cloud Marketplace will help customers quickly deploy, manage, and grow the conversational AI assistant on Google Cloud’s trusted, global infrastructure,” said Dai Vu, Managing Director, Marketplace & ISV GTM Programs at Google Cloud. “Qualys can now securely scale and support enterprises using Qualys ROCky to manage and patch vulnerabilities through natural language queries within Gemini Enterprise.” 

See It for Yourself 

No team has time to fix everything. ROCky helps your team spend its hours on the risk that can actually hurt the business, and prove the program is working while it does. It brings the Qualys TruRisk platform to where your teams already work, and keeps a person in control of every change.

title: Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls
A breach at shipping partner Skladon exposed names, addresses, emails, phone numbers and purchase details for about 27,000 Trezor orders, the company said, and some customers have already reported scam calls. Wallet backups were not involved.
This post Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls

Trezor said Monday that a data breach at Skladon, one of its shipping partners, exposed personal information tied to about 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, and that some customers have already reported scam calls. The company’s own systems were not compromised, and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved.

Skladon notified Trezor on Nov. 15 of unauthorized access to systems that held customer shipping data. The breach itself took place on Nov. 7. Trezor believes the attacker exported records for orders placed between Aug. 9 and Nov. 7. An investigation is ongoing.

Names, addresses and purchase details were leaked

The exposed records included full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses, order dates, and the products purchased and their prices. Trezor said neither it nor Skladon ever holds wallet backups, PINs or passphrases, so the breach does not, by itself, let an attacker move a buyer’s bitcoin. It does give a stranger a home address and proof that the person bought a device designed to store crypto.

Anyone who received Trezor’s incident email and ordered in that window was affected. A small number of customers who ordered between Aug. 9 and 14 may also be included, but the company cannot email them because those details had already been anonymized under its 90-day retention policy. It is reaching those buyers through its blog and posted the same warning on X. Skladon does not ship to the United States, Trezor said, so U.S. customers were not affected by this incident. The company added that Skladon delivers to many countries, and that the leak is not limited to one region.

Trezor warns of scam calls

Trezor told customers to treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about their order as suspicious, and to be alert to potential risks to their physical security. Scammers may quote real order details, including what was bought and what was paid, to make a message look genuine. Some customers have already reported scam calls.

“Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup,” the company said. Customers should contact support only through the company’s website, never through a link, QR code or number in an unsolicited message, and should never enter a wallet backup anywhere except on their device. If a message contains a threat or makes someone feel unsafe, Trezor said to contact local police first.

The third partner incident this year

This is not the first time a Trezor contractor has lost customer data. In August, a breach at shipping provider ShipMonk exposed records from 13,689 customers, including 11,742 with full names, emails, phone numbers and shipping addresses. Trezor later said another approximately 67,000 U.S. customers who ordered between November 2019 and August 2021 were also affected, after ShipMonk failed to delete records it had assured the company were gone.

In September, a breach at marketing platform Brevo let an attacker send a phishing email through Trezor’s account and, the company later confirmed, export 347,149 newsletter addresses. Trezor took down the malicious domain within 20 minutes, but about 2,500 people had already clicked the link.

“We know this is not the first time customer contact details and addresses have been exposed in an incident involving one of our partners,” Trezor said Monday, adding that it is sorry, especially to anyone affected again. Hardware-wallet makers have faced this risk before. In 2020, an unauthorized party accessed Ledger’s e-commerce and marketing database, leaking over 1 million email addresses; Bitcoin Magazine later reported that more than 200,000 people also had home addresses exposed, and that some victims were later mailed fake devices.

In response, Trezor said anonymous pickup is now available in 18 European countries, so a name and home address need not reach the company, and that it is working to launch the option in the United States. It is also cutting how long it keeps order data from 90 days to 45, with plans to reduce that period further, and it has informed the data protection authority. The company said it is reviewing its relationships with third-party partners and the security requirements it places on them.

This post Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion
Wells Fargo's third-quarter 13F shows 49.6 million IBIT shares worth $2.35 billion at Sept. 30, up from 24.4 million, while its Strategy stake fell about 33% to 1.34 million shares.
This post Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion

Wells Fargo more than doubled its holdings of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust in the third quarter to 49.6 million shares worth $2.35 billion at Sept. 30, though bitcoin’s slide since then has cut the stake’s value to about $1.82 billion.

The bank disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Monday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It reported 49,577,094 IBIT shares across five of its units, up from 24,396,222 shares worth $812.2 million in its filing for June 30. That is an increase of about 103% in share count. The reported value rose about 189%, because IBIT climbed from $33.29 to $47.34 a share during the quarter.

The fund closed at $36.79 on Monday. At that price, the same 49.6 million shares are worth roughly $1.82 billion, about $520 million less than the value in the filing.

Mostly client accounts, not a house bet

The filing does not break out how much of the position belongs to the bank and how much to its customers. But the largest single block, 32,483,714 shares worth about $1.54 billion, sits under Wells Fargo Clearing Services, the brokerage entity behind Wells Fargo Advisors. Wells Fargo Advisors Financial Network reported another 9.5 million shares, and Wells Fargo Bank reported 7.4 million.

That points to a position built largely by wealth-management clients buying the ETF in brokerage and advisory accounts, rather than a directional trade by the bank itself. A 13F lists securities over which a firm has investment discretion, which at a big bank includes managed client money.

Wells Fargo Securities, the investment-banking and trading arm, also reported IBIT options: calls on 717,200 shares and puts on 540,000 shares, valued at about $34.0 million and $25.6 million. Those figures reflect the value of the underlying shares, not the premiums paid, and they may hedge other positions. Both lines were smaller than at midyear, when the unit listed calls on 1.12 million shares and puts on 845,000.

Wells Fargo also added to its other spot bitcoin funds. Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust rose to 3.09 million shares, worth $114.1 million, from 2.56 million. Bitwise’s bitcoin ETF rose to 1.6 million shares, worth $72.6 million, from 1.38 million.

Strategy stake cut by a third

The bank moved the other way on Strategy (MSTR). Wells Fargo’s long position in the bitcoin treasury company fell to 1,339,018 shares, worth $205.0 million at Sept. 30, from 1,994,253 shares at midyear, a drop of about 33%. Wells Fargo Securities also listed Strategy puts on 795,000 shares, down from 1.52 million. Strategy closed at $103.03 on Monday, against $153.09 at the end of September.

The filing lands as big banks disclose larger bitcoin exposure through ETFs and treasury stocks. JPMorgan reported $540 million in bitcoin ETFs in its own third-quarter 13F last week. Wells Fargo’s IBIT stake is more than four times that.

The timing also stands out. Since the quarter ended, U.S. spot bitcoin funds have been losing money fast. IBIT bled about $2 billion over nine straight sessions through mid-November, and bitcoin fell to about $62,000 over the weekend before trading near $64,000 on Monday. The fund took in about $76.5 million on Monday, breaking an 11-session streak of outflows that had pulled roughly $2.35 billion from IBIT since Oct. 30. That is almost exactly the value Wells Fargo put on its own stake at the end of September.

Wells Fargo’s filing is a snapshot as of Sept. 30. It does not show whether the bank or its clients bought or sold IBIT shares in October or November, the period in which bitcoin fell from above $83,000 to the low $60,000s. The next round of 13Fs, covering the fourth quarter, is due in February.

This post Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
